Sports.title: Disguised funding and dishonest witnesses: key findings in Manchester City case
Sports.content:
Agreements were ‘shams’

The independent commission’s “core decision” is a 40-page document which appears to confirm the worst interpretation of Manchester City’s behaviour. Central to the finding that the club were guilty of all charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules is the conclusion that City’s lucrative sponsorship arrangements were “shams”.

When a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family, Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, bought the club in 2008 he set out “ambitious plans” for City. But those ambitions could not be met by the finances then being generated. “The club appreciated from the early days of [Mansour’s] ownership that very significant funds would be required if the steps needed to realise … ambitions were to be fulfilled,” the commission said.

In the first instance the club relied on extra injections from Mansour, or “owner equity”. But according to the commission: “The club recognised that [this] was not a sustainable model”, and that with owner equity to be excluded from financial fair play rules it “needed to grow its commercial operations”. One way of doing this, the club decided, was to “seek high-value sponsorship arrangements in the UAE generally and in Abu Dhabi in particular”.

What resulted was what the commission call the “Disguised Funding Scheme” (DFS). Traditional sponsorship valuations would not be enough for City to meet their ambitions and forestall financial losses. So City applied a different approach. In the words of the commission: “The club would enter into sponsorship agreements with Abu Dhabi sponsors which contained substantial [fees] at well above fair market value. However, the sponsor would not be liable to pay the recorded sponsorship fee, and would not do so.” Instead the sponsor would pay only a small percentage of the fee, described by the commission as the “base sum”. The rest, or the “tagged sum”, would be paid for by Mansour, or at least the company that he had formed to control City, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

The DFS, the commission said, allowed the club to state that “its commercial revenues from Abu Dhabi sponsorship agreements (and so its income generally) were far, far greater than was in fact the case”, and also “conceal from third parties the true extent of the equity contributions in fact being made into the club by ADUG”. As a result, it said: “Each of the Abu Dhabi sponsorship agreements was a sham.”

City had argued in their defence that sponsors had paid all the money but that the sponsors had required, “from time to time”, financial assistance from the Abu Dhabi government and its crown prince court to meet their sponsors’ obligations. City’s argument therefore was that although money was given by the Abu Dhabi government to sponsors, the club was not involved.

The scale of the funding

The commission calculated that, over the course of the nine seasons under investigation, from 2009-10 to 2017-18, City had booked £949.94m in sponsorship revenues from Abu Dhabi-based companies. Of that total, only £119.25m had been paid in “base fee”. The rest, £830.69m, were “tagged sums” paid by ADUG to the club.

By some estimates, the £830m accounted for as much as 30% of City’s revenue over the period of the investigation. It was a sum far greater than the total revenue of most of their Premier League rivals. The scale of the funding also grew heavily over time. In 2009-10, the commission identified £22.5m in “tagged sums” paid by ADUG. By the 2017-18 that figure had risen to £134.73m, the highest total across the seasons under investigation.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City fans show their appreciation for their wealthy owner in 2014. Photograph: Matt West/BPI/Shutterstock

The knock-on effect

The commission broke the charges into four blocks and once the first had been proven – relating to the provision of accurate financial information – a domino effect ensued. Blocks two and three related to City’s requirement to meet the financial rules of first Uefa then the Premier League. Removing the “tagged sums” from any balance sheet meant that City had failed to comply with either set of regulations “in any of the seasons” under which they were charged.

The submission of inaccurate financial information meant that City were also in breach of group four of the charges, relating to the “duties of cooperation” it owed to the Premier League. But City’s behaviour went further in this regard. The commission found that the club had “made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the Premier League investigation” and had “concocted” explanations for the DFS “well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the reality”.

Dishonest witnesses

The commission also made damning comments on the behaviour of witnesses called by City during the hearings. “Evidence given by a number of important factual witnesses called to give evidence on behalf of the club was false in a number of key respects,” the commission wrote, arguing that some of falsehoods had been deliberate. “Certain of those factual witnesses had given evidence at the hearing that they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest,” it said. Also contained in the verdict is the detail that, in the event of City being found guilty, the Premier League had reserved the right to challenge “additional and perhaps more egregious acts of non-cooperation” relating to City’s behaviour during the League’s own investigation.

Further wrongdoing

Further, smaller charges were proven against City. Payments “not recorded in an employment contract … but instead recorded in a consultancy agreement”, totalling more than £15m, were found to have been made to three former employees, understood to include Roberto Mancini and Yaya Touré. Equally, a scheme known as the “Fordham arrangement”, was shown to be another sham whereby City sold their players’ image rights to a third party which was “in reality little more than a front for ADUG”.

The only charge City were cleared on related to one subset of the club’s obligations to act “in the utmost good faith” towards the Premier League.

View image in fullscreen Roberto Mancini (right) and Yaya Touré (centre) were found to have had payments not recorded in their employment contracts. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Shutterstock

No love lost

The commission describes the case as having been “fiercely contested” and there is no sense of either side pulling their punches. City were revealed to have sought to dismiss the Premier League’s investigation, its decision to charge the club and its decision to prosecute the charges. The verdict was published after one party failed in an attempt to keep it private. “The proceedings were at all times extremely hard fought on both sides,” the commission said. “We in no way mean that as a criticism of either party; it is simply fact. No stone was left unturned.”

The competitive nature of the proceedings will have been a key factor in turning the case into such a substantial endeavour that the verdict could be published only more than two years after proceedings began. The commission said evidence submissions ran to “many, many thousands of pages”, the core bundle of documents to “tens of thousands” of pages, and even the index to the documents used in the hearing was 1,000 pages long.

“It has taken us much longer than we would have wished, and much longer than we had anticipated would be the case when the hearing concluded, to produce our decision,” the commission wrote. “That is regrettable.”

The submissions are likely to continue given City intend to appeal against the decision before Friday. The commission must also meet to decide upon its sanction.

What do City say?

The club continue to deny wrongdoing. City have said they will appeal “on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”. Their chief executive, Ferran Soriano, said in a video to employees that the decision was based on a “Premier League conspiracy theory”.

Sports.title: Man City face lawsuit of at least £400m and future chaos as rivals sharpen knives after verdict
Sports.content:
Man City face lawsuit of at least £400m and future chaos as rivals sharpen knives after verdict

Manchester City have been warned they face 'years and years' of legal cases if their Premier League rivals sue them for damages.

Prior to the verdict in the club's Premier League financial rules case, four top-flight sides pre-reserved their right to sue City for damages.

4 The walls are closing in on City but they still maintain their innocence Credit: Getty

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has now detailed how Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur could seek over £100million each, and could even join forces to pursue a mammoth lawsuit against them.

Meanwhile, additional legal challenges from other Premier League clubs past and present could follow along with sides across Europe seeking damages of their own.

talkSPORT previously revealed clubs were considering launching collective legal action in light of the independent commission's ruling.

City have been found guilty of all charges against them, the Premier League announced on Tuesday.

The club are expected to appeal against the decision, having been given a deadline of Friday to respond to the verdict.

City face potential £400m lawsuit

Providing an update on what is set to come next for City, Jacobs explained: "Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Spurs have all pre-reserved their rights to sue Manchester City for damages, predominantly for seasons where they missed out on Champions League football or potentially silverware.

"Each could seek over £100million, but you have a wider issue for City if found guilty subject to appeal and that is collective action.

"There’s two routes. One is the clubs could pool together and start their own individual action for compensation, but for one lump payment distributed in different ways.

"Or the simpler legal solution is for the Premier League to take class action for damages and then choose how to distribute it.

"You could say clubs that went down might want compensation. You could say at a very base level, clubs that feel Manchester City should be removed from the league in those seasons bump themselves up a place and that’s a little bit extra prize money.

4 United are one of four Premier League clubs who have pre-reserved their right to sue City for damages Credit: Getty

"You’ll have teams that missed out on European football and silverware. So this is a very complicated legal situation.

"Whereas the City case can hopefully resolve itself before the season is out, the damages if they’re found guilty subject to appeal could lead to years and years and years of legal cases.

"This is why certain clubs like the four I mentioned are already prepared.

"There’s even a chance European clubs look at the situation and they lost out to Manchester City in the Champions League in some of the seasons in question and they decide they’re entitled to something as well."

City's offences took place between 2009 and 2018, a period in which they did not finish lower than fifth in the Premier League.

They also won three titles and failed to qualify for the Champions League just once, in the 2009/10 campaign.

4 City won three Premier League titles during the nine-year period in which their offences took place Credit: Getty

The club won a further FA Cup, Community Shield and three League Cups as well as reaching the semi-finals of the Champions League in 2016.

talkSPORT understands Premier League clubs are set to contact chief executive Richard Masters to stress the need for a conclusion to the case before the end of this season including appeals.

Independent Football Regulator latest

Following the confirmation of the independent commission's verdict, several other bodies could also look through the case against City.

Amongst them is the Independent Football Regulator, which was created in September 2025, two-and-a-half years after City were first charged.

Explaining how the regulator could become involved, Jacobs added: "The Independent Football Regulator was not around when this case started.

"It is now and they have the power and the ability to effectively re-review directors and owners.

4 The Independent Football Regulator could re-review City's owners and directors as well as looking into the case Credit: Getty

"So as this case comes to a close, sources tell me the Independent Football Regulator wants to also comb through everything regarding the owners and individual directors to determine whether any other action is necessary.

"The same applies to the FA as well. With Chelsea, it was a Premier League settlement plus an FA settlement plus a UEFA settlement.

"It’s going to be very interesting to see whether other regulators and bodies read the evidence and feel the need to act."

Chelsea were handed a record £10.75million fine and a suspended transfer ban in March for breaching Premier League rules regarding payments to agents.

Independent Football Regulator statement

The chair of the Independent Football Regulator, David Kogan has also released a statement regarding City's case.

He stated: "The independent commission’s decision raises serious issues.

"The IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate, in the interests of protecting the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals.

"This includes taking account of findings made by the leagues. However, as the proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League we will await further developments.

"We hope it can be resolved quickly for the sake of fans. For now, we have no further comment."

Sports.title: Tottenham star forced to cut short international team training session after just seven minutes
Sports.content:
Tottenham star forced to cut short international team training session after just seven minutes

Jan Paul van Hecke has returned to Tottenham following a foot injury suffered during the Netherlands' win over Serbia.

The Spurs defender had been part of Xavi's first-ever Dutch squad for the extended international break, and started in the first two of their four Nations League fixtures.

4 Van Hecke has been a staple in the Netherlands' back line this year, including at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Van Hecke was part of an effective back line alongside Virgil van Dijk and club captain Micky van de Ven in a 1-1 draw with Germany last week, and again in a 2-1 win over Serbia on Sunday.

However, Spurs have now been dealt a blow as it's emerged that the £52million man suffered an injury in their last outing.

Van Hecke initially took part in team training on Wednesday, but withdrew from the session early and has now left the camp.

Reports in the Dutch media claim the 26-year-old lasted just seven minutes in training, and the Netherlands have since announced that he has now left the camp.

The rest of their squad have departed for Thessaloniki, where they will face Greece on Thursday night in the Nations League before going on to play Serbia again on Sunday.

A post from the Netherlands on X read: "Jan Paul van Hecke won’t travel to Thessaloniki with the squad.

"The defender got injured during the away game against Serbia and will return to Tottenham Hotspur.

"Get well soon, JP!"

Tottenham given injury headache

Tottenham will now be hoping Van Hecke's injury isn't a serious one, with the centre-back an ever-present since his summer arrival.

The Dutchman joined from Brighton in a £52m deal, reuniting with former boss Roberto De Zerbi as one the first of Spurs' big-money arrivals in a window which saw them splash out over £300m.

4 Van Hecke has had his first chance to impress new Netherlands boss Xavi cut short Credit: Getty

4 De Zerbi needs his key players available as he navigates a difficult period at Tottenham Credit: AFP

Van Hecke has played every minute of his new team’s first five Premier League games this season.

While he opened his Spurs account with a late consolation in their last match - a 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa - it has been a challenging start to life in north London otherwise.

De Zerbi's side sit bottom of the table after their first five matches, and are still searching for their first league win.

With just two points on the board, Spurs remain one of just three teams yet to taste victory this term alongside Bournemouth and Fulham.

As for Van Hecke, his performances have come in for scrutiny too, with Stuart Pearce questioning his huge price tag after he struggled to cope with Nicolas Jackson in the defeat to Villa.

Commentating for talkSPORT, the England great said: “Honestly, when he moved for the summer money that he did, it raised an eyebrow or two in my head."

4 Van Hecke is yet to taste a league win in Spurs colours Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

And Van Hecke now faces a race to be fit in time to prove his doubters wrong at the first available opportunity.

Spurs return to action following the international break with an away trip to Old Trafford to face Manchester United on Saturday, October 10, as they again go in search of their first three points.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard injury update after Norway scan results come back
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard is making a progress on the ankle injury he suffered during Norway's 2-1 defeat to Portugal in the Nations League.

The Arsenal star was on the receiving end of an off-the-ball tackle by Bernardo Silva, which incited an angry reaction from Odegaard.



3 Odegaard was left furious with the tackle on him and exchanged words with the former Manchester City star Credit: Getty

But after a scan, Norway are hopeful of him playing this week.

Odegaard had an X-ray, which confirmed he avoided any serious damage.

He is yet to return to training with his teammates with Norway set to face Wales and Portugal again.

Speaking about the scan, former Fulham star and Norway's team coordinator Brede Hangeland said on Wednesday: "Martin was in the breakfast room, he was happy and he had less pain in his ankle than yesterday.

"It is a long time until the next match. It is a full two and a half days. A lot can happen in that time.



"Martin will be able to do what he wants in training today with regards to his ankle, and I am happy that it is much better than yesterday.

"Ola Sand (the national team doctor) has that under control. As far as I understood, there was nothing dramatic in those images [X-ray]. The most important thing is that the guy is feeling better. The images show a snapshot, while he’s still recovering. And the progress is positive."



And Hangeland expects him to be involved against Wales on Thursday, adding: “There’s no doubt about it, as far as I understand. We don’t intend for him to be there just as a social minister. The goal is for him to contribute on the field.”

But the actual tackle by Silva also angered Norway boss Stale Solbakken, who said on the incident: "It’s ugly, and it is on the verge of a red card.



"He just wants a stop in the game, and it is something that happens from behind. Odegaard’s reaction also says a little."

3 Odegaard carried on until the end of the game, but he was hobbling around Credit: AFP

What happened to Odegaard?

Former Man City star Silva was brought on late in the game by Jorge Jesus with Portugal leading 2-1.

Odegaard picked up the ball deep and looked to start a late attack in stoppage time.



But as he passed the ball on, Bernardo came across and kicked him, catching his ankle in the process.

Silva was booked for the challenge while Arsenal captain spent the rest of the game limping around.

Footage emerged showing Odegaard swearing at Silva before speaking to Norwegian TV after.

He said: "It's a head fog from him. Just kicks me down long after I've played the ball away. I don't understand what he's doing.



3 Odegaard has been in sparkling form for club and country Credit: Getty

"You have to ask him. I don't know what he's doing. It doesn't belong on a football field. It's a shame people do that, but that's life."

In response, Silva was less than apologetic when quizzed after the game, saying: "What tackle? That's football, my friend."

But Arsenal fans can probably breathe a sigh of relief with Odegaard looking to be back in action soon.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs want Man City sanctions applied this season amid gridlock concerns
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs are demanding that any possible sanctions Manchester City face are applied this season following Tuesday's bombshell verdict.

talkSPORT understands that Premier League clubs plan to write to Premier League chief executive Richard Masters, stressing the importance of the City case, inclusive of appeals, is resolved this season.

3 Manchester City have until Friday to appeal the charges against them Credit: Getty

And that any sanctions subject to appeal are in play this campaign and as soon as reasonably possible.

Rival clubs have concerns City will explore avenues to bring proceedings to gridlock.

Clubs are expected to stress they welcome the verdict and now want action taken to end the long running case definitively.

What happened to Man City?

This comes after City were found guilty on all charges of serious financial breaches by the Premier League on Tuesday.

The charges, which were first brought forward in 2023, showed that City inflated their financial position by over £900million between 2008 and 2019.

While City deny any wrongdoing, and talkSPORT understands that the club are planning to appeal, teams are hoping any punishment is dished out this season.

"It's worth noting, before we get into the details that, although a sanction hearing is expected to be the next step, Manchester City have until October 2nd to appeal the actual verdict itself," talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs told Drive.

"We know from City sources they will appeal, we just don't know whether they'll appeal the verdict and then any sanction hearing, or effectively wait until the punishment."

Rival clubs prepare massive lawsuit against Man City

If City's appeal and any gridlock bid are unsuccessful, the floodgates will open regarding rival clubs wanting them to pay up.

Jacobs told talkSPORT: "Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Spurs have all pre-reserved their rights to sue Manchester City for damages, predominantly for seasons where they missed out on Champions League football or potentially silverware.

3 Man City continue to plead their innocence with CEO Ferran Soriano (right) claiming the charges are a 'Premier League conspiracy theory' Credit: Getty

"Each could seek over £100million, but you have a wider issue for City if found guilty subject to appeal and that is collective action.

"There’s two routes. One is the clubs could pool together and start their own individual action for compensation, but for one lump payment distributed in different ways.

"Or the simpler legal solution is for the Premier League to take class action for damages and then choose how to distribute it.

"You could say clubs that went down might want compensation. You could say at a very base level, clubs that feel Manchester City should be removed from the league in those seasons bump themselves up a place and that’s a little bit extra prize money.

"You’ll have teams that missed out on European football and silverware. So this is a very complicated legal situation.

"Whereas the City case can hopefully resolve itself before the season is out, the damages if they’re found guilty subject to appeal could lead to years and years and years of legal cases.

3 City fans have no idea what the future holds, but it looks very bleak Credit: Getty

"This is why certain clubs like the four I mentioned are already prepared.

"There’s even a chance European clubs look at the situation and they lost out to Manchester City in the Champions League in some of the seasons in question and they decide they’re entitled to something as well."

Chelsea's sanctions

As for potential punishments, Jacobs pointed to Chelsea's own sanctions earlier this year.

Chelsea were hit with a one-year transfer ban, suspended for two years, and a £10.75million fine in March for breaching Premier League rules over agent payments.

The Blues self-reported the issue, which meant the Premier League took a more lenient view on the capital side, whereas City's refusal to co-operate could result in a severe punishment.

"Non-cooperation tends to lead to a more severe punishment," Jacobs said.

"The other thing is that Chelsea self-declared, it was a new ownership regime, Clearlake-Boehly reported Roman Abramovich immediately in May 2022 when they discovered in due diligence that there were breaches.

"So that's why it's not a perfect comparison, even though the scale of Chelsea charges was also very high.

"The other factor in all of this is that Manchester City and not co-operating are less likely, if they choose to then later down the line try and enter into a settlement with the Premier League to mitigate the severity of the punishments, find that maybe the Premier League aren't prepared to mediate, because ultimately a vast proportion of these charges, nearly a third, are about City circumventing this investigation in the first place."

Sports.title: Man City wrong to give fans false hope after damning Premier League verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City still have information regarding their Premier League financial rules case that the public has not been made aware of yet.

That is according to the club's former chief operating officer, Chris Bird.

3 City have information that has not yet been made public, says their former COO Credit: AFP

However, football finance expert Stefan Borson believes it is wrong to give supporters hope that more details will emerge in the case.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday that City have been found guilty of all charges against them.

talkSPORT understands the club are set to appeal against the ruling, having been given until Friday to respond to the verdict.

City were first charged back in February 2023 for 115 alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009 and 2023.

City 'innocent', says former COO

Following a damning Premier League statement, both Bird and Borson appeared in a heated clash on White and Jordan on Wednesday morning.

The former, who was City COO between 1998 and 2003, claimed that 'full process' has not yet been completed.

Bird told talkSPORT: "I think the words that are being used at the moment are one-sided and I think until both sides of the story are compared then I think we’ve got to be careful the way we describe things. There hasn’t been a full process yet."

In a statement of their own, City reiterated their stance that they are innocent.

When asked if he agrees with the club's statement, Bird added: "I agree. The club has got information that it is yet to put forward and is yet to be in the public eye."

'Wrong' to give City fans false hope

However, fellow City fan Borson believes it is wrong to give supporters false hope, as he said in response: "We know there was a 12-week hearing where they told us that they were presenting all of their evidence.

3 Borson admits it is wrong to give City fans false hope that more details are to come Credit: Getty

"Frankly, it’s clearly obvious in the initial hearing you would put your best foot forward because your opportunity to overturn the initial hearing is always severely limited.

"In fact, under the Premier League rules, they are not permitted to raise new evidence without permission of the Premier League or of the panel that sits. So it would be an incredibly risky thing to do.

"So I don’t think we should be giving City fans in particular false hope in terms of what’s coming.

"City clearly believe they’ve done nothing wrong. We accept that, but this is the independent commission panel coming with a very, very detailed set of reasons after a 12-week hearing.

"We should not be silly about what they’ve done, City did put forward an incredibly expensive and high quality case and we can’t just dismiss what’s there in writing in front of us."

Meanwhile, Bird remained convinced there is more to come in the case ahead of a potential appeal by City.

3 City have been given until Friday to respond to the verdict and are expected to appeal the ruling Credit: PA

He added: "I think there’s a story that will come out that will show that City are not the picture that the Premier League or the media are trying to paint."

The Premier League's verdict follows an independent commission hearing on the case between September and December 2024.

A sanctions hearing is now set to follow next, but City's anticipated appeal will cause a delay to proceedings.

The club have until Friday to respond to the verdict in the case.

Once underway, the sanctions hearing is expected to last for several weeks.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon has not learnt new skills at Barcelona – he’s still capable of more
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon has not learnt new skills at Barcelona – he’s still capable of more

Anthony Gordon can offer more for both club and country despite scoring in recent meetings with Spain and Czechia.

Gordon, who completed a £70million move from Newcastle United to Barcelona back in May, struck in each of England's UEFA Nations League outings this month.



3 Gordon has been directly involved in a goal in each of his last four England outings Credit: Getty

The 25-year-old has now netted in each of his last three outings for the Three Lions following his second-half opener in Prague on Tuesday night.

The forward's performance against Czechia earned an eight-out-of-10 from Adrian Durham on Tuesday night.

Despite his recent goalscoring form for England, Gordon is yet to net for Barcelona, though has provided four assists for Hansi Flick's side in the 2026/27 La Liga campaign.



And Danny Murphy believes that while Gordon is a 'really good footballer', he's not learned anything new during his opening months at Barcelona.

What did Murphy say about Gordon?

"I've always banged the drum for Anthony Gordon," Murphy began on White & Jordan on Wednesday.



"I said he was good value when Newcastle paid £40million [to sign him] from Everton. People laughed at me.

"I think his confidence and belief has heightened since he's been in a team that dominate games and he's playing with world-class players.



"He's going to get more of the ball and you'll see his qualities more. His quality's always been there. His work ethic and tenacity and pace have always been.

"The problem is when you're playing at Newcastle, they have good and bad spells. Hence, sometimes he's talked about well and other times he's criticised.

"His numbers weren't brilliant at Newcastle because he's in a team that aren't dominating games and dominating leagues.

3 Murphy is hoping for more from Gordon at Barcelona



"At Barca, he was always going to be better, but I don't think his IQ's gone up.

"I think he is what he is. I think he's a really good footballer. He's maybe being a little bit more appreciated by some because he's playing for Barca now, but I don't think he's learnt new skills in two months. I don't think his IQ's gone up in two months.

"A year down the line, playing with those type of players and the quality that they have, you might see him learn some new things."

'I've always liked him'

Murphy continued: "I've always thought he should be hitting better numbers even at Newcastle because of his quality. His pace is obvious to anyone who watches football. His work off the ball has always been brilliant. I love that about him.



"He's a team player. His end product was up and down a little bit at Newcastle. He gets himself in such wonderful positions, so I think he's more than a running machine.

"I've always felt that. I've always liked him. And I think he's capable of really good things. And I think, hopefully, we'll see them at Barca.

3 Gordon is yet to score for Barcelona following his big money move to Spain over the summer Credit: Getty

"But let's not forget, he hasn't scored yet [for Barcelona]. So put it in perspective, he doesn't start every game. You know, you've got to create the balance with this. I like a player who's confident in himself.



"I hope it does keep going well for him at Barca. It's good to see us have players go abroad and do well. So, I've got no problem with him having belief in himself. I know some have been a bit critical of it and saying, just calm down a little bit.

"But it's good. It's good that he is confident. I don't see a problem with it. I just hope he carries on."

Gordon will hope to maintain his fine England form when the Three Lions face Croatia on Saturday evening.

Sports.title: Croatia vs England LIVE commentary: Game being played behind closed doors as Tuchel eyes key win
Sports.content:
Croatia vs England LIVE commentary: Game being played behind closed doors as Tuchel eyes key win

England face Croatia in the third match of their Nations League campaign, and it will be played in an empty stadium.

Thomas Tuchel's side suffered defeat in their opening game against World champions Spain at Wembley at the weekend.

3 Gordon put England 1-0 up against Czech Republic thanks to an Alexander-Arnold assist Credit: Getty

However, they bounced right back in Prague against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night with a 2-0 victory.

England now face Croatia and it will be the second time the two have faced each other recently, following the Group L opener at the World Cup.

The two sides met at the AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas and Tuchel's men were victorious, courtesy of a Harry Kane brace.

There's further history between the two sides after Luka Modric and co defeated England in the 2018 World Cup semi-finals in Russia.

Croatia will remain an awkward opponent for the Three Lions despite having an aging squad, with a 41-year-old Modric still scoring goals for fun.

Why is Croatia vs England behind closed doors?

In March 2025, there were incidents of crowd trouble that involved Croatian fans in the Nations League quarter-finals against France.

UEFA's disciplinary action included a one-match home stadium ban and a separate one-match ban on Croatian away supporters.

UEFA opened disciplinary proceedings concerning racism and discrimination, and the governing body were also fined a total of €93,000 (£79,000) and ordered to cover the cost of repairing damage caused to the Stade de France by the fans.

While the game was set to have no supporters from either team, lobbying from FA chiefs has softened UEFA's plans.

3 A small delegation of England fans will watch their Nations League match against Croatia Credit: Getty

England released a statement, that read: "We’re pleased to confirm that, following discussions with UEFA, a small delegation of England Supporters Travel Club members will be permitted to attend England’s UEFA Nations League fixture against Croatia on Saturday 3 October.

"It was announced shortly after confirmation of this fixture that the match will be played behind closed doors, but we have secured an allocation of 100 complimentary tickets for active 2026-2028 England Supporters Travel Club members."

The statement added that the only eligible fans who can register are active 2026-2028 England Supporters Travel Club members and they can only do it for themselves only.

Tickets will be allocated based on all-time caps, with active caps used to separate those who have the same all-time caps total.

How to follow Croatia vs England

The fixture will be played on Saturday, October 3.

The Three Lions will be heading to the Stadion Rujevica on Saturday in Rijeka at 5pm BST (6pm local time).

Sports.title: Why would the likes of Erling Haaland and Marc Guehi stay at Man City when they have been lied to and betrayed? Footballers have morals and it would be hard to blame them if they now wanted out, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Why would the likes of Erling Haaland and Marc Guehi stay at Man City when they have been lied to and betrayed? Footballers have morals and it would be hard to blame them if they now wanted out, writes IAN LADYMAN

After full-time in Prague on Tuesday night, the message from the Football Association arrived pretty quickly. Neither the England manager Thomas Tuchel nor any of the players about to walk through the interview area at the Fortuna Arena would be answering any questions about Manchester City.

Eventually, however, reality will catch up with the likes of Elliot Anderson, Marc Guehi, Nico O’Reilly and the 166 other players who have represented City in the Premier League since they were first found to have been trampling all over spending rules back in 2009-2010.

This, sadly, is a matter from which nobody who wore the club’s pale blue shirt in their era of monotonous on-field success will ever be able to hide.

Not Yaya Toure, who sat and talked to the media on a sofa in the plush environs of a Hoboken hotel after being introduced as the club’s highest-paid player during City’s pre-season tour of America in the summer of 2010. Toure had just been lured from Barcelona and, understandably, the money had played a part.

Not Sergio Aguero, scorer of City’s most famous goal at the denouement of the 2011-2012 season. Not David Silva or John Stones, who both gave 10 years of service. And now, not even Erling Haaland.

City’s acolytes will argue that the club’s recent achievements – such as the 2023 Treble – should be viewed differently given that the club is accused of breaking the regulations only up until 2018. They will say that the 15 trophies won between then and now are ‘clean’.

The FA made it clear that Manchester City players such as Marc Guehi would not be answering questions on the 115 charges while on international duty

Why would Erling Haaland (right) stay when the club - and executives like Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) - have been proved wrong in their defiance on the charges?

But where did the money come from to lay the platform for all that glory? Would Pep Guardiola and his team have been able to win so relentlessly without the years of ill-gotten investment that had previously been ploughed into a playing squad that was eventually to run rivals such as Liverpool and Arsenal into the dust with such monotony?

The answers to the questions are clear and that is why so many City players from both past and present will wear the stain of their club’s dishonesty like so many modern footballers wear a sleeve of tattoos.

And that is one of the great sporting tragedies of this miserable catalogue of City sinning. Institutional skullduggery is always like this. It doesn’t just bring down the architects. The fall-out crushes the innocents too.

Senior City executives will carry the weight of their wrong-doing for a lifetime but so too will the club’s supporters and players.

They are the ones who have been able to pretend for so long that none of this was true, that none of it would ever be proven, that it was all part of a campaign by the established Premier League clubs to keep City in their traditional place some way down the hierarchy of relevance. This, after all, is what their club was telling them.

But now that the truth is known, it leaves City’s players in a quite dreadful spot, one in which no sportsman or woman should ever be placed.

For if sport is not honest and fair then it loses its legitimacy. If sport is not honest, achievements pale to nothingness. So as City players past and present look now at their medals and awards in their cabinets at home, they may just see them start to rust.

The likes of Toure and Aguero and Silva and Stones have no choice but to somehow make peace with it all. None of this was their doing.

The likes of Sergio Aguero may start to look at the medals in their trophy cabinet at home a little differently in light of the verdict

Why would Elliot Anderson – a young Geordie raised on the sporting values of the North East’s great Wallsend Boys Club – not question the wisdom of turning down other interested clubs?

Footballers are not stupid but they know their place. They are paid to play. They will perhaps take solace from the fact that out there on the grass, battle was always fought gamely and fairly. Those memories will remain and sustain them to a degree.

As for the modern group, preparing for a clash with Liverpool of all people on the resumption of the Premier League a week on Sunday, what motive is there now to remain at the club that has effectively been lying to them just as much as it has been to the rest of us?

Haaland had suitors from all across Europe when he signed for City in May 2022. We know this because City told us at the time. It was a coup, they said. It was proof of the club’s modern standing and power.

The great Norwegian has repaid that £50million transfer fee spectacularly in the four years that have followed. The goal tally sits at 169 and counting across all competitions. He has done his bit.

But everywhere he goes now, the whiff of this week’s judgement will follow. This is a crime that is not of his making but his achievements now stand as tainted – they will say – and who is to say they are not correct? With that in mind, why would Haaland not feel betrayed? Why would he stay?

Why would Anderson – a young Geordie raised on the sporting values of the North East’s great Wallsend Boys Club – not question the wisdom of turning down other interested clubs when he left Nottingham Forest last summer?

Why would Guehi – a player of deep Christian faith – not look back and ask himself why he didn’t move to Liverpool as had originally been the plan?

Footballers have a remarkable ability to leave the serious stuff in the dressing room when they run out to play. It’s part of the mental strength that enables them to operate under such extremes of stress and public attention. But we should not confuse that with a lack of emotional intelligence.

City supporters will carry the weight of the club's wrongdoing for a lifetime

Of immediate concern to City’s current squad will be the prospect of expulsion from the Premier League and what that would do in terms of their income and their standing in the game.

However, as they wait for news of punishment and indeed the outcome of a City appeal that will undoubtedly drag this sorry affair out even longer, we should not presume that simple matters of right and wrong don’t matter to them also. They do.

City’s players have heard the noise for years and now they know it has its roots deeply embedded in a sordid and embarrassing truth. They have to come to terms with that now and if some of them decide it would be more easily done some place far away from the Etihad Stadium then it would be hard to blame them.

Sports.title: 'He's the most committed player I have ever seen': Inside the rapid rise of Lewis Koumas and how 'brilliant' winger persuaded Andoni Iraola to U-turn on exit, plus Reds' new bill for Rio Ngumoha revealed - Liverpool Confidential
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola promised he would trust in youth and no one at Liverpool has benefited more than young Lewis Koumas.

The new boss is winning over fans with his holistic approach to life in charge of the club and his appearance at the women’s Merseyside derby on Sunday did his PR no harm. Nor has the fact he has been spotted around the city, immersing himself in the culture of Liverpool, several times.

Another stick used to beat former boss Arne Slot was his supposed ignorance of academy players (although, in the Dutchman’s defence, he was the man who gave Rio Ngumoha his break in the first team).

Iraola is treating everyone equally at Anfield, be it a £100million player – and there are several of those – or a rookie academy kid with limited first-team exposure.

Koumas is the shining example of Iraola’s trust in a flourishing academy that has seen midfielder Trey Nyoni nearly double his league minutes from last year already, Ngumoha force his way into the England first-team squad and James McConnell be given chances with the seniors.

Defender Luke Chambers is also trusted, while strikers Jayden Danns or Will Wright could be the next cabs off the rank, fitness permitting.

Lewis Koumas had been set to leave Liverpool on loan at one point in pre-season - but now the 21-year-old winger is playing regularly, and impressively, for the Reds

Koumas is the shining example of new boss Andoni Iraola’s trust in Liverpool's youngsters

For all intents and purposes, Koumas was slated for a loan this season. Hull City were firmly in the hunt to sign him after a positive spell there last term culminated in the Tigers winning promotion, with the Wales international scoring a few important goals along the way.

Indeed, Liverpool's loans manager Gary Probert had held talks over the possibility – but it was soon kiboshed by Iraola, a move revealed in Liverpool Confidential. The boss had seen enough and asked to keep a small number of academy stars that were originally earmarked for an exit.

Koumas' off-the-ball work, attitude and tactical understanding were what swayed Iraola, plus his versatility and ability to cover a number of positions.

‘He is absolutely as committed a player as I have seen in all the time I have been coaching,’ Hull’s experienced assistant manager Dean Holden tells Confidential. ‘He is a workaholic.

‘He wants to stay around the training pitch as long as he can, and loved the one-to-one individual development programmes we did with him. He wants to learn and is really mature in the way he sees the game tactically.

‘He was brilliant. We wanted to keep him at one point, he only wanted to come back here if he was going to leave Liverpool.

‘Before he came to Hull last year, we told him how we could help develop his game as well as the strengths he’d bring for us in terms of his willingness to run in behind, which for a young player is refreshing.

‘His first loan last season did not work out (at Birmingham) and he wanted a manager who believed in him and would be honest with him, he just wanted honesty which says a lot about his maturity.

‘I loved him to bits and I am really, really pleased for him that he’s doing so well.’

‘He is absolutely as committed a player as I have seen in all the time I have been coaching,’ Hull’s experienced assistant manager Dean Holden tells Confidential of Koumas

Trey Nyoni (right) has been similarly impressive to Koumas, while Jayden Danns (centre) could be the next cab off the rank for the Kop Kids

Koumas has a chance of featuring against Manchester City in the Premier League next week, especially in light of international break injuries to Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo. Detailed prognoses are not clear on either just yet.

Another player knocking on the door for a start after the international break is Nyoni, the 19-year-old midfielder who has been a class act in every cameo appearance this season.

Given Liverpool’s midfield woes last term, Nyoni was right to privately feel aggrieved he did not get more of a chance under Slot. But it appears new boss Iraola trusts him and it would not be a surprise should he make his first league start in the coming weeks.

Also challenging for game-time in midfield is McConnell, who had agreed to go on loan to Championship side Preston – and had spoken to now-sacked boss Paul Heckingbottom – only for Iraola to block the move.

McConnell held a meeting with then sporting director Richard Hughes and his representatives where he was told that Iraola does not have a ‘pecking order’ and, due to impressing in training, the former Sunderland midfielder would be staying around.

In a similar category is defender Chambers, who can play at both centre half and left back, though he is yet to make a first-team appearance. If that does not change, the situation could be revisited in January.

All examples highlight how Iraola is trusting in youth, which is delighting fans and club recruitment staff alike.

Chelsea’s small windfall

Ngumoha played for England on Tuesday night, which would have frustrated many at Chelsea given the player once described as the best kid in the Cobham academy is now at Liverpool.

But Confidential has been told Chelsea are set for a small cash payment when Ngumoha, who has two caps, makes a certain number of first-team England appearances.

Rio Ngumoha won his second England cap against Czech Republic last night - Liverpool will have to make a payment to Chelsea when he makes a set number of international appearances

Liverpool were last year ordered to pay an initial £2.8million to Chelsea for the winger, who recently turned 18. The figure could rise to £6.8million based on add-ons that include England appearances and also success at Anfield.

When the Reds do have to pay Chelsea a small fee for Ngumoha’s accolades at club and country level, they will do so with a smirk on their face after poaching a talent that has the world at his feet, clearly.

Ngumoha is currently in talks over a new, bumper deal at Liverpool.

Trent still making waves on Merseyside

Trent Alexander-Arnold is still helping out in Liverpool – with several kids from his youth programmes making it to academies across the North West.

The popular 'TAA League' sessions, held across Merseyside, are free, with equipment such as football boots provided for those who might not be able to afford it.

Alexander-Arnold has funded the League since 2022 and it has expanded into more locations. The right back, who left Liverpool for Real Madrid 15 months ago, was a huge advocate of giving back to his community and several of the youngsters who took part in sessions have received call-ups to the academies of Liverpool and Manchester City, among others.

Will Ward hit the mark?

Julian Ward was this week officially appointed as Liverpool's sporting director, which was no surprise to anyone really.

It is a good move given Ward knows the club exceptionally well and has relationships already in place.

Julian Ward (second left) has been officially announced as Liverpool's new sporting director, replacing Richard Hughes (second right)

One the most important early decisions Ward must make is whether to hand new contracts to club legends Virgil van Dijk (left) and Alisson

But equally his knowledge of the inner workings mean he won't be allowed a grace period and the hard work starts now.

He must decide on Alisson and Virgil van Dijk’s futures – do the club extend the expiring contracts of two key players who are 33 and 35 respectively? If not, succession planning must be in place (and it has already started).

Then Ward must look to bolster the defensive midfield position, with Monaco’s Lamine Camara well liked. Full back is arguably an area of weakness, too.

Ward must also oversee a turbulent period in which 1892 Holdings, the investment consortium led by Amit Bhatia and backed by the likes of Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin, are hoping to buy a stake of around 38 per cent – which could rise at a later date – in the club.

That is not Ward’s remit, of course – CEO Billy Hogan deals with that side of the operation – but will the changes have an impact on transfers? The official word is absolutely not, but you never know.

Frimpong signs for Chester!

Jeremie Frimpong’s brother Wesley has signed for local team Chester FC.

Frimpong had been training at the club for a short period after leaving Austrian champions LASK, whom Liverpool play in the Champions League next month.

Coming next week: have your questions answered

Roll up, roll up, next week’s edition of Liverpool Confidential is set to be a Q&A special.

So get your questions in by commenting on this article, emailing me at lewis.steele@dailymail.co.uk or sending me a message on X @LewisSteele_.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo holds showdown talks with manager and head of Portuguese FA today after 41-year-old skipped training following furious reaction to sub snub
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has held showdown talks with national boss Jorge Jesus and the head of the Portuguese FA amid a row over the star being an unused substitute in the win over Norway. The 41-year-old captain - who skipped training on Wednesday - was left on the bench for his side's 2-1 victory. It was the first time in 18 years that Ronaldo has not featured at all for Portugal - aside from injury or suspension absences. At full-time on Sunday, Ronaldo stormed straight down the tunnel and did not return to thank the travelling fans alongside his team-mates. Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench. The decision was validated by Portugal holding on to win the Nations League clash but Ronaldo's anger has led to FA chief Pedro Proenca hurriedly changing his travel plans to sit down for a three-way meeting held at a hotel in Malmo on Wednesday morning, according to Record. Reports in Portugal claim the talks were 'calm and cordial'. Cristiano Ronaldo was angry at being an unused substitute for Portugal's win over Norway Proenca had been due to fly to the Azores for an Under-21s match but dealing with Ronaldo's discontent became the priority. Portugal face Denmark on Thursday but Ronaldo did not take part in team training today, along with Joao Felix and Francisco Conceicao. According to A Bola, he briefly spoke to Jesus and left Malmo's training facilities due to the Swedish club not having the right equipment. It is an inauspicious start to the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo, who opted not to retire from international duty after the World Cup. Only a week ago, Ronaldo reiterated his commitment to the cause, saying: 'I had a conversation with our president, with our coach (about his future). 'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here. 'I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football. 'This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.' Ronaldo will turn 42 in February and has scored three goals in five games for Al-Nassr so far in the Saudi Pro League this season. Jesus and Ronaldo worked together successfully for a year when the 71-year-old was in charge of Al-Nassr but they could be on a collision course if the forward's playing time remains limited. Roberto Martinez stepped down after Portugal's 1-0 World Cup defeat by Spain and when Jesus was announced as his successor, he was asked the Ronaldo question. Jesus insisted: 'As long as he's playing and is in a condition to be selected, I will pick him, within certain limits and under the conditions that I consider best for the national team.' Goncalo Ramos, 25, scored the winner against Norway on Sunday and is considered by many to be the natural evolution up front for Portugal. But it seems as long as Ronaldo is around the national side, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's playing demands will continue to be an issue for the new boss.
