Sports.title: Simone Biles details fresh health battle with eczema... just months after Olympics icon revealed she 'almost died'
Sports.content:
Simone Biles details fresh health battle with eczema... just months after Olympics icon revealed she 'almost died'

Simone Biles has opened up about a painful health battle with chronic skin conditions, just months after revealing she 'almost died' during a medical emergency.

The seven-time Olympic gold medalist revealed that she spent over two years quietly dealing with severe itching and flaking skin before receiving a formal diagnosis.

Speaking to TODAY, the 29-year-old admitted the condition became so unbearable during competition prep that she found herself 'standing at the chalk bucket, just itching until I'm bleeding.'

Doctors finally diagnosed Biles with two separate inflammatory skin conditions: eczema on her arms and seborrheic dermatitis across her scalp.

'Obviously, (I have) trusted professionals around me and great, great doctors, so I'm doing a lot better,' Biles explained. 'It's still an interesting road, but I am doing a lot better.'

Her skin journey began roughly two years ago when red, itchy patches first surfaced on her scalp and arms.

Simone Biles has opened up about a painful health battle with chronic skin conditions

The seven-time Olympic gold medalist revealed that she spent over two years quietly dealing with severe itching and flaking skin before receiving a formal diagnosis

'I was really self-conscious of it at first, so I kind of brushed it to the side,' Biles said.

Ahead of the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, where she captured three golds and a silver, Biles addressed the flaking on TikTok to get ahead of public scrutiny.

'If people noticed on the TV, I didn't want them to say something before me,' she said. 'So I was like, I have to address this because you couldn't just avoid it. If they zoomed in, you could probably see it.'

Following the Games, having to repeatedly explain her scalp to new hair and makeup crews at photo shoots took a heavy emotional toll.

'That's when I felt it was the worst,' she admitted. 'At first I was really embarrassed and ashamed.'

Biles and her personal stylist initially experimented with over-the-counter products and oils without success, before she finally consulted a dermatologist while being seen for a 'dent' in her arm.

She has since regained control of the condition using prescription treatments, applying foam medication for her scalp and a cream for her arms.

The gymnastics legend also revealed she helped husband and NFL safety Jonathan Owens recognize his own symptoms, after initially fearing she had passed the non-contagious condition to him.

Biles said earlier in June that she nearly died due to a mystery medical emergency

Biles has not disclosed the details surrounding that particular health scare

'Like I was in denial, he was in denial,' Biles said. 'I think I have motivated him in some form, and he's like, 'Okay, this is a normal thing. A lot of people have it.''

The revelations come shortly after Biles shared that she was hospitalized earlier this year following a severe health scare she described as 'almost dying.'

Biles also recently revealed that three masked intruders broke into her Chicago home and stole her luxurious Porsche.

The legendary Team USA gymnast dropped the bombshell news during a TikTok video this week. It remains unclear when the burglary happened or if the police have made any arrests but Biles confirmed the car was recovered.

'Feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche,' she said.

'Stole the GTS. But that's another story. If you guys want to know, I'll do a story time on that.'

Sports.title: Stubborn Pep Guardiola has his head in the sand and is risking his Man City legacy... he has been reduced to a trusting submissive, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
At 1.10pm on Wednesday, Pep Guardiola reattached his colours to the mast. Such a show of loyalty was remarkably ballsy at a point when Manchester City are at risk of emulating the Titanic. One can only imagine the thought processes that went into his 57-word missive, posted on his social media channels. Or the wisdom behind it. But his position of loyalty is now clear, which is to say it remains resolutely unchanged, even when everything else has shifted beyond recognition. The Premier League’s confirmation on Tuesday afternoon that City were guilty of the worst acts of cheating ever seen in British sport has irrevocably altered how we view them – and how we view the managers who benefited from it. None more so than Guardiola. There is no suggestion that he knew what was going on above him, but there is even less doubt that his legacy, his achievements, are tethered to those who apparently held such an egregious lack of regard for the rules of engagement. If the ship sinks following the appeals process, Guardiola’s reputation will get wet. With that in mind, we might have expected more than 57 words. We might have expected some temperance, some questions of his own, some room for doubt now that a tangible verdict has finally been delivered. But this is what we got: ‘I want every single Manchester City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran (Soriano, CEO), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca) and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.’ Pep Guardiola cosies up to Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak after lifting yet another title The credibility of Guardiola's achievements has been smashed into 114 pieces and the former City manager could be viewed as a victim

Your browser does not support iframes.

Accompanying the love letter were four pictures. In one, we see him in an embrace with City’s chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. And there’s another of his celebrations with the Champions League trophy, as well as his farewell ovation on the pitch of the Etihad Stadium last summer. Finally, there’s a group shot with Soriano, Al Mubarak and Txiki Begiristain, the director of football who brought Guardiola to the club. Collectively, they built and shaped an empire; individually they have evidently said enough about irrefutable evidence and conspiracies to reduce the great Guardiola into the role of a trusting submissive. My owner. My chairman. Oh my word. Guardiola once said he would walk away if City’s version of the truth proved to be a pack of lies, and we can only assume he took the time to read Tuesday’s verdict. If he had, he will have noticed the most damning lines about ‘sham’ deals and witnesses who gave evidence ‘they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest’. Maybe City will be exonerated in time. And perhaps our memories of Guardiola’s beautiful football and his accomplishments will be restored. But as we view them today, their credibility has been smashed into 114 pieces and Guardiola could be perceived as a victim. Many of us will still see him that way if the verdict holds, because he has so much to lose from the actions of others. Those asterisks will be Guardiola’s asterisks, irrespective of who was responsible. But any defensive instinct towards one of football’s most spellbinding thinkers might also be reduced by his desire to keep his head in the sand. By his stubborn, ongoing refusal to countenance that he, like the rest of us, has been duped by cheats. Any defensive instinct towards Guardiola might also be reduced by his desire to keep his head in the sand City’s hierarchy including chairman Al Mubarak (left) and CEO Ferran Soriano (second right) are clearly persuasive behind the scenes It seems astonishing that his sense of conviction has survived Tuesday’s blasts – City’s hierarchy are clearly more persuasive on home turf than they were in the hearing room of an independent commission. But this was no close battle. This was no verdict that left itself vulnerable to semantics. This was no fight where both boxers greet the final bell with arms raised. No, City were dealt a hiding. It was a mauling. The iceberg won. If City lose their appeal, that much will be utterly irrefutable, barring the conspiratorial ravings of the defeated. It would only compound the shame further if Guardiola was still part of their deluded chorus.

Sports.title: MAN CITY, WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: When will they be punished? Can Premier League look at post-2018 accounts? Is anyone criminally liable? How much can rivals sue for? And what now for ex-City chief Omar Berrada? MIKE KEEGAN reveals all
Sports.content:
MAN CITY, WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: When will they be punished? Can Premier League look at post-2018 accounts? Is anyone criminally liable? How much can rivals sue for? And what now for ex-City chief Omar Berrada? MIKE KEEGAN reveals all

Eight years on from the start of the biggest scandal in recent British sporting memory, we finally have a verdict. But we don't yet have all the answers.

While the football world is reeling from the bombshell news that Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges against them, the Premier League dropped the other shoe on Tuesday night – revealing in full, excoriating detail the scale of the cheating.

The club remain insistent they are innocent, and that they intend to appeal, despite the League presenting such overwhelming evidence that City cooked the books to the tune of £900million in a nine-year period from 2009 to 2018.

So what happens now? What will the punishment be? Will City have to sell off all their star players? And when will it all finally end?

Here, Chief Sports Reporter MIKE KEEGAN answers the big questions that remain after the most explosive week in the history of the Premier League.

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of charges against them by the Premier League

Pep Guardiola won six league titles across 10 seasons at City

What is the timeline now - what information is still to come out and when?

The first landmark date is this Friday, which is the deadline for City to submit an appeal. An appeal was always viewed as an inevitability given the club continue to protest their innocence and chief executive Ferran Soriano has now confirmed one will be forthcoming.

The Premier League handbook goes into great detail about the time constraints surrounding appeals as part of an attempt to expedite the process. For example, any hearing can only last for five days, should be concluded within 12 weeks of the initial verdict and witness and expert statements should run to no more than 30 pages.

However, the first hurdle will be the make-up of a new panel. The chair of the existing panel should ‘as soon as reasonably practicable’ inform the parties involved of the identities of the proposed individuals.

Objections should then be made within two working days. Given how this has played out so far, this could be the first stage that suffers a delay. With so much riding on the choice of the panel, and so much at stake, an objection may well be forthcoming should either side have misgivings over a proposed individual.

Legal experts believe it is unlikely there will be a conclusion this season. With regards to a sanction, the Premier League are refusing to comment on whether that will come before the appeal is finished. However, it would appear there is a desire within the League to speed things along.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters now faces the prospect of kicking out the most successful team in his league for the last 15 years

What will happen to the witnesses judged to have given dishonest evidence?

Good question. Section 29(b) of the released judgment said that 'certain... factual witnesses had given evidence at the hearing that they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest'. The identity of these people, who gave evidence on behalf of City, has not been revealed.

It would appear the Premier League are pushing for redactions to be removed, with a clue given at the bottom of their bombshell statement on Tuesday.

It stated that while the League were ‘only permitted to publish a redacted version of the summary of the Commission’s "core findings"’ that ‘the process remains ongoing and any further information related to the proceedings that has not been published by the Premier League remains confidential’. They also vowed that, ‘unless legally prevented from doing so’ they would ‘publish the full decision’.

One to watch.

Why were the panel members not named?

If you were asked to rule on such a hugely-emotive case as this, would you want the public to know your identity?

As the Premier League have noted, the process is ongoing and there is a hope that more material will be released. The exact reason for the panel not being named is unclear at the moment, but that may change further down the line, depending on legal arguments.

Are there any grounds for criminal prosecution?

That remains to be seen. The priority for both parties right now will be the appeal.

The difficulty here is that there is not really a precedent in this country. In Italy, suspended sentences were handed out to former Juventus executives, including ex-chairman Andrea Agnelli, with regards to a false accounting case.

Agnelli got 20 months, while ex-sporting director Fabio Paratici – by then managing director of football at Tottenham – was handed 14 months.

There are few parallels for criminal punishment - in Italy, Juventus chairman Andrea Agnelli (second left) and sporting director Fabio Paratici (right) were handed suspended sentences

How will the compensation claims work?

Four of City's Premier League rivals – Arsenal, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and Liverpool – lodged legal claims ensuring that they would not be ‘out of time’ in the event that City were found guilty.

Each will already have an idea how much they are going to claim for. The most obvious avenue is the argument that City cost them European qualification and it would appear that, in that area, Spurs have the strongest case. Between 2009 and 2018, they finished one place outside the Champions League spots, with City ahead of them, on four occasions.

The irony here is that a process instigated by former Arsenal chief executive Tim Lewis could net their north London rivals a huge windfall, with £200million mentioned.

It is not just, however, failure to qualify for Europe. Knock-on effects, such as an inability to sign a certain level of player, could also be considered.

The likelihood is that an independent arbitration panel would sit and decide on level of payout, as was the case when Burnley won a £35m payout from Everton in June over the Toffees' PSR breach.

For time purposes, it could be that all four cases would he heard at the same time, although each club may want their own situations to be dealt with individually.

Arsenal are one of four clubs who have reserved the right to seek compensation against City

Tottenham can feel most aggrieved - City denied them Champions League qualification four times in the nine-year period being investigated

Would compensation payments count towards future financial calculations?

It is highly unlikely, given that it would run the risk of creating a vicious circle in which City breach year after year, and be viewed as a double punishment.

Are there any grounds for UEFA to revisit their own City case?

UEFA will wait to see the result of the hearing in full before making a decision. But Daily Mail Sport understands it is highly unlikely they will revisit the case, despite the Premier League stating City were 'significantly in breach' of both their and UEFA's rules.

The verdict obtained by City at the Court of Arbitration for Sport when they overturned their two-season Champions League ban in 2020 would be incredibly difficult to reverse given it upheld some of UEFA’s findings but not others, which it found were ‘time-barred’. City instead received a fine of €10m and had their ban rescinded.

Could the Premier League look at transactions post-2018 now?

They could. Whether they would want to, given the expense and effort that went into this case, is another issue.

At the moment, the feeling within Premier League Towers is one of vindication, and that will linger should City’s appeal fail. Would they want a second leg having won the first so convincingly?

How could City being put into the EFL work in practice? Would EFL clubs have a vote or just be told this is happening?

The EFL have declined to comment. However, there is a rule (11.6.2) that seems to exist for such situations.

Should City be given a points deduction that only sees them relegated to the Championship, then it is simple. They will be relegated. If, however, the sanction relegates them to League Two, it gets a little complicated.

First, they would need to apply to the FA to re-enter the pyramid. If that were successful, their absence would mean one more team would need to be promoted from each of the EFL divisions next season, to make up for the gap in the Premier League.

City could be kicked all the way back down to League Two - but would first have to apply to re-enter the pyramid

Could City’s auditors face any action?

BDO have audited City's accounts for years, and still do. But the Premier League found City 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of their finances from their auditors and football regulators'.

When contacted by Daily Mail Sport, BDO said they ‘remain bound by confidentiality so cannot comment on this occasion’.

Some would view the prospect of action against the firm as incredibly harsh, although we understand BDO could still face an investigation by the Financial Reporting Council (FRC). Sources say the regulator is 'aware' of the situation and 'looking into it to see if there is anything that falls under its remit'.

The FRC refused to comment.

BDO could argue they only acted on information they were given and point out that had it not been for the hacker Rui Pinto (rather than the Premier League’s compliance team) none of these details would have come to light.

What does this all mean for Omar Berrada?

The Manchester United chief executive joined them in 2024 from City, where he held a number of executive roles from 2011 including chief operating officer.

United have declined to comment. That said, it would be hard to imagine a world in which club officials did not carry out the relevant due diligence when Berrada was appointed in 2024 – almost a year after the City charges were made public.

Sports.title: Football regulator hints it could kick Man City owners OUT of the English game as boss vows to 'protect honesty and integrity' after Premier League verdict
Sports.content:
Football regulator hints it could kick Man City owners OUT of the English game as boss vows to 'protect honesty and integrity' after Premier League verdict

The chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has hinted that Manchester City's owners could be removed from the English game after the club were found guilty of all the substantive charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing.

The official verdict was released on Tuesday afternoon, which showed City had cooked the books to the tune of nearly £900million through money artificially pumped into the club by their Abu Dhabi owners over a nine-year period.

The IFR was founded last year and could now play a part in potential sanctions that are to come from the verdict.

The Football Governance Act 2025 gives the regulator permission to remove club owners and suspend or revoke licences if they deem the wrongdoing by said club to be sufficiently serious.

Chair David Kogan has said: 'The independent commission's decision raises serious issues.

'The IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate, in the interests of protecting the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals.

IFR have hinted that Man City owner Sheikh Mansour could be kicked out of English football

The Premier League confirmed that Manchester City have been found guilty of 'all charges related to serious breaches' of the league's financial regulations

'This includes taking account of findings made by the Leagues. However, as the proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League, we will await further developments.

'We hope it can be resolved quickly for the sake of fans. For now, we have no further comment.'

On Friday, Daily Mail Sport reported how City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges against them.

However, there had been no official comment from the Premier League on the findings of an independent panel that oversaw a hearing that concluded in December 2024.

That has now dramatically changed. In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'.

It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee.

The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

As the Premier League noted, this allowed City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend.

Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed that the commission's verdict had 'vindicated' the league's decision to pursue the charges

Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'.

The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'.

It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018, when it won eight major trophies.

Had City reported accurately, 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'.

The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker.

Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said: 'The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

'It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

'It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

'This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.

'Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.'

In a statement released a short time later, City said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ and referred to the ‘opinion of the Premier League Commission’.

It added: ‘The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

‘The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

‘The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.’

City have until Friday to appeal.

Sports.title: 3 questions that still must be answered as scale of Man City scandal emerges
Sports.content:
3 questions that still must be answered as scale of Man City scandal emerges

Manchester City were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, but questions remain over their accounting in the years that followed

View 2 Images Manchester City's success has been tainted (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

For the 2017/18 season - a season which ended with Pep Guardiola winning the first of his six Premier League titles - Manchester City cooked the books to what was, even by their standards, a jaw-dropping extent.

‌



According to the independent commission, they recorded sponsorship income as £145.73million. It turned out only £11m of that was genuine. The other £134.73m was paid by the club owners.

‌



Of the nine seasons of eye-watering financial transgressions, this was City’s crowning effort. Their previous ‘record’ had come in the 2016/17 season when they added £129.59 million to the real sponsorship figure of £11m. It was clearly building towards a crescendo of cheating.

‌



But what happened after that?

What happened after the 2017/18 season?

Did it just stop?

‌



Because the investigation, the hearing and the verdicts have taken so long - a total of eight years in the making - one of the understandable reactions is to be thankful the matter is reaching some sort of conclusion.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



And it truly is a seismic conclusion. But even when the sanctions have been handed out, this cannot be the end of the matter. City’s accounts for every season since 2017/18 have to be forensically re-examined. And then re-examined again.

Seriously, are we to believe they decided to go straight at the start of a 2018/19 season that brought another Premier League title? Seriously, are we to believe they abided by every financial rule when winning Premier League titles in 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24?

Regardless of the financial machinations during the post-charges period, the past eight full seasons - during which City won five Premier Leagues, three FA Cups, four League Cups and a Champions League - have been tainted by the crushing ‘sham’ verdict.

‌



Actually, not tainted. Sullied, poisoned, rendered irrelevant. The whole Guardiola era of domestic dominance and European competitiveness was built on a foundation of monumental deceit. Did that deceit just stop in 2018?

How should Manchester City be punished? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester City spent £100million on two different players this summer (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

‌



Since that 2017/18 season, City have spent £1.65billion on a procession of elite players. They spent £100m on Jack Grealish in the summer of 2021. They bought Enzo Fernandez for £125m a couple of months back. He followed Elliot Anderson, who had moved from Nottingham Forest for £116m.

The same executives who were, presumably, responsible for the ‘sham’ contracts in the period investigated by the commission were still there post-2017/18. It is hard to believe they suddenly saw the error of their ways and transformed into sticklers for the regulations. It is hard to believe they saw the light. Perhaps they did.

Well, let’s see the figures to prove it. Because right now, it is not just the Aguero moment that has one of sport’s biggest asterisks next to it.

‌



It is the four in a row, it is everything that Guardiola achieved during his entire tenure at the club. Understandably, most people think it would be ideal if the sanctions could be imposed, accepted by the club, leaving everyone to get on with the business of enjoying football.

But that is not going to happen. And nor should the damning verdict - and subsequent punishment - be the end of the matter. Far from it. City will run out at Anfield on Sunday week to the most toxic of welcomes.

Article continues below

Erling Haaland and his team-mates would argue they knew nothing about it and were told by those executives that the club had done nothing wrong. Anyhow, Haaland and his colleagues will protest, this is a different time.

Only it’s not. We now know City cheated. What we need to know next is... are they still cheating?

Sports.title: How to watch Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury press conference live
Sports.content:
How to watch Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury press conference live

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will come face to face for the first time tonight after a late row over their heavyweight showdown was resolved

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are set to come face-to-face today, putting to rest concerns that their scheduled December 11 bout might be canceled.

‌



Unless there are any last-minute surprises, the rival British heavyweights will meet at a London press conference to launch the promotional buildup for their massive clash at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium.

‌



The fight appeared to be in doubt over the weekend following claims by Fury and Zuffa Boxing head Dana White that an ongoing feud between White and long-time Joshua promoter Eddie Hearn (Matchroom Sport) was threatening the event. Hearn questioned White’s role after the UFC CEO was listed as a co-promoter alongside Turki Alalshikh’s The Ring.

‌



However, Hearn seems to have prevailed: White is not expected to attend today’s media event, and he also missed out on his bid to hold the fight at Madison Square Garden in New York. Here is all the key information ahead of today's press conference...

How to watch and stream press conference

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

What time will the press conference start?

The press conference is due to start at 6pm tonight but as with many boxing events, it could well be delayed. Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will be completing their media obligations before returning to their training camps in Dubai and Miami respectively, and so the start time could change.

Quotes corner

Tyson Fury: “How ridiculous does that sound [that Dana White’s involvement is now the roadblock]. Like, a promoter who is not actually the promoter of the fight, nor can he be the promoter of the fight ever — he cannot be the promoter of this fight, Eddie Hearn. Categorically, Eddie Hearn and Matchroom are not a promoter of this fight, no way. Contractually they are not allowed to be the promoter, so now you got a spoiled little posh boy chucking his dummies out the pram because Dana White’s involved."

Anthony Joshua: "I am inspiring a generation. The quietest ones often pull the strings. Those who appear least involved may hold the greatest control. Let them shout first, the wisest wait until the final move."

Sports.title: Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour faces being STRIPPED of club in brutal punishment
Sports.content:
Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour faces being STRIPPED of club in brutal punishment

The chair of English football’s independent regulator, David Kogan, says Manchester City’s guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules “raises serious issues”

View 2 Images The Manchester City owner Abu Dhabi royal Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan (centre with scarf) next to chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (Image: 2023 Tom Jenkins)

Manchester City are facing the very real prospect of the owners being stripped from the club.

‌



The Independent Football Regulator has confirmed it has the power to investigate the “suitability” of owners, directors and executives of clubs. That will raise serious question marks for City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and the Abu Dhabi group after being found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

‌



They were accused of making “sham” contracts, were accused of inflating £900million worth of deals and “widespread” deception. Abu Dhabi have bankrolled the club to glory since taking ownership. Now the very heart of City is at serious risk.

‌



Pep Guardiola breaks silence on Man City charges with clear message to owners READ MORE :

The IFR has the powers to step in and strip ownership of clubs. IFR chair David Kogan said: “The independent commission’s decision raises serious issues.

“The IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate, in the interests of protecting the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals.

“This includes taking account of findings made by the Leagues. However, as the proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League we will await further developments.”

‌



City have until Friday to lodge an appeal which seems certain but there is no set timescale on how long the appeal will take. Rival Premier League clubs are pushing hard to get the case heard before the end of the season - but there is no guarantee of that.

View 2 Images Khaldoon al-Mubarak, Manchester City chairman, is at the centre of the mess (Image: Getty)

There are further concerns for City as there is a chance they could be expelled from the Premier League which would see them have to join the EFL at League Two or even below. That would take an extraordinary vote and need 15 clubs to vote in favour of that move.

‌



Mirror Sport understands a more likely outcome would be a huge points deduction which would see City relegated but keep them within the system. But they would still have to conform with EFL spending rules and that would mean they would struggle to keep their top stars.

They are also facing a lengthy transfer ban which would affect their ability to rebuild if they are hit with the strongest punishment.

Furthermore, even though Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United took out legal notices to reserve the right to sue it is understood the brutal nature of the Premier League’s findings has made lawyers believe other could could successfully sue for damages.

Article continues below

They will attack the statute of limitations because of the nature of the fraud in the 40 page legal document opens the door for more clubs and a belief there is no set time.

That could cost them even more money and threaten the club’s finances even further.

Sports.title: Premier League boss hit with FA charge for behaviour after Man Utd match
Sports.content:
Premier League boss hit with FA charge for behaviour after Man Utd match

Alvaro Arbeloa made controversial comments after watching his Fulham side narrowly miss out on a first Premier League win of the season against Manchester United earlier this month

View 2 Images Alvaro Arbeloa was furious after his team dropped points to Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has been charged with misconduct by the Football Association after he claimed that officials did not want Manchester United to lose against his side. The head coach's comments came after a 1-1 draw between the two teams at Craven Cottage on September 20.

‌



United were poor in West London, going 1-0 down against the team that began the afternoon bottom of the top-flight. Michael Carrick's side ended up rescuing a point thanks to Matheus Cunha's deflected effort in the 89th minute.

‌



And Arbeloa was left fuming after the fixture. The Spaniard was furious that, 35 seconds before United's equaliser, the Red Devils were given a free-kick for a foul on Harry Maguire on the halfway line.

‌



Pep Guardiola breaks silence on Man City changes with clear message to owners READ MORE :

Man Utd suffer third injury blow during international break as star forced off READ MORE :

The former Real Madrid head coach went on to accuse the referees of not wanting United to lose against Fulham because of the injustice Carrick's men faced in the Manchester derby seven days earlier. The incident in question saw Erling Haaland's goal incorrectly allowed to stand despite Manchester City's Enzo Fernandez interfering with the build-up from an offside position.

Arbeloa felt this influenced refereeing decisions against his team. He said: "All fouls for them. You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, he's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them.

‌



"And I knew. I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here. We deserved a little bit more.

"We were so close. So, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

"Also we knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referees have been doing all the match so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky."

‌



View 2 Images Alvaro Arbeloa was left furious at the referee following Fulham's draw with Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

Now, the FA have accused Arbeloa of acting improperly in his post-match comments. The governing body said: "Alvaro Arbeloa has been charged with misconduct for comments made after the Premier League fixture between Fulham and Manchester United on Sunday, 20 September.

"It is alleged that the Fulham manager acted in an improper manner by making comments in a post-match interview that imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official. Alvaro Arbeloa has until Thursday, 1 October to provide a response."

‌



Arbeloa appeared to attempt to temper his initial frustrations after the game against United.

The 43-year-old said: "My English is not so good. Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"When you say something that you don't have to say, it's better to stay calm, focus on the performance of my team and focus on the next game.

"I'm not really happy. Like I said, I need to be focused and put my energy in all the things that I have to improve.

"[Maguire] is a very big guy and maybe it wasn't a foul. But it's ok. Like I said, I prefer to analyse the game - players, systems and it's the best for win."

Article continues below

Potential punishments for the ex-defender, if found guilty, include a fine and a touchline ban. Fulham return to action at Ipswich Town on October 10 (3pm).

United, meanwhile, take on Tottenham Hotspur later that day (5:30pm).

Sports.title: Ex-boxing champion Lee Selby to make bare-knuckle return against undefeated rival
Sports.content:
Ex-boxing champion Lee Selby to make bare-knuckle return against undefeated rival

Former featherweight world champion Lee Selby will make his highly-anticipated return to the bare-knuckle boxing ring later this year against Ollie Sentance

View Image Former world champion Lee Selby will return to the bare-knuckle boxing ring in November (Image: Getty Images)

Former boxing world champion Lee Selby will make his highly-anticipated return to the bare-knuckle boxing ring later this year.

‌



Selby, 39, will take on Ollie Sentance in the main event at BKB 61 on November 14 - which is scheduled to take place at the iconic O2 Arena in London, England.

‌



The Barry native and ex-IBF featherweight title-holder called time on his boxing career back in 2022 following back-to-back defeats to George Kambosos Jr and Gustavo Daniel Lemos. Selby - who had a professional boxing record of 28-4 - made the switch to bare-knuckle boxing back in June.

‌



On that night, he scored a vicious second-round knockout victory over Antonio Rizzo, and in just his second fight under the BKB banner, he has been rewarded with a main event slot.

He takes on experienced combat sports veteran, Sentance, who has already won two fights in bare-knuckle boxing. Speaking about his return, Selby said: “I’m really looking forward to getting back in the Trigon and fighting in London again.

"Ollie is a tough opponent and I know he’ll be coming to bring a fight, so I’m expecting a proper battle. It’s always special fighting in front of the British fans, and I’m excited to headline BKB 61 and put on a great night for everyone at The O2."

Sports.title: Man City set to be punished THIS SEASON as 'Premier League rivals get wish'
Sports.content:
Man City set to be punished THIS SEASON as 'Premier League rivals get wish'

Manchester City have been found guilty by the Independent Commission and now await their punishment while they make their appeal over the ruling

View 2 Images Manchester City could receive a points deduction quickly (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester City are set to receive a punishment this season after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules and failing to cooperate with the division's investigation. Premier League rivals are pushing for the sanctions to be rapidly imposed.

‌



City intend to appeal the verdict and a sanction for their indiscretions has not yet been decided. A separate hearing will be held to decide the club's punishment.

‌



The appeal must be filed by Friday, October 2, and Premier League sides are pointing to new regulations that were agreed in June that should now fast-track the process, reports the Sun. According to those rules, any hearing should be concluded 'no later than 12 weeks after filing of the appeal.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That timetable would bean the appeal would need to be resolved by Christmas Day, but given the timing, the appeal could be heard from December 14. From there, the board would have 30 days to produce a verdict.

The Premier League have said that they 'are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans'.

‌



There is a 'very high chance' that Manchester City's situation is resolved by the end of this season to avoid additional problems unfurling in the future, according to Football Finance expert Kieran Maguire.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Depending on the deduction, waiting until next season would give teams who have missed out on Europe or been relegated the opportunity to argue that their fortunes would have been greater if the punishment had been administered sooner.

‌



Maguire added that applying a punishment is often a swifter process than the initial hearing, as seen with points deductions for Nottingham Forest and Everton.

Maguire told BBC Radio 5 Live: “I think there’s a very high chance it will be resolved because if it isn’t we end up with a situation like that of Burnley and Everton where a club could be relegated, Manchester City are not given a deduction this season and it’s given next season instead and the club which finishes 18th could say had the deduction been applied sooner we would not have been relegated so that adds to the complication.

‌



“Looking at the Premier League’s press release it does seem it is keen for this to be resolved as quickly as possible. If you take at the length of time it took in respect of Forest and Everton, once they had heard the evidence, actually applying the tariff was the quick part of the equation. It is listening to the evidence which is the torturous period which we have had up to now.”

Even after the announcement of any sanction, Manchester City are likely to exhaust every avenue they can to overturn the verdict. Maguire believes that City will have a greater chance of success trying to take the case outside of Premier League jurisdiction to the High Court.

Any argument is more likely to be successful if it attacks the people involved rather than the evidence in his mind. City have previously been successful in fighting a verdict when they were initially kicked out of the Champions League before seeing a two-year ban overturned.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City have been found guilty by the independent commission following their legal battle with the Premier League. (Image: PA Wire)

“If they were going to appeal against the initial verdict they have to prove that the composition of the panel was flawed, either in the selection process or they have been able to identify bias in the individuals concerned," Maguire added. "When I’ve spoken to sports lawyers, the universal response to that is that it’s almost impossible but that’s not the same as impossible.

“The other issue would be could they try to take this outside of the football bubble and say it is ultimately a commercial dispute between two bodies and, therefore, the Premier League doesn’t have the right to impose such penalties and try to get it resolved in the High Court.

‌



"When I’ve spoken to legal professionals, they think it highly unlikely but it’s always a possibility.

“Manchester City have previously overturned a UEFA verdict based on the strength of their lawyers and some of their lawyers do have a fantastic reputation for being able to do things which in normal circumstances would be considered highly unlikely.

“The evidence seems to be overwhelming. Reading the summary report, one of Manchester City’s defences seems to be that the Premier League wasn’t in a position to hold this hearing because of the way the evidence had been obtained. That was very firmly rejected by the commission and I can’t see that overturned.

Article continues below

“As for what appears to be an overwhelming amount of evidence and the lack of faith in the Manchester City witnesses, I can’t really see anything based on hundreds of thousands of pieces of evidence and 7,000 pages of testimony for how it could be overturned from a legal point of view. It has to be an attack on the people involved.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola breaks silence on Man City charges with clear message to owners
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola breaks silence on Man City charges with clear message to owners

Pep Guardiola left Manchester City in the summer after 10 years at the helm, and the club have recently been found guilty of breaching 114 of the Premier League's financial rules

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola has spoken (Image: Sky Sports)

Pep Guardiola is backing Manchester City to clear their name despite being found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. Guardiola walked away from City - who continue to strongly deny the charges and maintain that they'll prove their innocence through an appeal - at the end of last season, having spent 10 years as manager.

‌



Breaking his silence in a post on social media, the former City boss declared: "I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano] the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters.

‌



"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

‌



Guardiola stated on several occasions that he believed the City hierarchy's stance that the club is innocent. But Tuesday's report published by the Premier League outlined how City had been found guilty of inflating commercial revenue and reducing costs by £900million, as well as misstating accounts and concealing their true finances between 2009 and 2018.

Speaking before leaving the Etihad in May, Guardiola reiterated: "I trust them. I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did. What happened, happened."

Previously, the 55-year-old said: "I believe what they say to me and the reasons why. I said, 'okay, let's see.' I cannot say [any more] yet because we're awaiting the sentence in February or March – I don't know when – but, at the same time, I like it.

"I read something about the situation and how we need to be relegated immediately. Seventy-five per cent of the clubs want it, because I know what they do behind the scenes."

Sports.title: Ferran Soriano's desperate video misses the point - nobody will ever believe Man City again
Sports.content:
Ferran Soriano's desperate video misses the point - nobody will ever believe Man City again

Manchester City Chief Executive Ferran Soriano released a video to staff shortly after the Premier League's bombshell and explosive ruling - maintaining their innocence

Man City: Ferran Soriano's leaked message to staff

Ferran Soriano must have thought the club he's knee deep in were smarter than the rest. Ahead of the game.

‌



So it feels fitting he's released a 'video nasty' a few weeks before Halloween. As the chief executive officer of Manchester City, Soriano must have felt obligated to record a message to all staff, insisting their club had done nothing wrong.

‌



That the guilty verdicts against the club for serious breaches of Premier League spending rules are based on a "single false accusation". That there has been a "Premier League conspiracy theory" at play.

‌



You'd have to be some sort of halfwit to believe the Premier League would risk its entire reputation, not to mention spend fortunes on legal fees, on the back of a "conspiracy".

City were never going to hold their hands up to this. And never will.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

So Soriano's insistence of innocence - and that his club will appeal the verdict - was about as predictable as Pep Guardiola winning trophies. But as we now know, some of those trophies were a result of cheating.

The first three years of Guardiola's decade of dominance overlapped the 2009-2018 period investigated. He was in charge of the team during the entirety of the four-year investigation.

‌



The Spaniard, who left before City's house was burnt down, moved to back his beleaguered former employers, claiming he will stand by 'his club' always. Only he knows, what he really knew all along.

But what we all know now, however, is that thanks to Soriano & Co, the legacy Guardiola left behind will be forever stained with an asterisk.

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola is yet to comment on the ruling handed down by the Premier League (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

‌



Soriano's transparent attempts at pleading innocence might make him feel noble and empowered. But he's missing a crucial point.

Which is that no-one will continue to believe a single word that comes out of his mouth. Posting a video claiming innocence, without providing substantial evidence to back up said innocence, is laughable.

But this isn't funny.

‌



Because the treacherous project of deception Soriano has been complicit in has turned City from champions to 'SHAMpions'.

And believing they could get away with it, suggests Soriano and his fellow Etihad rulers had egos even more inflated than the club's revenue.

Instead of digging a deeper hole to lead City further into the footballing abyss, Soriano would be better served keeping quiet. Soriano needs to accept both himself, his senior colleagues and his club have been unmasked.

‌



View 2 Images Ferran Soriano maintains City's innocence - despite the weight of evidence against them (Image: Getty Images)

The repetitive wrongdoing has been laid bare, in all its ugly and damaging detail. The shame of such subterfuge has left his reputation in tatters.

Yet the language used in Soriano's response is devoid of contrition. It smacks of threats and reprisals instead.

Article continues below

An attitude which remains in the DNA of a club which got drunk on power and success, but is now supping in the last chance saloon which their appeal represents.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
