World.title: Fort Hare council U-turns on Buhlungu notice period
World.content:
EAST LONDON - The University of Fort Hare’s Council has made an about-turn, accepting to shorten suspended vice-chancellor Professor Sakhela Buhlungu’s notice period after initially refusing to do so.

Buhlungu submitted his resignation on Monday, shortly before he was due to begin presenting his defence at a disciplinary hearing.

Council had initially rejected his request to leave with immediate effect, arguing that his employment contract required him to serve a notice period.

However, in a new communique issued on Wednesday, Council reversed that decision and agreed to shorten the notice period.

Buhlungu will now vacate his position on 23 October, although he had requested that his resignation take effect immediately.

Despite agreeing to shorten his notice period, Council said the disciplinary proceedings against Buhlungu would continue until their conclusion.

“Council further confirms that the disciplinary proceedings currently underway will continue to their conclusion, in accordance with the applicable procedures and principles of due process,” the Council said.

READ | Fort Hare VC Buhlungu placed on precautionary suspension

Council said it had taken the decision after considering the matter carefully and remained committed to “fairness, consistency, procedural integrity and the best interest of the University.”

Buhlungu is facing several disciplinary charges, including gross misconduct, insubordination and bringing the university into disrepute.

Among the allegations against him is that he unlawfully appointed two executive directors.

World.title: Tshuma plea deal hits another snag
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Ndodana Tshuma made a brief appearance at the Johannesburg Magistrate's Court on Wednesday.

The reason for his short appearance was that plea agreement negotiations between Tshuma and the state had not been finalised.

The 45-year-old is sought for the murder of his wife Zandile,42, and two children Natalie,15, and Nala, five, in July in the United Kingdom. He fled the country via Heathrow Airport.

He was arrested in Johannesburg and was found in possession of a firearm. He has pleaded guilty for contravening the Immigration Act and being in possession of an unlicensed firearm.

World.title: GBV cases must move from reports to convictions, Commission says
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Commission for Gender Equality is calling for a major shift in the country’s response to gender-based violence and femicide, from simply reporting cases to ensuring that they are successfully prosecuted.

The commission said too many GBV cases fall through the cracks of the criminal justice system, leaving alleged perpetrators free while victims are denied justice.

Acting chairperson Mfundo Nomvungu said the National Prosecuting Authority must account for gaps within the prosecution system and demonstrate that GBV cases can be taken through the courts successfully.

“Let there be an example of these cases in court so that we see that gender-based violence and femicide can actually be prosecuted,” Nomvungu said.

His comments follow President Cyril Ramaphosa’s address on gender-based violence and come as the commission prepares to engage with the National Prosecuting Authority.

Nomvungu said the commission wants the NPA to explain why so many cases are dropped before reaching a successful prosecution.

“It’s no longer an issue of reporting cases. It’s about the system that can put a solid case together to prosecute that case,” he said.

The commission said failed prosecutions can have devastating consequences, particularly when alleged perpetrators return to communities and potentially come into contact with the same women who reported them.

Nomvungu said the justice system must ensure that victims do not walk away empty-handed after reporting abuse.

World.title: Yellow Level 2 weather warning for Limpopo, NW, Gauteng
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for the northern parts of the country.

The affected areas include the central to eastern parts of the North West, Gauteng and the central to western parts of the Limpopo province.

The Weather Service has warned of severe thunderstorms with heavy downpours, strong damaging winds and hail. This can cause localised flooding of susceptible roads, low-lying areas and bridges.

Localised damage to settlements and infrastructure is expected over Gauteng, North West and Limpopo.

The Weather Service also warns of damaging winds over Nelson Mandela Bay and Buffalo City Metro Municipalities. These winds will also travel over the Ndlambe, Nqgushwa and Sundays River Valley Local Municipalities.

A fire warning has also been issued for Matzikama Municipality, Cederberg, Bergrivier and Kamiesberg municipalities.

World.title: Ad hoc committee | MPs near completion of report
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The SAPS Ad Hoc Committee is nearing the final stretch of its long-running work, with MPs now pushing to complete a draft report by 30 October.

The committee is working against its sixth extended deadline, as members continue deliberations on inputs submitted by political parties.

Once the draft report is finalised, implicated individuals will be given an opportunity to respond and provide their input.

The process will then move to the National Assembly, where the report will be formally tabled.

World.title: Raila Odinga Mausoleum nears to be unveiled next week
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Outlook of the Raila Odinga mausoleum on September 30, 2026. [Courtesy]

The mausoleum of former Prime Minister Raila Amolo Odinga is now more than 95 per cent complete ahead of its planned unveiling next week.

Speaking during the inspection of the progress ahead of the unveiling during the forthcoming memorial milestone, Defence Principal Secretary Patrick Mariru said the final touches are being put to a new chapter in the history of Kang’o ka Jaramogi, Bondo.

The imposing memorial, being constructed alongside the resting place of Kenya’s first Vice President, the late Jaramogi Oginga Odinga, is taking shape as a permanent site of remembrance for one of Kenya’s most prominent political figures.

“In just two months, the project has progressed significantly and is now over 95 per cent complete,” Mariru said. Engineers explains to Defence PS Patrick Mururi the artwork at the Raila Odinga's Mausoleum on September 30, 2026. [Courtesy]

The Ministry of Defence took over the construction in July 2026, following a directive by President William Ruto, and has overseen a rapid acceleration of works in the past two months.

He was accompanied by National Museums of Kenya Director General Prof Mary Gikungu, with officials from NMK, Kenya Defence Forces, National Government Administration and Bondo Sub-County also present.

The project is being implemented jointly by the Ministry of Defence and NMK, with the museums body providing heritage and technical support. An emblem of former Prime Minister Raila Odinga inside the mausoleum on September 30, 2026. [Courtesy]

The project incorporat specialised architectural works, landscaping, heritage elements, security infrastructure and finishing, would ordinarily run into tens of millions of shillings.

The mausoleum has also undergone redesign during its development, evolving into a more prominent contemporary memorial structure while retaining its connection to the heritage of Kang’o ka Jaramogi.

Its current form is defined by a substantial, sculptural profile designed to stand out within the historic compound, with broad architectural lines and a formal memorial character.

Defence PS Patrick Mururi taken through the artwork of the Raila Odinga mausoleum on September 30, 2026. [Courtesy]

The redesigned structure is intended to do more than provide a resting place. It is being positioned as a permanent heritage landmark within a site already closely associated with Kenya’s political history and the Odinga family legacy.

During the inspection, Mariru said the remaining work largely involves final finishing, inspections and preparations for the unveiling.

“Today, I led a team from the Ministry of Defence to Kang’o ka Jaramogi to assess the progress of the project and ascertain its readiness ahead of the unveiling,” he said.

Engineers working on the Raila Odinga mausoleum with Defence PS Patrick Mururi on September 30, 2026. [Courtesy]

The development marks the latest addition to Kang’o ka Jaramogi, a site deeply associated with Jaramogi Oginga Odinga and the political history of independent Kenya.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: KRA seizes 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret Airport
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The consignment was intercepted by KRA enforcement teams following an intelligence report.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has seized a consignment containing 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret International Airport, averting a potential tax loss of Sh21.5 million.

KRA enforcement teams intercepted the consignment after an intelligence report indicated it contained undeclared mobile phones and other high-end electronic goods.

The cargo, which had been declared under five Customs entries, was part of consolidated shipments that also included shoes, clothing, automotive spare parts, household goods, electronic accessories and other assorted items.

KRA said an initial declaration listed only 3,000 smartphones. However, verification established 55,607 ordinary smartphones, alongside 309 undeclared high-end smartphones.

The high-end devices included Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max models.

“The consignment therefore reflects both under-declaration and non-declaration of dutiable goods,” KRA said in a statement issued on Wednesday.

The tax authority said the verification exercise was conducted to establish whether all mobile phones contained in the consignment had been properly declared.

KRA said the alleged tax evasion contravenes Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), 2004.

The law provides that a person who makes a false or incorrect Customs entry, or knowingly participates in the fraudulent evasion of duty, commits an offence.

“A person who, in any matter relating to Customs, makes any entry which is false or incorrect in any particular, or in any way is knowingly concerned in any fraudulent evasion of the payment of any duty, commits an offence,” KRA said, citing the law.

According to the authority, a person convicted under the provision is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a fine of up to US$10,000.

KRA said it was intensifying efforts to uncover tax evasion schemes to improve revenue compliance and ensure adherence to tax laws and procedures.

“KRA is actively engaged in unearthing tax evasion schemes to boost tax revenue compliance as well as adherence to tax laws and procedures, hence ensuring fair trade is maintained within the market,” the authority said.

The authority also appealed to members of the public, taxpayers and businesses with information on individuals, companies or networks involved in the generation, sale, purchase or use of fictitious VAT invoices to report them.

KRA said information provided would be treated confidentially and the identity of informants kept anonymous.

World.title: 'We know what happened': Uhuru claims Raila won 2022 polls
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [File, Standard]

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta says he remains convinced that Raila Odinga won the 2022 presidential election.

Speaking during a Jubilee Party meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, September 22, Uhuru questioned how the Azimio coalition could have lost the presidency despite performing strongly in other elective races.

“We did everything to help Baba become President of the Republic of Kenya. He got the votes, and to this day I know that he is the one who won those votes. We know how things happened, and we do not want it to happen that way again,” Uhuru said.

The late Odinga contested the August 9, 2022 election under the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition Party, with Martha Karua as his running mate. Ruto ran under the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as the presidential candidate of the Kenya Kwanza Alliance.

Ruto was declared president-elect after garnering 7,176,141 votes, 50.49 per cent, against Odinga's 6,942,930 votes, 48.85 per cent. Ruto's margin was 233,211 votes.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld his election after dismissing petitions challenging the results.

But Uhuru pointed to the coalition's performance in the parliamentary and county races to question how Azimio could have lost the presidency.

“How can you say we were defeated when we had most of the MPs, governors and senators? How were we defeated in the presidency?” he asked.

In the National Assembly, figures published after the election initially put Azimio ahead of Kenya Kwanza, with 165 seats against 160, while 12 seats were held by independent MPs.

Azimio also won 23 of the 47 governorships, while Kenya Kwanza secured 22. The remaining two were won by Taita Taveta Governor Andrew Mwadime and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, who ran as independent candidates.

In the Senate, Kenya Kwanza had an advantage, winning 24 of the 47 directly elected seats against Azimio's 23.

The parliamentary balance later shifted in favour of Kenya Kwanza after several MPs changed their political allegiance.

In October 2022, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula declared Kenya Kwanza the majority coalition with 179 MPs against Azimio's 157, after several MPs from parties including UDM, MDG, Maendeleo Chap Chap and PAA moved towards the Kenya Kwanza side.

Uhuru also rejected claims that he was responsible for Odinga's loss, saying he was not a candidate in the election.

“I am surprised when people say that we did not help Baba and that they defeated me. I was not on the ballot, and they are lying. I was only Raila's handyman,” he said.

He warned against what he described as divisive and dirty politics, saying Kenya should not repeat the events surrounding the 2022 election.

“Dirty politics and politics aimed at dividing Kenyans will take us nowhere. Let us not divide each other. What does it help us? Sell your manifesto,” Uhuru said.

He said he accepted the Supreme Court's decision after the 2022 presidential petitions and handed over power to Ruto without disputing the outcome, accusing Ruto of dragging his name in his failed leadership.

“When we finished and the court ruled, we did not dispute it. We went and handed over the presidency to them. And now, after four years, they are still talking about Uhuru. But when things are not working, people tend to look for excuses,” he said.

This is the clearest public assertion by the former president since the 2022 elections that Odinga won the presidential vote.

World.title: Venezuela’s unelected leader Delcy Rodríguez seeks lost legitimacy. Will she get it?
World.content:
When she addresses the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, Delcy Rodríguez will stand just a 20-minute cab ride from where her deposed predecessor Nicolás Maduro languishes in pre-trial detention.

Looking at the agenda she has followed during her trip to New York, Rodríguez appears to have allowed enough time ahead of her address to try to bring her country out of the isolation it has faced since 2018, when Maduro delivered the last speech at that forum by a Venezuelan head of state.

After landing in the United States on Monday, Rodríguez said she had arrived “with the firmness and hope of a people that believes in dialogue and unity among nations.” The same day, she met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres; Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) President Ilan Goldfajn; World Bank Group President Ajay Banga; and International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva.

It is unclear what benefits these meetings might bring Rodríguez, still bedeviled by questions of legitimacy because she was not elected to the position she holds.

But time’s passage is working in her favor.

While Donald Trump’s presidency ends in January 2029, there is still no date for Venezuela’s next presidential election. If she withstands pressure from the current US administration, which has many irons in the diplomatic fire, the Chavismo movement of which she is the current torch-bearer will be better positioned to face the future. It still controls the state apparatus, and there are no signs of that changing any time soon.

Rodríguez met with Trump on Tuesday on the sidelines of the General Assembly, during which the leaders “discussed strengthening the bilateral relationship between our countries and advancing a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, and security,” Rodríguez said in a post on X, alongside a photo of the two.

For now, Rodríguez has in Trump her main and unexpected backer.

Gone are the days when, as Maduro’s vice president in September 2019, she used a UN General Assembly address to accuse Washington of imposing “a new form of state terrorism without using bombs, but rather through banks and insurance companies.” She was referring at the time to US sanctions that prevented the South American country from selling its oil through the global financial system.

The acting president’s trip is also the next step in the process of relaunching diplomatic relations following Maduro’s capture by elite American Delta Force soldiers on January 3.

Since then, Venezuela has reactivated consular relations with Chile, Ecuador, Peru, the Dominican Republic and Israel, and has received visits from two Latin American presidents: Colombia’s Gustavo Petro before he left the Nariño Palace and, more recently, Paraguay’s head of state, Santiago Peña.

Trump has presented Venezuela as his great foreign-policy victory, and repeatedly emphasizes how he is overseeing the country after winning what he now describes as a war. The latest demonstration came Tuesday in his speech before the delegations attending the General Assembly.

“To the victor belong the spoils,” he said, referring to the agreement signed by the Pentagon with private energy company Nabep to gain access to 65 billion barrels of oil from Venezuelan reserves.

This display of dominance contrasts with the stalemate in the war with Iran and the inability to successfully mediate a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, all amid the impact of rising fuel prices in the US and a decline in his popularity five weeks before midterm elections.

Rodríguez appears to be taking advantage of this situation to present herself as a reliable partner, willing to leave behind the image projected by Maduro’s government and to bolster the political survival of the Chavismo project at the expense of opposition leader María Corina Machado, who is currently stranded outside Venezuela. According to her spokesman, Machado made three attempts to return to Venezuela while Rodríguez was away, but was refused entry.

But is Washington’s support enough to overlook the fact that Rodríguez does not hold the presidency as the result of free elections? For Brazil’s president, it is not.

Earlier this week, in an interview with CNN, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was highly critical of the relationship Washington and Caracas have been forging in recent months. In his view, Trump has demonstrated that he plays a “very dominant role” over the South American country, while stating that “Venezuela’s sovereignty is over.”

During the interview, the Brazilian president said that, if he were in Rodríguez’s position, he would call national elections so that Venezuelans could decide the political direction of their country. In his address to the UN plenary, he once again invoked that same combative discourse and defense of the principle of sovereignty that he displayed in the interview, contrasting with the silence of the other countries in the region over the absence of a firm date for presidential elections in Venezuela.

Rodríguez will have her turn on Wednesday, and there is considerable anticipation surrounding her speech at a forum where global concerns are routinely aired. For many years, Chavismo relied on the condemnation of imperialism to construct its political identity, and consistently invoked it on this stage.

Now, Washington’s imperial ambitions have been deployed much more forcefully through the revival of the Monroe Doctrine – and a fierce initiative to deport as many migrants as possible from US territory, which has particularly affected the Venezuelan community.

Before January 3, Chavismo would have railed forcefully against these policies. For Delcy Rodríguez, this is no longer the case.

CORRECTION: This story has been updated to correct the date when Rodriguez is speaking at the UN General Assembly.

World.title: Harry and Meghan blame ‘extraordinarily reckless’ paparazzi for security scare at children’s school
World.content:
London —

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex have condemned what they described as “extraordinarily reckless” behavior by international photographers who they say sparked a security scare at their children’s school.

Private security and school staff are understood to have spotted two young men carrying backpacks, later identified as international photographers, walking around the school and stopping to look into the grounds.

A spokesperson for the Sussexes called it “an extraordinary lack of judgment” and an “unacceptable intrusion” after the photographers were seen “walking the perimeter of the school.”

“It is concerning enough that certain European paparazzi appear unwilling to respect the privacy of children at school,” the spokesperson said. “But to behave in this manner in these particular circumstances, and so soon after the incident at RAF Fairford, demonstrates an extraordinary lack of judgment.”

The spokesperson continued, “Whatever photographs they may have been seeking, this was not only an unacceptable intrusion into the privacy of children; it was an irresponsible and ill-considered way to conduct themselves in the vicinity of a school.”

CNN has reached out to police for comment.

British media outlets have taken care not to identify the location of the school or the Sussexes’ residence following a request from the Independent Press Standards Organisation, though their rules do not apply to representatives working for international media outlets.

Prince Harry has long expressed concerns over his family’s security, even before they returned to the UK in late August. Earlier this month, they moved Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, from a previous school just days into the start of the academic term due to security practicalities.

When Harry and Meghan stepped back from royal duties in 2020, the British government decided to downgrade their level of taxpayer-funded security – a decision which the duke fought unsuccessfully in the courts for years. In one of those rulings, the UK’s Home Office argued it was not appropriate for wealthy individuals to buy protective security from specialist police officers.

Harry has continued pressing for protection, often drawing comparisons of what his wife has faced with that of his mother, Diana, who died in 1997 in a high-speed car crash while paparazzi were following her.

This latest incident comes as the couple are reportedly waiting on an official risk assessment now they have returned to the UK from Montecito, California.

The couple has been asked to provide authorities with as much detail as possible about their new daily routines, including trips such as the school run, addresses routinely visited, routes taken and more, according to The Telegraph newspaper earlier this month. That information, along with any other evidence considered relevant, will be used by a branch of the UK’s Home Office to evaluate any changes to the level of threat they face.

World.title: Flight emergency brings Israelis to a country that doesn’t recognize their state
World.content:
The emergency landing of an Israel-bound flight in Saudi Arabia marked a rare mass arrival of Israelis in the kingdom, which has no diplomatic relations with Israel.

Just a few years ago, Israeli airlines and Israel-bound flights were forbidden from even entering Saudi airspace, forcing Israeli holidaymakers to take an hours long detour while traveling east to avoid the vast kingdom.

That changed in 2022, when Riyadh unilaterally allowed Israeli flights to use its airspace as part of a push by the Biden administration to normalize ties between the two countries. It was a milestone for Israeli aviation, significantly shortening routes to Asia, and what allowed Wednesday’s Dubai-Tel Aviv flight to fly over Saudi Arabia.

This wasn’t the first time scores of Israelis unexpectedly landed in the kingdom. In 2023, a Tel Aviv-bound Air Seychelles flight made an emergency landing in the Saudi Red Sea city of Jeddah because of an electrical problem, forcing passengers to stay at an airport hotel. And last year, another Flydubai plane landed in the Saudi capital Riyadh after a passenger suffered a stroke.

Such incidents have been seen as rare signs of Saudi-Israeli cooperation, even as formal normalization remains out of reach.

The Gaza war and its devastating humanitarian toll have hardened Saudi Arabia’s position on recognizing Israel. Riyadh says it will not establish diplomatic relations without the creation of an independent Palestinian state.

World.title: How Dubai became one of Israel’s most popular foreign destinations
World.content:
Dubai – from where the diverted Israel-bound flight was returning – has become one of Israel’s busiest and most frequently served international destinations.

This is thanks to the normalization of relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in 2020, through the brokered Abraham Accords, which allowed commercial aviation services between the two countries to resume.

Since then, the aviation corridor between Ben Gurion Airport (TLV) and Dubai International Airport (DXB) has seen significant growth, with both Israel- and UAE-based airlines expanding operations to meet the demand for tourism and business travel.

According to flight tracking website FlightRadar24, there are typically 70 flights running between Dubai (DXB) and Tel Aviv (TLV) per week. Flydubai is the main carrier operating the route, in addition to Emirates and Israeli airlines Israir and El Al.

Data from Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport in December showed that 1.1 million Israeli passengers traveled to Dubai in 2025.

World.title: Shakira concert sparks surge in travel demand to Egypt
World.content:
Egypt’s tourism market has seen a recent spike driven by the announcement of a concert by global superstar Shakira—scheduled for November 28 at the Giza Pyramids—as well as growing interest in cultural tourism following the full opening of the Grand Egyptian Museum.

European and Russian tourism reports indicate a notable rise in prices for travel and accommodation packages linked to the concert dates.

Rates at hotels near the Pyramids, in particular, have surged by up to 50 percent, alongside increased demand for flights to Cairo during the event period.

Travel packages to Sharm el-Sheikh and Hurghada have also seen varying price increases for the upcoming month of November.

Premier destination

The National Geographic magazine highlighted Egypt as one of the world’s premier destinations for cultural tourism and unique experiences, featuring a guide that outlines 15 diverse itineraries and activities extending far beyond traditional beach tourism.

The list included visits to the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Giza Pyramids; exploring Historic Cairo and the Khan al-Khalili market; Nile cruises on traditional sailboats; hot-air balloon rides over the monuments of Luxor; and visits to the Valley of the Kings.

It also featured adventure excursions in the Sinai Mountains and to Saint Catherine’s Monastery, as well as visits to the pottery village in Fayoum and other heritage sites.

World.title: Abu Marawat Gold Mines to begin production next year
World.content:
The Head of Abu Marawat Gold Mines, Ayman Ibrahim, announced that Egypt’s mining sector is witnessing an unprecedented phase of streamlined processes and expedited procedures, with the Abu Marawat Gold Mines readying to begin production by next year.

He explained that the pre-production phase usually takes three to four years, adding that actual production is scheduled to commence in 2027.

Speaking on the sidelines of a mining conference, Ibrahim explained that the “open block” system—introduced during the latest mineral resources tender—has brought about a qualitative shift in the mining sector.

He added that tendering for gold, phosphate, and kaolin exploration helps simplify and accelerate the offering process compared to the previous system.

Gold exploration

Regarding the allocation of approximately 70 percent of the areas in the latest tender to gold exploration, Ibrahim noted that this attracts a significant number of investors, driven by the rapid evolution and sharp surges in global gold prices.

He referred to significant opportunities and promising indicators of economically viable reserves—with grades ranging from one to two grams per tonne—typically attract investor interest, making the gold sector an appealing prospect for major global and local companies.

Ibrahim said that the company is currently in a transitional phase, which involves completing infrastructure and technical studies, as well as finalizing plant preparations in accordance with the latest global environmental standards.

Ibrahim explained that estimates indicate the project’s reserve volume stands at approximately 150,000 ounces, rising to around half a million ounces in certain areas.

The Abu Marawat Gold Mine Company represents a successful strategic partnership between the Egyptian Mineral Resources Authority and the Canadian company Aton Resources.

World.title: Sisi issues new Presidential directives regarding private vehicle licensing
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered the Interior Ministry to take the necessary measures to serve the best interests of citizens in private vehicle licensing.

These directives emphasize improving the quality of services provided, rationalizing vehicle licensing costs, and ensuring that citizens are treated with courtesy and respect.

These instructions arise when vehicle licensing and renewal procedures are a matter of significant public interest, impacting millions of citizens due to the numerous requirements and steps involved in the licensing process.

Vehicle license renewal fees at traffic units vary based on the vehicle’s engine capacity and the duration of the license. Additional costs apply for inspection, insurance, documentation, the electronic sticker, and other required procedures.

Based on available data, the total cost of renewing a car license for three years may range from LE4,000 to LE 6,000 or more—depending on the vehicle category and engine displacement—excluding the cost of any traffic fines

Vehicle Tax

The renewal tax amount varies according to the vehicle’s engine displacement: it is approximately LE 225 for cars with an engine capacity between 1,030 cc and 1,330 cc.

For cars with an engine capacity between 1,330 cc and 1,630 cc, the tax reaches approximately LE 750 , while it stands at about LE 3,000 for cars with an engine capacity between 1,630 cc and 2,030 cc.

For vehicles with an engine capacity exceeding 2,030 cc, the tax is calculated at a rate of 2.5 percent of the vehicle’s value.

Cost of Three-Year Renewal

When renewing the license for a three-year period, the cost of the tax and mandatory insurance increases; figures indicate approximately LE 3,390 for the tax and LE 190 for the insurance.

Car Licensing Requirements for 2026

The key requirements for car licensing include the following:

Payment of prescribed taxes and fees.

Civil liability insurance covering vehicle accidents and resulting property damage.

Compliance of the vehicle with safety and road-worthy standards.

Installing a GPS device.

The license applicant must be at least 18 years old (or 21 years old for professional-use licenses).

Passing a medical examination at centers accredited by the General Directorate of Traffic.

Possession of an educational certificate or a literacy certificate.

Completion of a safe driving fundamentals course at a traffic-affiliated driving school.

Undergoing a drug screening test.

The applicant must not have a conviction for certain criminal offenses, in accordance with applicable regulations.

No prior convictions for homicide or causing injury while driving a vehicle.

Submission of four 4×6 personal photos, two medical certificates (general health and vision), and two copies of the national ID card.

Equipping the vehicle with a reflective warning triangle, a first-aid kit, and fire extinguishers.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: When is the longest total solar eclipse in Egypt?
World.content:
Next year, Egypt and several other Arab nations are anticipating a rare astronomical event – a total solar eclipse.

During this event, the solar disk will be completely obscured for several minutes in certain areas—an extraordinary spectacle that captures the attention of astronomy enthusiasts and researchers worldwide.

Astronomical calculations indicate that this upcoming astronomical event will be one of the longest total solar eclipses of the current century, with a path that spans regions including Egypt and various Arab countries.

When is the Total Solar Eclipse?

The rare total solar eclipse will fall on Saturday, August 2, 2027. It will be visible to people across the globe, and clearly observable from Egypt.

An eclipse is prolonged when the Moon is at its closest point to Earth and the path of the Moon’s shadow lies near the equator.

Path of the 2027 Total Solar Eclipse

The path of the total eclipse will begin over the Atlantic Ocean, crossing the Strait of Gibraltar and southern Spain before entering North Africa.

It will traverse Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, and Somalia, continuing on to the Indian Ocean.

Spanning approximately 170 miles (about 270 km) in width, the eclipse’s path will cover densely populated areas, offering millions of people the opportunity to witness the event firsthand.

In Saudi Arabia, the total eclipse will pass over the cities of Jeddah and Makkah, while a partial eclipse will be visible across parts of southern Italy and the island of Lampedusa.

Duration

At its peak, the total solar eclipse lasts more than six full minutes—an exceptional duration ranking among the longest in modern records of solar phenomena.

This offers a rare opportunity for scientific observation and photography.

Arab and international astronomical observatories are expected to release detailed maps of the eclipse paths, the best viewing locations, and guidelines for safe observation using specialized glasses.

Prime Locations

The total solar eclipse is set to reach its peak in the city of Luxor, where darkness will envelop the sky for more than six consecutive minutes—making it one of the best locations in the world to witness the event.

By comparison, most total eclipses typically last no more than three minutes.

Cities such as Cádiz and Málaga in Spain will experience total darkness lasting between four and five minutes, while Benghazi, Libya, will be plunged into deep darkness for nearly five minutes.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Liberia: Criminal Court Rejects Peter Bon Jallah’s Acquittal Bid, Orders Him to Take Witness Stand
World.content:
Judge Wesseh Says Prosecution Evidence Requires Defense Response as Statutory Rape Trial Moves Forward

By Willie N. Tokpah

Monrovia-Criminal Court “E” for Montserrado County has rejected a motion seeking the acquittal of 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, ruling that the prosecution’s evidence presented so far is not “wholly insufficient” to terminate the case before the defense has presented its evidence.



In a ruling delivered Wednesday, September 30, Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonsus Wesseh, Sr. denied and dismissed Jallah’s Motion for Judgment of Acquittal, clearing the way for the defendant to take the witness stand as the trial enters a critical phase.

Jallah is facing charges growing out of allegations of Gang Rape, Statutory Rape and Kidnapping involving a 16-year-old male. He has denied the allegations and opted for a bench trial.

The ruling followed the prosecution’s presentation of 12 witnesses, including the alleged victim, police investigators, medical personnel and a Rwandan forensic expert who testified concerning DNA analysis.

The defense had argued that inconsistencies in the alleged victim’s account, questions surrounding an alleged crime scene on Camp Johnson Road, the absence of a woman the victim said he encountered there, medical evidence and the DNA findings created sufficient doubt to warrant an immediate acquittal.

But Judge Wesseh rejected the defense’s position at this stage of the proceedings.

‘Premature’ to End Trial

The court said granting the motion after the prosecution had rested would be premature, particularly because the prosecution had given notice that it could present rebuttal witnesses after the defense completes its case.

The judge emphasized that a judgment of acquittal may be granted where the evidence is “wholly insufficient” to establish guilt, citing the Supreme Court’s decision in Republic of Liberia v. Robert A. Smith, 25 LLR 207 (1976).

According to the ruling, however, the evidence already produced by the prosecution provides sufficient grounds for the court to hear the defense before determining the case.

The court also cited Potter v. Republic, 1 LLR 67, and Logan v. Republic, 33 LLR 434 (1985), in addressing the defense’s arguments concerning alleged defects and inconsistencies in the indictment.

Judge Wesseh said that if the defense believed the indictment was defective, it should have raised those objections through a motion to dismiss before trial.

Defense Attacks Crime Scene Evidence

A major component of the defense’s motion centered on the alleged Camp Johnson Road location where the alleged victim said he was taken and sexually abused.

The defense pointed to testimony from Police Officer Lindsey Gould, who reportedly told the court that investigators were unable to identify or locate the alleged crime scene.

The defense argued that the alleged victim’s testimony concerning the unidentified location should therefore be stricken from the record and that the uncertainty surrounding the location created reasonable doubt.

The court, however, declined to resolve the credibility and evidentiary disputes at the acquittal stage.

The defense also highlighted alleged differences between the victim’s testimony and the police charge sheet concerning the dates and locations of the alleged sexual encounters at Jallah’s Airfield residence.

Medical, DNA Evidence Challenged

The defense further attacked the prosecution’s medical and forensic evidence.

According to the ruling, defense lawyers argued that a medical nurse who testified about lacerations and bruises observed in the alleged victim’s anus did not conclusively state that the injuries were caused by rape.

The defense also relied on the testimony of the Rwandan forensic expert, arguing that the DNA examination could not establish penetration or independently classify the alleged offenses as statutory rape or gang rape.

The prosecution countered that it had established a prima facie case linking Jallah to the alleged crimes and urged the court to allow the trial to proceed.

Judge: Defense Must Now Respond

In a significant portion of the ruling, Judge Wesseh said the court could not properly determine the defendant’s guilt or innocence solely on the prosecution’s evidence without giving the defense an opportunity to present its case.

The court stated that the prosecution’s evidence contains the material elements requiring the defense to provide a response before the bench makes a final determination.

Judge Wesseh further referenced Allen Yancy v. Republic, 4 LLR (1935), stating that the surrounding circumstances of a criminal case should be placed before the fact-finder before a final decision is reached.

The court therefore ordered the trial to proceed “unhindered.”

Jallah Ordered to Take Witness Stand

Following the ruling, the court ordered that Jallah take the witness stand as the defense begins presenting its evidence.

One of Jallah’s lawyers immediately excepted to the ruling and announced that the defense would take advantage of the statute governing such exceptions.

The judge noted the exception as a matter of law.

The ruling leaves the central allegations against Jallah unresolved. The court has made clear that Wednesday’s decision was not a determination of guilt or innocence, but rather a decision that the evidence presented thus far does not justify ending the case before the defense is heard.

World.title: 72-Year-Old Ill Man Cries Out for Help, Decries Snail-Pace Justice System with No Means of Survival
World.content:
Monrovia – Liberia’s justice system is among many in the world that continues to receive backlashes from the public with many terming it weak, corrupt, and for sale to the highest bidder.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

Successive reports have cited case backlogs, shortage of judges and magistrates, limited prosecutorial capacity, and overcrowded prisons.



In the case of 72-year-old ailing Andrew S. Boikpah, his family is in complete despair as a result of slow litigation that spanned over nearly two years in conference room and more than 90 days now since it appeared at the Criminal “C”.

All started when he entered into a lease agreement with one Edwin J. Nyarngo for a parcel of land around the James Spriggs Airfield in Sinkor, on the outskirt of Monrovia.

Prior to the agreement, Boikpah explained that the parcel of land in question was used as gas station, and as such, it contained two tankers beneath the ground.

The tankers, which he narrated, worth a combined value of US$30,000, were surreptitiously removed from beneath the ground by the leaser without his knowledge.

“I reported the matter to my lawyer, and he wrote him for a conference. It took more than a year, in fact nearly two years. During that period, my son passed away. I called and texted him several times, but he and his lawyers never showed up for the conference. My counselor then advised me to sue him, which I did,” explained Boikpah.

With the matter now before the court, the aging ailing man narrated that the matter has never been heard despite admittance by the defendant during pretrial.

“When the matter went to court, at Criminal Court ‘C’ where it has been for over nearly three months, they admitted to having the tanks and asked me to go and get them. But when I went, he showed me a different tank, which I refused to take in exchange of my tank. Despite all these, the court has never heard the case one day. Anytime we get there, there is always a new excuse that the case cannot be called.”

“What pains me most is that someone took my treasure worth $30,000 and the court that supposed to be our refuge does nothing about it. You are making me cry more and my family is dying. Absolutely, I have no other means of survival. I have been sick for very long time and been in Ghana seeking medication. All that I have is gone. I am sick; very sick and no means to cater to my family. That lease is up to 20 years and an optional five years extension. My life is completely miserable, especially for my children and grandchildren. I need help,” Boikpah burst up in cry while explaining to this write at the offices of FrontPage Africa.

Liberia’s judicial system has been in a middle of controversies amid varying reports of justice tempering, corruption among other others.

A New Narratives investigative report published by the New Dawn Newspaper January 19, 2026 revealed that many say “no one believes in the same national courts” because of political interference. It states that justice is seen as a tool for the political elite to suppress dissent. The separation of powers is compromised, with the judiciary operating under the influence of political elites.

The Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Fiscal Year 2026 Scorecard — May 15, 2026 also revealed that Liberia failed the Rule of Law indicator with 44%, posting a negative score of -0.06 against the peer-group median of 0.00. This marks the second consecutive year of failure, down from 47% in FY2025 and 59% in FY2024. According to MCC: The indicator evaluates “public confidence in the judiciary and police, including the government’s ability to enforce laws, contracts, and property rights fairly and effectively.”

World.title: Liberia: Succession Shockwaves Offer Challenge to Potential Presidential Hopefuls
World.content:
Monrovia – It was the kind of moment politicians plan for and pretend they didn’t.

By Rodney D. Sieh

In a hall full of Liberians who had driven in from Maryland, New Jersey, Minnesota and beyond, someone asked President Joseph Nyuma Boakai the question that has hovered over the Executive Mansion since the day he took the oath: Will you run again?



The 81-year-old did not answer. He turned it around. Did they want him to seek another term? The room said yes. The President smiled, the easy smile of a man who has spent more than four decades in Liberian politics, and replied: “I am still entitled to one term.”

Seven words. No declaration, no denial. But in a country where the 2029 race has been quietly underway for months, it was enough to set phones buzzing from Alexandria to Zwedru.

A question with an age attached

The setting was the Liberia Diaspora Annual Conference. Boakai addressed the gathering in Alexandria, Virginia, pressing Liberians abroad to move past talk and turn their patriotism, skills and money into measurable projects at home. The theme, fittingly, was about moving from dialogue to delivery.

But the arithmetic behind his answer is hard to ignore. Boakai was born on November 30, 1944, in Worsonga, Lofa County. He would be 84 on election day in 2029 and 91 by the end of a second six-year term. The Constitution allows him to run; the question Liberians will debate at kitchen tables and in attaya shops is whether he should.

His remark was also not quite a bolt from the blue. In June, Vice President Jeremiah Koung told a crowd in Nimba County’s Yarwin Mehnsonoh District that Boakai intended to seek a second term and that he, Koung, would serve as campaign manager. Weeks ago, presidential adviser MacDella Cooper posted a message cheering “6 more years” for the President. What changed over the weekend is that, for the first time publicly, the signal came from Boakai himself.

Koung: heir, or man in the waiting room?

No one has more riding on that smile than Jeremiah Kpan Koung.

Born in Yekepa in 1978, Koung rose from the House of Representatives to the Senate before becoming Vice President in January 2024. At 48, he is young enough to wait, and ambitious enough that waiting is painful. A Liberian Observer commentary last year described him as visibly eager to occupy the presidential chair in 2029.

A Boakai second term pushes that dream to 2035. Yet Koung has chosen to embrace it rather than fight it. “I’m currently paving the roads for the president of Liberia to come back,” he told residents in Nimba. It is a calculated bet: carry the old man’s bags to victory, and inherit the party’s machinery and goodwill when he finally steps aside.

The risk is that six more years is a long time to hold a coalition together. Koung is not just Vice President. He also leads the Movement for Democracy and Reconstruction (MDR), the party founded by the late Senator Prince Y. Johnson, which was a key pillar of the coalition that carried the Boakai-Koung ticket in 2023. The Nimba alliance that once rallied behind Johnson has already shown signs of splintering under ambition and mistrust, and reports, not independently verified, that Koung is backing a challenger to Unity Party Senator Prince Moye in Bong have raised questions about whether coalition politics and party loyalty can coexist. The longer the succession question stays open, the more those tensions fester.

Ngafuan: been here before

If Koung is the heir in waiting, Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan is the loyalist with a long memory.

Ngafuan knows what it means to put ambition on hold. He was national campaign manager for Boakai’s 2017 presidential run. Before that, he left the Unity Party in 2016 to pursue the presidency, only to announce in May 2017 that he would no longer run, unwilling to stand against the party. He came home, and today he holds the most powerful purse in government.

Now 56, Ngafuan has spent recent days at the UN General Assembly, where he laid out a goal of reaching 75 percent electricity access by 2029-2030. That target is a campaign promise waiting to be written. The question is whose campaign.

A Boakai second term would ask Ngafuan to do what he did in 2017: step back and wait. By 2035 he would be 65 and competing not only with Koung but with a new generation of politicians who will have spent a decade building their own bases. For a man whose power flows from the President’s trust, openly challenging the boss is unthinkable. Quietly building a network while delivering the numbers may be the only path.

Other figures in the President’s circle face the same calculation: loyalty now, or positioning for a future that keeps moving further away.

The opposition’s unexpected gift

As Boakai smiled in Virginia, the opposition was busy in Monrovia. On the same Sunday, five opposition parties signed a joint communiqué committing to closer cooperation ahead of 2029, at a roundtable hosted by MPC leader Simeon Freeman at Sinkor Palace. Former President George Weah of the CDC was joined by Alexander Cummings of the ANC, Maxwell Kemayah of MOVEE, Freeman, and Mason of the ULDP.

The document accuses the government of losing territory to Guinea, fighting corruption and drugs selectively, defying the Supreme Court, and using a new cybercrime law against critics. But on the big question of who leads, the leaders held back. “We are not discussing who becomes president, who becomes vice president,” Freeman told reporters.

That is precisely where a Boakai candidacy could change the equation. An open seat in 2029 would have invited every opposition heavyweight to believe his moment had come, the same clash of egos that undermined the Collaborating Political Parties. An incumbent on the ballot concentrates minds. The election becomes a referendum on one man’s record, one government’s promises, and one very visible question about age and vigor.

The margins invite them to try. Boakai beat Weah in 2023 by roughly 20,567 votes. Weah has already declared that the road to 2029 begins now.

But incumbency cuts both ways. A sitting president controls the budget, the appointments and the calendar of ribbon-cuttings. And the opposition has made this promise before.

The people who decide

For all the drama at the top, the verdict on a second Boakai term will not be delivered in a Virginia ballroom. It will be delivered by the market woman in Red-Light counting the cost of rice, the motorcyclist in Ganta dodging potholes on a road he was promised would be paved, the teacher in Voinjama waiting on salary arrears.

They did not get to answer the President’s question on Sunday. In October 2029, they will.

World.title: Liberia: President Boakai’s Name Drags In Courtroom Record In Saudi Rice Trial
World.content:
MONROVIA — President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s name entered the courtroom record Monday as former General Services Agency (GSA) Director-General Mary T. Broh testified in the Saudi-donated rice trial, linking a letter from Boakai’s transition activities to a request for rice for young people working on a national cleanup campaign.

By Willie N. Tokpah

Broh, a subpoenaed defense witness for former Foreign Minister Dee-Maxwell Saah Kemayah and other defendants, told Criminal Court “C” that Kemayah’s intervention in the rice matter was intended to “rescue the rice” and described the indictment against her and other officials as “character assassination.”



Her testimony offered a different account from the prosecution’s theory that the movement and distribution of the Saudi-donated rice formed part of an unlawful scheme.

The remaining defendants face charges including theft of property, economic sabotage, misapplication of entrusted property, abuse of office and criminal conspiracy.

The Saudi donation consisted of 29,412 bags of 25-kilogram rice intended for disaster victims and vulnerable communities. Prosecutors allege that 25,054 bags, valued at approximately US$425,918, were unlawfully diverted or could not be accounted for.

Boakai’s Name Enters the Record

One of the most significant portions of Broh’s testimony concerned President Boakai’s transition activities.

Broh testified that John-Charuk Siafa, now Monrovia City Mayor, approached her while coordinating a cleanup campaign associated with Boakai’s inauguration.

According to Broh, Siafa told her he had been appointed by then-President-elect Boakai to coordinate the campaign and showed her his appointment letter.

She said the letter directed Siafa to contact her because she was considered a source of assistance for mobilization.

Broh testified that she later became concerned when young people participating in the cleanup complained that they had nothing to eat. She said she contacted Siafa and instructed him to write the Ministry of Internal Affairs requesting rice.

According to Broh, Siafa subsequently wrote then-Internal Affairs Minister Varney Sirleaf, after which rice was made available.

Broh’s testimony did not establish that President Boakai personally ordered the distribution of the Saudi rice. Rather, her account placed the transition-related cleanup campaign and Siafa’s appointment at the beginning of a chain of events through which rice was requested for “hungry cleanup campaign workers.”

‘Kemayah Was Rescuing the Rice’

Broh also challenged the prosecution’s characterization of Kemayah’s involvement.

She testified that Kemayah contacted her about the Saudi-funded rice and that a meeting was subsequently held at the GSA involving the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Internal Affairs, the National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) and GSA.

Because of Kemayah’s official engagements and travel, Broh said he designated Deputy Foreign Minister Thelma Duncan Sawyer to participate in his place.

According to Broh, the institutions agreed to work together and minutes were taken during the meeting.

She characterized Kemayah’s intervention as an effort to “rescue” the rice.

Broh said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs became involved because the donation was connected to Liberia’s bilateral relationship with Saudi Arabia.

She maintained that the participation of Foreign Affairs, Internal Affairs, NDMA and GSA was part of an institutional effort to secure and manage the humanitarian commodity.

GSA Transfer Defended

Broh also defended the transfer of 13,895 bags of rice from NDMA to GSA, a movement that prosecutors have placed at the center of their case.

She testified that it was agreed through an interagency mandate that the remaining Saudi rice be moved to GSA for storage until further notice.

She also argued that GSA had a statutory responsibility to serve as custodian of government property and maintained warehouses for commodities and emergency supplies.

Had she known about the rice earlier, Broh testified, she would have recommended that it be stored at GSA because NDMA lacked adequate facilities for such a large quantity.

According to her, this has been the practice with several previous donations to the government. She cited, as an example, 60,000 bags of rice donated by the Government of the People’s Republic of China, which she said were stored by the GSA and subsequently distributed to beneficiaries.

She said the rice was inventoried upon arrival at GSA and that subsequent releases were subject to documentation and a gate-pass system.

According to Broh, requesting organizations were required to provide supporting documents, while information about trucks, including drivers’ names, telephone numbers and license plates, was recorded before rice could leave the warehouse.

She further testified that she and Sawyer used personal resources to facilitate the transfer, including securing trucks from the Liberia Electricity Corporation, and that no government funds were used for transportation.

‘The Indictment Is Character Assassination’

Broh stood by her earlier description of the indictment as “character assassination.”

“I sincerely mean what I said,” she told the court.

She maintained that officials were acting within their respective mandates to receive and distribute commodities based on requests.

She also pointed to documents she said she provided to investigators, questioning why she would voluntarily turn over records that could help trace the rice if she intended to steal it.

The 1,050-Bag Dispute

Broh also addressed allegations involving approximately 1,050 bags of rice, connecting the quantity to the Boakai transition cleanup campaign.

She testified that young people working long hours on the campaign complained about a lack of food. According to her, Siafa approached her for assistance after being appointed to coordinate the cleanup.

Broh said she helped facilitate communication with government institutions, after which a request was made to Internal Affairs and rice was released.

Her testimony sought to place the disputed quantity within a government-related request rather than a personal diversion.

Johnson Challenges Prosecution’s Accounting

For his part, former Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs Momolu Johnson testified Tuesday, challenging aspects of the prosecution’s accounting of the rice.

Johnson questioned how certain quantities were treated in the government’s case, including 720 bags that he argued had not been properly exhibited to support the stealing allegation.

He also cited figures he said were presented to the defense, including 12,095 bags under relevant control and 2,281 bags remaining at GSA.

His testimony formed part of the defense effort to challenge both the prosecution’s calculations and its theory of criminal intent.

The competing figures have emerged as a central issue in the trial.

The indictment states that the original donation consisted of 29,412 bags. Prosecution evidence has placed 11,200 bags at GSA initially and another 13,895 bags transferred from NDMA, producing a reported 25,095 bags in GSA custody.

The prosecution has alleged that 25,054 bags were diverted or could not be accounted for, while defense witnesses have introduced additional figures involving distributions, pre-positioned rice and quantities remaining in storage.

The defense is using those discrepancies to challenge the prosecution’s accounting and argue that the movement of the rice through government institutions does not, by itself, establish criminal intent.

The defendants have pleaded not guilty and remain presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

The trial continues today, Wednesday, September 30, with the continuation of defendant Johnson’s testimony.

World.title: Liberia: Support the Women of the Lofa Women Weaving Center
World.content:
Illustration: Women weave Lofa Cloth from local cotton into blankets, bags and garments.

A short video from James Dorbor Jallah, Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority, made my day.

By Axel M. Addy

It showed the Lofa Women Weaving Center open again. The center started as an idea while I was Minister of Commerce and Industry. For years after 2018, it stood idle. Now the Government of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has brought it back. I thank the President and every official, community leader and weaver who kept pushing for this day.



For me, this is personal. I know the women, the land and the promise behind that building.

One question

The project began with one question. How can Liberia turn a product we treasure into a steady income for rural women?

Lofa has woven country cloth for generations. Families wear it and keep it. Yet the women who made it earned little from their skill. We wanted to change that. We wanted a Liberian brand called Lofa Cloth, with quality standards, legal protection and buyers at home and abroad.

Help from Japan

The answer started in Tokyo.

The Government of Japan invited me on an official visit. I met members of the Diet, Japan’s parliament, and made the case for Liberia’s small businesses. Our Japanese friends listened, and they acted.

In 2014, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry established the Liberia Innovation Fund for Entrepreneurship, the LIFE Fund, under a grant from the Government of Japan. Japan signed the Note Verbale on April 22, 2014. The fund had an approved budget of US$665,000. It supported three initiatives: the E-Plus youth entrepreneurship program, the Liberian Marketplace at the Nancy Doe Market, and the Lofa Women Weaving Center.

The road to Kolahun

After Japan, my team and I travelled to Kolahun. The Superintendent hosted us. We sat with weavers, producers and community leaders. We asked how much cloth they made, what they needed and where a center could stand.

The elders of Lofa answered with a gift. They donated land from a 25-acre site for the center. The people of Bolahun and Kolahun, in Liberia’s cotton belt, worked together to make it possible. That cooperation showed the community owned this project from the first day.

We also gave the women a challenge. We asked them to create two or three new colour patterns. We asked them to make blankets, throws and placemats for the national MSME Conference.

They exceeded every expectation. At the MSME Conference, their products won a US$5,000 prize. At the Made in Liberia Trade Fair, their work sold out.

I learned a lesson in Kolahun that still guides me. Liberia does not lack talent. We lack organized production, design support, finance, market access and steady follow-through.

Munah Pelham’s vision

The late Hon. Munah Pelham saw this early. As a designer and model, she brought Liberian designers together for a country cloth fashion show at the 2014 MSME Conference. Designers made handbags, garments and accessories from the cloth. The show proved a traditional fabric could compete in modern fashion and remain Liberian. I remember her energy with gratitude.

What we built

The center was part of the Rural Industrial Promotion Program for Economic Empowerment (RIPE). Its goal was to organize rural women into cooperatives of 50 to 150 members. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry provided US$231,000 for construction through the LIFE Fund, under the Japanese grant.

The design included:

A showroom for sales and exhibitions

A tailoring hall for at least 10 tailors

A weaving hall for at least 30 weavers

A cotton receiving and processing hall for at least 5 machines

Apprenticeship training for young weavers

The building went up. After 2018, it lacked the management, funding and market support it needed. The plan also relied on several ministries. The Ministry of Agriculture would support cotton farming. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry would connect the center to industrial policy, design and markets. When that coordination stopped, the center stopped too.

The next task: build the market

Phase one built the center. Phase two must build demand.

Liberia needs a national strategy for Lofa Cloth. It should cover cotton supply, weaving capacity, quality standards, modern design, cooperative management and reliable markets.

The Buy Liberian, Build Liberia agenda gives us a platform. The Wear Your Pride campaign gives us a simple action. If government officials wear Liberian-made clothing every Friday, weavers, tailors and designers gain regular customers. Citizens see that national pride includes buying Liberian.

Government can go further. Use Lofa Cloth for national gifts, official delegations and state events. Ask our embassies and diaspora groups to promote it abroad. Encourage hotels, airlines, universities and large firms to buy it.

The industry also needs investment in cotton processing, modern and manual looms, training, packaging, quality certification, e-commerce, trade fairs and geographical indication protection.

At a WTO Public Forum, I met a group from Burkina Faso that builds manual looms and trains women across Africa. Liberia should partner with African producers like them. Appropriate tools can multiply what our weavers produce.

Every Liberian has a role

The center can employ hundreds of women. It can create work for cotton farmers, transporters, designers, tailors, traders, photographers and exporters.

Government must lead with policy and resources. Businesses must invest and buy. Designers must innovate. The diaspora must promote and purchase. Development partners must support export readiness. Consumers must choose Liberian.

Lofa Cloth carries the history and skill of Liberian women. With steady support, it can travel from Kolahun to Monrovia, to the region and to the world.

So I ask every Liberian: Wear Your Pride. When you buy Lofa Cloth, you support a woman at her loom in Kolahun. You support a farmer, a tailor and a designer. You Buy Liberian, and you help Build Liberia.
