World.title: Iraq’s US dollar exchange rate slightly falls after days-long spike
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar slightly declined on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil, following a days-long spike.

The US dollar exchange rate declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,570 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,572.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,575 Iraqi dinars and 1,565 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also declined, fluctuating between 1,571.5 and 1,571 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars for every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq declares conclusion of US-led mission, thanks member states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, announced on Wednesday the conclusion of the US-led international coalition’s mission to combat ISIS in Iraq.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi government, al-Zaidi thanked the international coalition’s member states for their participation in defeating the terrorist group ISIS.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during an official military event held in Baghdad to mark Iraq’s Sovereignty Day, a national holiday marking the withdrawal of US and international coalition forces from Iraq.

The event marked the formal conclusion of the Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve, following the complete withdrawal of coalition forces and equipment from key military bases in Iraq.

Al-Zaidi thanked the international coalition’s member states, commanders, and advisers, stating that collaboration has effectively overcome a difficult period of extremism.

The handover is an indication of Iraq’s full responsibility for the security and stability of the country, as well as combating terrorism.

Addressing armed factions, al-Zaidi declared that there shall be no firearms outside the framework of the law and no force outside the institutions of the state.

The Iraqi prime minister said earlier that October 1, 2026, will mark a new day in Iraq’s statehood when the country achieves complete sovereignty free of foreign troops.

Iraq’s future engagements with the international coalition’s member nations will center on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared the defeat of ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to offer assistance and training services at Baghdad’s request.

World.title: Iraqi security forces mark Sovereignty Day as US forces leave
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security forces held large military parades on Wednesday to mark ‘Sovereignty Day,’ a national holiday that signifies the withdrawal of US and international coalition forces from Iraq.

The celebrations follow the expiration of the international coalition’s mission against ISIS on September 30, 2026. This event marks the conclusion of over two decades of foreign military involvement that began with the invasion in 2003.

The Iraqi government has announced a four-day national holiday from September 30 to October 3, 2026, known as sovereignty days.

Security forces and convoys carrying national flags paraded across major cities, flashing victory signs to commemorate the formal transfer of complete security authority to state institutions.

While foreign combat forces are completely withdrawn and bases totally evacuated, the US-Iraq relationship moves to a traditional bilateral security and intelligence collaboration centered on counter-terrorism.

While authorities and pro-Iran political forces celebrated the pullout as a victory for independence, some locals and analysts have voiced worries about potential security gaps, which might strengthen local militias or spark a comeback of ISIS remnants.

World.title: US announces military mission conclusion in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Department of War announced on Wednesday that the US military has completed its withdrawal from Iraq.

The department said in a statement that the United States and its partners in the international coalition officially concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq.

The orderly withdrawal of the international coalition forces and equipment from Erbil Air Base marks the conclusion of the military mission that defeated ISIS in Iraq, according to the statement.

The US War Department mentioned that it will continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to Iraqi partners.

The step marks the end of a 12-year campaign that saw ISIS eliminated as an organized military threat in Iraq and throughout the region. It also represents a shift from a wartime coalition mission to an Iraqi-led security operation backed by a more regular bilateral security partnership.

Iraqi security forces are expected to lead ongoing efforts to secure the country and ensure that ISIS remnants remain suppressed.

The terrorist group, which had seized vast swathes of territory, was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019; however, international coalition forces remained to continue fighting the group’s remnants.

Following the official US announcement, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi declared the start of a new phase defined as “Iraq’s sovereignty” following the international coalition’s withdrawal.

Baghdad and Washington agreed in 2024 to gradually end the international coalition’s mission, with forces subsequently withdrawing from bases across the country.

The Iraqi government sees that the withdrawal eliminates the justification for Iran-backed armed groups to keep their weapons.

World.title: Ocon to leave Haas at end of F1 season
World.content:
Sepang – Esteban Ocon will leave Haas at the end of the Formula One season, the racer and his team said Wednesday, following a difficult campaign for the Frenchman.

The 30-year-old joined the American outfit from Alpine ahead of the 2025 campaign, teaming up with British rookie Oliver Bearman.

Speculation about his departure had mounted in recent months as he complained about his car and hinted that his teammate was treated better.

Ocon plans to stay in the sport.

“My time with Haas F1 Team will come to an end at the end of the 2026 season,” Ocon posted on X.

“I leave this project with my head held high and proud of my performances in what were not always the easiest of circumstances for various reasons and factors outside of my control.

“My immediate focus is the next race weekend. I will continue to work hard with the team, maximise every opportunity, and keep extracting every bit of performance from the car.

“I am still motivated. I am still hungry. This is absolutely not the end of my Formula 1 career.”

Haas did not say who would replace him.

Ocon currently sits 16th in the drivers’ standings with seven points, three places behind Bearman.

The Frenchman has scored 12 points finishes across 39 grands prix with Haas, his best fifth place in China last year. He won the Hungary GP with Alpine in 2021.

His announcement came ahead of the rescheduled Bahrain GP, which will take place on Sunday in Malaysia due to the war in the Middle East.

World.title: Iraq enters new era as US forces leave after 23 years
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq opened a new chapter on Wednesday as US soldiers officially completed their departure from the nation, ending a military presence that began with the 2003 war that deposed Saddam Hussein and putting main responsibility for Iraq’s security in Iraqi hands.

U.S. Central Command said that American soldiers and equipment have left Erbil Air Base, the last major base for the US-led coalition in Iraq, thereby terminating Operation Inherent Resolve’s mission in the nation.

The departure marks the end of an unparalleled 23-year chapter in contemporary Iraqi history.

For an entire generation of Iraqis born after Saddam Hussein’s demise in 2003, some sort of American military presence has been an almost permanent fixture of the country’s political and security environment.

US soldiers invaded Iraq in March 2003 and deposed Saddam Hussein’s administration before staying in the nation for years of insurgency and sectarian warfare.

Most American soldiers left in 2011, but they returned in 2014 at Baghdad’s request after ISIS conquered Mosul and significant portions of northern and western Iraq.

That second intervention evolved into Operation Inherent Resolve, in which the US-led coalition provided air power, intelligence, training, and other assistance to Iraqi troops and the Peshmerga throughout the fight against ISIS.

Iraq claimed military victory over ISIS in 2017, and the coalition’s involvement evolved from heavy combat operations to advising and assisting Iraqi troops.

The last phase of the pullout began last year, following an agreement between Baghdad and Washington, and ended on September 30 with the departure from Erbil.

According to CENTCOM, the facility served as the coalition’s primary operating center, housing the majority of the approximately 1,500 American and coalition forces supporting counter-ISIS operations throughout the mission’s final stages.

CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said that Iraqi security forces, including the Peshmerga and other Kurdistan Region forces, now have the operational capabilities and leadership to handle threats to the nation without the coalition’s prior involvement.

For Baghdad, the milestone means more than just the end of the anti-ISIS coalition campaign.

It delegated the entire main responsibility for national security to Iraqi institutions at a time when the government is working to build state authority and prevent the country from becoming a battleground for competing foreign forces.

The departure does not mark the end of Iraq-US security cooperation. Washington and Baghdad are developing a bilateral military partnershipand they expect US training and intelligence collaborationed to continue under new terms.

Outside of Iraq, Operation Inherent Resolve continues.

The coalition task force has relocated its headquarters to Jordan, while US and coalition troops continue anti-ISIS operations in Syria.

The change presents major obstacles.

ISIS no longer controls Iraqi land, but militants and sleeper cells pose a security danger.

The Iraqi government must also deal with formidable armed groups that operate outside of traditional security organizations, as well as preserve peace in the absence of the country’s long-standing coalition backing.

The US pullout comes as Iraq strives to refocus its international alliances around commerce, oil, investment, and diplomacy rather than foreign military deployments, while balancing relations with Washington, its Arab neighbors, Turkey, and Iran.

For Iraq, September 30 represents a symbolic dividing line: 23 years after the US-led invasion ended Saddam Hussein’s dictatorship, the nation enters a time without the American-led military presence that molded most of its post-2003 history.

World.title: Iraq offers larger discounts on oil sales in October
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has significantly raised its discounts for term-contract buyers of October-loading crude oil.

These significant price reductions are intended to encourage buyers to accept delivery of cargoes directly from Iraq’s southern terminals, despite the serious geopolitical transit blockades and increasing shipping risks.

According to official marketing documents, price reductions have increased considerably in the past few months.

Basrah Medium is currently offered at a discount of $34.50 per barrel compared to market benchmarks, while Basrah Heavy is available at a $37.00 per barrel discount.

The current reductions are notably larger than the discounts offered in August and September, which were under $30 per barrel.

More than 90 percent of Iraq’s crude shipments were halted after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the military operations in the region. The discounts are an unprecedented concession to persuade purchasers to accept the security risks of sending oil tankers to the northern Arabian Gulf.

Attacks on vessels have dramatically slowed maritime activities. The steep discounts are designed to offset rising chartering expenses and war-risk insurance costs, thereby attracting major commodities merchants like Vitol and national players like the UAE’s ADNOC to buy Iraqi crude.

Since oil sales account for the vast bulk of Iraq’s national income, the Iraqi government has been compelled to aggressively increase discounting mechanisms to avoid production shutdowns and sustain state revenues.

World.title: Japan court rules human voice is protected in TikTok AI case
World.content:
Tokyo – A Tokyo court ruled Wednesday that the human voice is legally protected in Japan, after a high-profile anime voice actor took TikTok to court over videos he says feature an artificial intelligence clone of his “lustrous” baritone.

The decision marks a partial victory for Kenjiro Tsuda, known for his starring roles in mega-franchises including “Jujutsu Kaisen” and “Yu-Gi-Oh!”, although the court dismissed his request for removal of the videos.

“The unauthorised use of a performer’s voice… can be considered an infringement on publicity rights,” said presiding judge Aya Takahashi.

AI imitation is a growing concern among performers worldwide, and the threat has roiled Japan’s storied animation industry, whose voice actors are sometimes worshipped as much as their characters by fans.

The lawsuit is believed to be the country’s first seeking to defend an individual’s vocal identity against AI-generated copies.

It centred around a slew of TikTok videos narrated by a distinctively “deep” and “lustrous” voice that Tsuda, 55, said can only be his.

The platform, however, argued it is a “generic male voice” whose perceived similarity to Tsuda’s is subjective at best, according to court records accessed by AFP.

Wednesday’s verdict is seen as Japan’s first declaring that the human voice is protected under publicity rights if “the purpose of using that voice is exclusively to take advantage of its commercial appeal”, judge Takahashi said, describing a voice “as symbolic of one’s personality as portraits are”.

Publicity rights refer to the ability to control and profit from the use of aspects of one’s identity.

– ‘Balance’ –

Takahashi, however, said TikTok was “no longer obliged to delete” the videos in question because the anonymous user behind them had taken them down several months after the lawsuit began.

Tsuda’s lawyer Takashi Hirano told reporters that the ruling “ended up making both sides look victorious”.

The anonymous account, whose picture resembled a “Jujutsu Kaisen” character dubbed by Tsuda, combined images and seemingly AI-generated speech about urban legends, occult phenomena and conspiracy theories.

It at one point boasted more than 200,000 subscribers and would have brought in upwards of 500,000 yen ($3,200) in monthly revenue, the legal complaint argued.

Tsuda’s legal team argued the account only gained traction because “its dubious, sordid content was narrated by the attractive voice of a popular actor”.

TikTok told AFP in a statement that it will “respect the court’s judgement while considering what steps to take after scrutinising details” of its ruling.

“We will continue to sincerely work on the balance between technology development and rights protection,” the platform said.

Interest in the ruling has been high among voice actors in Japan, who worry AI mimicry of the tool of their trade will go a long way toward the decline of the storied industry.

An actor’s voice “is the result of years of rigorous training and apprenticeship” to hone talent, Yuko Sasaki, executive director of the Japan Actors Union, told AFP ahead of the ruling.

“It’s something we spend lots of time and money perfecting,” said Sasaki, a fellow voice actor, adding that “we support Tsuda wholeheartedly”.

Parallel to the lawsuit, Sasaki and other Japanese voice actors have launched a campaign, called “No More”, against using generative AI to mimic performers without permission.

“Our industry can be crushed” if “unbridled” AI voice cloning spreads on social media, actor Bin Shimada, who is part of the campaign group, had told AFP.

World.title: Protests against SIR, CEC: Is it time for Congress and INDIA bloc to take a leaf out of CJP's playbook?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, has announced a mega action plan to take forward its campaign against âvote choriâ and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The key stakeholders of the INDIA bloc met today in the national capital to chalk out a roadmap for nationwide protests against the Election Commissionâs âflawed and partisanâ approach.

The INDIA bloc's renewed offensive comes days after an Indian Express report citing internal differences within the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding the implementation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and modifications to voter registration processes. The opposition parties' meeting also comes in the backdrop of successful mobilisation programmed led by the Cockroach Janata Party against NEET paper leak, which brought the GenZ to the streets and forced the government to accept their demands.

After hours long deliberations, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge unveiled the oppositionâs blueprint for intensified demonstrations against ECâs âmalpracticesâ and shared details of how the INDIA bloc will stand up against electoral irregularities.

INDIA bloc's action blueprint

Here is what the INDIA bloc allies decided on their action plan against ECâs âpartisan approach and malpracticesâ

'Save Democracy March' in each district from October 2 to 8

On October 6, opposition MPsâ march to Election Commission headqaurters

Five rallies across India in October-November

Mega rally in Delhi on November 1 to explain â vote chori â by EC

â by EC Appeal to Supreme Court to expedite pending cases pertaining to SIR and other electoral malpractices

Detailed presentation before President Droupadi Murmu on âcompromisedâ electoral process

INDIA bloc's demands

Then there was also a list of 6 demands which the opposition parties announced. It included

Return to voting by ballot paper instead of EVMs

Pre-SIR electoral roll for all future elections

Due reasoning and effective appeal mechanism before any legitimate voter is removed from roll

Protection of eligible voters from exclusion caused by administrative failures, inadequate documentation or lack of awareness

Simple and accessible voter registration for our young citizens

Maintaining institutional accountability and an Election Commission that commands confidence across political spectrum

So far, so good. But the problem is that all these demands have already been raised by various opposition parties from time to time without any success.





We have heard several leaders in the past demanding a return to ballot paper. This has not happened and is unlikely to happen.

The fight over alleged discrepancies in the SIR process has been an ongoing one. We have seen

and other regional leaders raise the issue. But none of them have managed to sustain the momentum or stop the process. Even the courts have refused to back their allegations and have not stopped the SIR process.

Effective action plan?

Now, letâs focus on the action plan.

Protests at district level, march to Election Commissionâs office, rallies, appeal in Supreme Court - all make for good optics, but can they bring about enough pressure?

The Congress, which is leading the opposition block, has been consistent in raising these issues, but has failed to keep the momentum going. Rahul Gandhi has addressed several press conferences in the last two years leading the charge against the Election Commission and Gyanesh Kumar.

His yatra in Bihar ahead of assembly elections last year brought the issue to centre stage but once again the momentum did not sustain.

Clearly, the Congress and the other opposition parties need to think how to run a sustained campaign for mobilisation.

'Congress raises issues but fails to keep momentum going'

At the CWC meeting held on Tuesday, ahead of todayâs INDIA bloc meeting, Rahul Gandhi had claimed that revelations about the Election Commission were now coming out in the open because of the Congress.

During the two-and-a-half hour CWC meeting, Rahul pointed out that the Congress had been raising the "vote chori" issue strongly with facts and talked about irregularities in polls in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra but many were sceptical of it.

Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha claimed that EVM and voters' list "match-fixing" of polls was underway in the country and asserted that his party should not budge from the path of "virodh" (opposing) as well as "pratirodh" (resistance) against it from streets to Parliament.

Rahul Verma, political scientist and a Fellow at New Delhi-based think tank Centre for Policy Research, feels that the Congress needs to be persistent and have patience.

âOne of the reasons why the congress fails to do mobilization is that they raise important issues but are not persistent. They need to have patience. Congress has been talking about all the important issues but did not sit on a protest like the CJP,â Rahul Verma says.

âEven the CJP would not have thought of the success they eventually got. They continued sitting on protest even when there was little traction in their favour. Eventually, they managed to mobilise a lot of support and forced the government to concede to their demands,â Rahul Verma adds.

BJP targets opposition unity, attacks Rahul

If the INDIA bloc meeting was about showcasing opposition unity, well the purpose was at best half achieved. There were more questions on INDIA blocâs united presence than answers.

The BJP has aggressively highlighted the division within the opposition ranks. With several regional parties openly against the Congress, the BJP leaders have been quick to question Rahul Gandhiâs acceptance as the leader of the opposition block.

BJP national media incharge Ashish Usha Agarwal questioned Rahul Gandhiâs leadership of the INDIA bloc and said the outcomes of the INDIA bloc meeting on Wednesday were "zero vision, 100 per cent frustration.

The BJP claimed that the meeting was an advance excuse for poll defeats, with the leaders of the opposition grouping rejecting Rahul Gandhi's leadership.

"The INDI Alliance fell apart even before the meeting took place. The DMK did not attend the meeting. Akhilesh was busy elsewhere. The AAP had already declined," Union minister

said at a press conference at the BJP headquarters.

âWhy is this happening? It is because the INDI Alliance is simply not willing to accept Rahul Gandhi as its leader.

His leadership is not being accepted; that is why they are not even showing up," Chouhan said, contending that Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav would have come to attend the meeting if it was "really so important."

Chouhan claimed that the opposition INDIA bloc is crumbling. "No matter how many times they (Congress) try to re-launch Rahul Gandhi, the INDIA bloc does not consider him their leader," he said.

Clearly, the opposition needs to do things differently. When Mamata Banerjee said the opposition had taken these matters to the Election Commission and the Supreme Court and "knocked on every possible door," it was an admission of the fact that the old ways had failed.

The meeting today discussed the need for mobilisation on the ground by involving the civil society along with the political fight.

âThis is a fight against the RSS. Donât forget that. Civil society will have to be involved,â CPM general secretary MA Baby said during the meeting, according to sources who spoke to news agency PTI.

World.title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.

The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.

The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.

Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft.

He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.

During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.





The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.

Also read:

What happened inside the cockpit

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.

Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.

Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.

Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.

The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.

Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.

Later, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilots became involved in a physical altercation as the flight approached Israel.

âDuring the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot,â Netanyahu said in a video address.

âApparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.â Netanyahu added âalmost allâ passengers were Israelis, with some passengers and crew members breaking into the cockpit and subduing the attacker. âI spoke with one of the Israeli passengers. He told me that the plane went into a spin and began to dive.

He told me that somehow he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and together they neutralized the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraftâs systems,â Netanyahu said.

âAnother air crew that was on the plane entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane,â he added. He also praised those who intervened, saying: âI salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.

They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.â

Flydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely.

"Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.



The airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it would not impose a blanket ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but would also not permit fireworks throughout the day, saying a balance had to be struck between public health concerns and peopleâs sentiments.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale said the court would consider allowing firecrackers only during specified hours."We will make it very clear. World.title: Upanishads to Mahabharata: NCERT explains roots of national, SC mottos
World.content:
New Delhi: NCERTâs new Class IX social science textbook traces Indiaâs national motto, âSatyameva Jayateâ, to the Mundaka Upanishad and the Supreme Courtâs âYato Dharmastato Jayahâ to the Mahabharata, linking modern institutions to ancient texts.

The lesson presents these connections as expressions of the values and responsibilities that should guide governance in a democracy.

âUnderstanding Society: India and Beyondâ, Part 2, became available on Tuesday, September 29, nearly six months into the academic session. Part 1 came out in June. The six-chapter volume, which TOI reported on Wednesday, spans history, geography, political science and economics under the National Education Policy 2020 and National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023.

The chapter âGovernance and Public Policyâ translates the national motto as âTruth alone triumphsâ and the Supreme Courtâs motto as âWhere there is Dharma (righteous duty), there is victoryâ. It places these alongside the Sengol and Gandhiâs conception of Ram Rajya.

These references are ânot just symbolic or superficialâ, the book says, but express institutional values and the responsibility to ensure good governance.





It contrasts the national motto with âHeavenâs Light, Our Guideâ, used by the British Order of the Star of India. The chapter acknowledges that colonial institutions persisted after Independence, but says Indiaâs leaders framed the Constitution in keeping with Indiaâs own values and ideals.

The Sengol is described as a âcultural marker of rulership and good governanceâ, with a tradition dating back more than 1,000 years to the Cholas.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi installed it near the Lok Sabha Speakerâs chair in the new Parliament building on May 28, 2023.

The textbook recounts Jawaharlal Nehru receiving the sceptre from Tamil Naduâs Adheenam saints at Independence. Modi had described it as a symbol of the transfer of power. Congress disputed this in 2023, saying there was no documentary evidence that Mountbatten, C Rajagopalachari or Nehru had described it in those terms.

Gandhiâs Ram Rajya is presented as an ideal rooted in probity, transparency, compassion and welfare. The chapter links it to the Ramayana and 16th-century Ramcharitmanas, calling it âone of the best examples of good governance and a good collective lifeâ. It discusses Rajdharma as the rulerâs duty to protect people and uphold righteousness.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âGood governance was measured not only by the rulerâs authority but by the peace, prosperity, justice, and well-being in society,â it says.

The chapter also draws on Kautilyaâs Arthashastra to place the rulerâs happiness in the happiness of the people.

The chapter also identifies seven features of good governance: responsiveness, transparency, participation, rule of law, accountability, effectiveness and inclusiveness.

It stresses citizensâ rights, equality before the law and access to public services, while assigning responsibilities to government, citizens, the media, civil society and the private sector in achieving public welfare.

World.title: Keralam witnesses 7th-lowest southwest monsoon season
World.content:
The southwest monsoon has officially ended in Keralam with the State recording a 28% rainfall deficit—it received 1,446.5 mm of rain against the normal 2,018.6 mm— leaving large parts of the State facing drought-like conditions.

This is the 7th-lowest southwest monsoon rainfall recorded in the State since 1901 and the fourth-lowest since 2001.

Idukki and Wayanad, two districts that account for a major share of Keralam’s large reservoirs and hydropower generation capacity, were among the worst-affected, each receiving around 50% less rainfall than normal. According to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data, nearly 70% of the State remained significantly rain-deficient at the end of the season on September 30 with eight districts recording deficits of 20-53% and six districts reporting deficits ranging from 0% to 20%.

Northeast monsoon

The State is expecting that the northeast monsoon, which normally sets in by mid-October, may bring in some relief. However, the latest forecast indicates below-normal rainfall during the opening month of the season, with the emerging El Niño over the equatorial Pacific expected to influence the rainfall pattern. Southern Kerala and parts of central Kerala may receive normal or slightly above-normal rainfall during the northeast monsoon season as a whole, with more rain likely in November.

The defining feature of the southwest monsoon was its uneven distribution, marked by fewer rain-producing systems over the Bay of Bengal and prolonged dry spells punctuated by occasional high-intensity spells. The trend was clearly evident in July. Kerala had received only 853.8 mm of rain against the normal 1,301.7 mm by July 31, a deficit of 34%. However, heavy rainfall over four days, aided by a depression over central India, pushed the cumulative rainfall to 1,059.6 mm against the normal 1,374.9 mm for the period from June 1 to August 4, narrowing the deficit to 23%.

The tropical storm towards the end of July and a strong offshore trough during the first week of August triggered heavy rainfall in several parts of the State, including Idukki and Kottayam, while a devastating debris slip occurred in Wayanad. The spells, however, did little to offset the overall deficit, with several pockets continuing to face rainfall stress. For effective groundwater recharge, prolonged spells of low- to moderate-intensity rainfall are required. Such sustained rainfall was largely absent during the four-month monsoon season.

According to climate scientist V.K. Mini of the IMD, the extended-range forecast also does not indicate any major rainfall over Keralam during the next four weeks. However, central and southern Keralam are expected to receive normal to slightly above-normal rainfall in November and during the remaining part of the northeast monsoon season, which could help bridge the shortfall in October, she said.

Unlike the southwest monsoon, the northeast monsoon does not follow a regular pattern and is largely dependent on the formation and movement of depressions and storms over the Bay of Bengal. El Niño, which is currently at near-record levels, could further influence the rainfall pattern. Climate experts said the prevailing oceanic and atmospheric indicators are consistent with a strong El Niño, which could favour the formation of more weather systems over the Bay of Bengal or Arabian Sea, raising hopes of intense spells interspersed with prolonged dry periods.

World.title: INDIA bloc to launch nationwide campaign against CEC, SIR from October 2
World.content:
The INDIA bloc on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) announced a nationwide campaign beginning Friday (October 2, 2026) with a graded agitation plan that includes protest marches at district headquarters, public meetings, a march to the Election Commission and a joint appeal to the Chief Justice for expedited hearings in cases related to the SIR and alleged electoral “malpractices”.

The decisions were taken after a three-and-a-half-hour meeting attended by 33 leaders from 19 political parties. Independent MP and senior Supreme Court lawyer Kapil Sibal also participated.

Mr. Sibal recommended that the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, should be legally challenged. The legislation states that “notwithstanding other laws, no court could entertain or continue civil or criminal proceedings against a person who was or had been CEC/EC for an act, thing, or word committed, done, or spoken while discharging official duty or function,” extending a blanket immunity to the CEC. In view of this, he suggested that legal action be taken against other Election Commission officials such as Seema Khanna, Director General (IT) at ECI, who have been instrumental in bringing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Most leaders backed the proposal.

There was, however, apprehension among some leaders about the Supreme Court’s stance. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and former Maharashtra Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray, who joined the meeting virtually, cited the Chief Justice of India’s observation while declining an early hearing of pleas related to the SIR in West Bengal. The CJI had observed, “These are only by-elections.”

There was no direct reference to involving the Cockroach Janata Party. However, leaders agreed that the bloc should engage with civil society and secular parties outside the INDIA alliance.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the leaders had agreed to fight together. “With unanimity, everyone vowed to fight together,” he said at a press conference attended by top INDIA bloc leaders.

Mr. Kharge alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were making the Election Commission function like a “puppet”. “These people are only winning elections by stealing votes. When our people oppose this, they are harassed,” he said. He alleged that the BJP was winning elections because they were “stolen”.

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi alleged that democratic institutions were under attack from the BJP, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. “We are not going to take it lying down,” he said, adding, “We are going to ensure this personal commitment of all INDIA leaders—people who have destroyed Indian democracy are punished, no matter how senior they are and who they are. Indian democracy is bigger than every single person in this country.”

“Save Democracy” marches

The bloc will hold “Save Democracy” marches in every district between October 2 and 8. The proposal, made by CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, initially faced resistance from some leaders citing State-specific political concerns. Senior Congress leaders, including Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, eventually backed it.

On October 6, Opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission headquarters. Mr. Kharge said some leaders had wanted to hold the march on Wednesday itself, though others suggested a later date to allow all MPs to participate.

The leaders will also seek an appointment with the President to brief her on the “constitutional hurdles being created by the government”. During the meeting, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expressed concern that such requests were often declined or the President’s office limited the size of the delegation.

The INDIA bloc will also hold five rallies across the country during October and November, including one in Delhi on November 1.

DMK among absentees

Notable absentees included the DMK, which has refused to share a stage with Congress after the latter switched its support to the TVK following the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav skipped the meeting because of Rajya Sabha polls in his State. JMM chief and Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren joined the meeting virtually.

The parties represented at the meeting included the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), RJD, CPI(M), CPI, National Conference, PDP, JMM, CPI(ML), IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.

World.title: Days after India-Pakistan sparring at UN, senior Indian official visits Islamabad for SCO planning meet
World.content:
Pakistan announced that it would host the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in August 2027, as an Indian delegation led by a senior MEA official attended a preparatory meeting in Islamabad—the first such official Indian visit to Pakistan since Operation Sindoor last year.

The three-day meeting of SCO National Coordinators that began on Monday (September 29, 2026) comes days after India and Pakistan sparred with each other over the issue of terrorism and the Kashmir dispute at the UN General Assembly (UNGA). External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif traded allegations in their national addresses, while Indian and Pakistani diplomats exercised their rights of reply to the speeches on the global stage last week.

On Tuesday (September 29, 2026), India also rejected Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s reference to Kashmir in his UNGA speech.

The participation of Joint Secretary (Multilaterals and Economic Relations) Alok Dimri marked a higher level of Indian representation than at the past few meetings held under Pakistan’s Chairpersonship of the SCO this year. In mid-September, a meeting of SCO-Regional Anti-Terror Structure in Islamabad was attended by the Indian Charge d’affaires in Pakistan Satyapal Pandey, without a delegation from India.

In a statement, the Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Pakistan’s SCO Chairship would promote the theme of “Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity,” for 2026-207.

“The [National Coordinator] meeting marks an important initial engagement under Pakistan’s Chairmanship and would contribute to preparations for various high-level engagements and activities to be undertaken during the Chairmanship, including the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State to be hosted by Pakistan in August 2027,” the MoFA statement issued in Islamabad said.

Indian officials made it clear that the SCO coordinators’ meet was being held in a multilateral format and hence had no particular significance for India-Pakistan bilateral ties. However, the participation does leave the path open to higher-level attendance at the Ministerial-level events and the Heads of Council meet, to which Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been invited. Thus far, New Delhi has avoided the leaders’ meetings in both Delhi and Islamabad.

In 2023, PM Modi hosted the SCO Heads of Council Summit virtually, while Mr. Jaishankar hosted Pakistani Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto in person for the SCO Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Goa. In 2024, Mr. Jaishankar travelled to Islamabad to attend the SCO Heads of Government meeting as well. The MEA has thus far declined to comment on whether Mr. Modi would travel to Pakistan next year, but has not ruled it out either.

At a briefing on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal brushed aside a question about whether India would oppose the induction of Turkiye to the 10-nation SCO, which currently comprises China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus and four Central Asian States- Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

Turkish President Erdogan had told journalists earlier this month that Türkiye would pursue a “higher level” of engagement with the SCO than its observer status, indicating he could ask for full membership next year, particularly given close ties and the military pact with SCO host Pakistan.

“As and when any issue of membership comes it is for [SCO] members to collectively decide as to how to go forward on that,” Mr. Jaiswal said. He also criticised Mr. Erdogan for referring to Kashmir in his UNGA speech last week, when he called for a resolution of all South Asian disputes “including Kashmir”.

“India rejects the unwarranted references to India and the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir made by the President of Türkiye during his address to the UN General Assembly. This is a matter, as you would understand, pertaining to India’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, and no external party has any locus standi on this issue,” Mr. Jaiswal said on Tuesday.

Senior Indian official visits Islamabad for SCO planning meet

World.title: Farmers demand Madurai district be declared drought-hit
World.content:
Farmers in Madurai district demanded that the district be declared drought-hit. They complained that agricultural activities had been affected due to the failure to release water from the Vaigai dam, at the farmers’ grievance redress meeting held at the Madurai Collectorate on Wednesday.

At the meeting presided over by Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna, the farmers urged the authorities to provide appropriate compensation for the crop loss.

Pointing to the long-pending demand, the farmers urged the authorities to take steps to restart the National Cooperative Sugar Mills in Alanganallur. Restarting the sugar mill would benefit sugarcane farmers of Madurai and the neighbouring districts, the farmers said.

The farmers opposed the proposed rough stone and gravel quarry in Thenpazhanji. They complained that water channels in the area had been encroached upon. This affected agricultural activities in the region. They said the people were suffering from health issues due to existing quarrying operations. Heavy trucks carrying tonnes of minerals posed a threat to the people and the roads in the area.

A section of farmers said a retaining wall was constructed to prevent the discharge of sewage into a water canal that connected to the Madakulam tank. This wall had been breached in Achampathu. Farmers urged the authorities to take necessary steps to prevent the discharge of sewage into the tank. A similar complaint had been raised earlier. However, no action had been taken, the farmers complained.

Farmers also raised complaints with regard to delayed crop insurance payments, particularly for maize. Issues pertaining to crop loan waiver were also raised during the meeting. They said workers under the MGNREGA scheme could also be employed for agricultural work.

Some of the other issues raised at the meeting were with regard to the removal of Seemai Karuvelam (Prosopis juliflora). They complained that wild animals were destroying crops and urged the authorities to take necessary steps to protect the livelihood of the farmers.

World.title: All four LeT commanders active in J&K since 2022 now dead, says Home Ministry
World.content:
The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) said that with the killing of a Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander in Jammu and Kashmir’s Budgam district in an operation that started on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), all four senior LeT commanders who had been operating in the Union Territory since 2022 are dead.

According to the MHA, the LeT commander, identified by the Army as Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, was killed in an intelligence-led joint operation by security forces at Gurwatkalan in the Khansahib area of Budgam district. The Ministry said security agencies had been pursuing him for a long time and recently put in place a specific multi-agency plan for his “neutralisation” after receiving technical and human intelligence inputs regarding his movements and presence.

The MHA described Moosa’s killing as a major blow to the LeT ecosystem in Jammu and Kashmir. It said that with his death, the entire four-member group of senior LeT commanders active in J&K since 2022 has been dismantled.

The Ministry said the group was responsible for several major attacks, including the Halan attack in August 2023, the Kandi attack in May 2023, the DKG attack in December 2023, the Shahsitar attack in May 2024, the Shiv Khori attack in June 2024, the Gagangir attack in October 2024, the Bootapathri attack in October 2024, and the Baisaran attack in April 2025.

The others

Suleman, one of these four commanders, was involved in the terror attack at the Baisaran meadow of Pahalgam on April 22, 2025, when 25 tourists and a local man were killed. Suleman was later killed during Operation Mahadev, along with two other Pakistani terrorists, on July 28, 2025.

Apart from Moosa and Suleman, two other LeT commanders who operated in J&K were also killed in separate operations, the MHA said. Junaid Bhat was killed in an encounter at Dachigam on December 3, 2024, and Yasir was killed in Operation Asdhar on September 4, 2026.

The Ministry said the operation against Moosa was part of a sustained counter-terrorism campaign and reflected the close coordination among the Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Indian Army and the Central Armed Police Forces.

“Over the past few years, all security agencies have been conducting counter-terrorism operations in close coordination, yielding positive results,” the MHA said.

World.title: ‘Swachha Unnathi’ programme held for sanitation workers in Bantwal taluk
World.content:
Mangala Resource Management Pvt. Ltd., which operates several material recovery facilities (MRFs) in Dakshina Kannada, organised the ‘Swachha Unnathi’ programme for sanitation workers from various gram panchayats in Bantwal taluk at its Narikombu MRF on Wednesday, September 30.

The programme saw the distribution of accident health insurance cover worth ₹5 lakh to over 80 sanitation workers; distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including safety shoes, hand gloves and masks; health check-ups for participating workers; a fire safety demonstration and emergency response training by the Fire and Emergency Services Department; and a snakebite awareness and emergency response session by snake expert Snake Kiran.

Speaking on the occasion, Zilla Panchayat Deputy Secretary Jayalakshmi Rayakoda said the contribution of self-help groups, sanitation workers and Mangala Resource Management, which manages various integrated solid waste management facilities in the district, had played a significant role in bringing national recognition to Dakshina Kannada.

Senior Fire Officer Harish Kumar and his team conducted a practical demonstration and training session on handling emergency situations during fire accidents and the safety measures to be followed.

Mr. Kiran provided information on snakes and other reptiles and explained the immediate steps to be taken in the event of a snakebite, creating greater awareness among sanitation workers about emergency response and personal safety.

Sachin Kumar, Executive Officer, Bantwal Taluk Panchayat; Ashok Rai of the District Health Department; Dilraj Alva, Director, Mangala Resource Management; and Sachin Shetty were present.

World.title: ‘A morning by the river’ recalls Phalguni’s lost traditions
World.content:
The Mangaluru Chapter of the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) organised a special boat-based programme, ‘A morning by the river’, on Sunday to mark World Rivers Day.

The programme, held on the Phalguni (Gurupura) River, began at the Sultan Bathery ferry point and brought together nature lovers, artists and citizens to reflect on the river’s ecological, historical and cultural significance. The programme also highlighted the gradual loss of traditional knowledge associated with the Gurupura River, including the seasonal formation of temporary islands that once supported the livelihoods of traditional fishermen.

Introducing the programme, INTACH Mangaluru Chapter convener Subhas Chandra Basu said rivers were an important part of the region’s heritage. “The Gurupura River was crucial to the development of Mangaluru from ancient times. Ports and forts were built along its banks, and water transport was an essential means of moving people and goods. Unfortunately, the city’s development today does not adequately take the river into consideration. It is becoming a dumping ground for the city’s waste,” he said.

Temporary islands

Social activist and environmentalist Yatish Baikampady said the river was once an important means of transport, with people from the Ghats travelling downstream by boat to coastal towns. He recalled a little-known phenomenon associated with the river during the monsoon. Natural debris carried by the river would accumulate at certain places to form temporary islands, locally known as palke, he said.

“These temporary islands were a boon to traditional fishermen. Fish would breed around them, providing an important source of livelihood during the monsoon when fishermen could not venture into the sea. Today, due to dams and other interventions, this system has disappeared,” he added.

Chartered accountant Giridhar Kamath recalled a time when the river was closely integrated into everyday life, with children swimming and bathing in its waters. He noted that the region had historically been blessed with abundant water and that the rivers also served as natural barriers against forces from the sea. “People here knew how to live with floods. But the floods we experience today are largely the result of human intervention,” he said.

The one-and-a-half-hour boat journey offered participants an opportunity to observe the river and its banks while reflecting on the communities and landscapes connected to it. The programme also highlighted the importance of preserving not just the physical river but also the traditional knowledge, memories and ways of life that have evolved around it.

World.title: ‘Stealing’ of candidates by ‘clean’ force caused byelection, alleges Kanimozhi
World.content:
DMK parliamentary party leader Kanimozhi on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) alleged the byelections to the Maduranthagam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies had been necessitated by the “stealing of candidates by those [TVK] who had proclaimed themselves a clean force”.

“By its actions, the ‘clean’ force has become a ‘stealing’ force,” she said while campaigning for party candidate I. Paranthamen in the Maduranthagam constituency.

She said the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) should have stopped with forming the government after “appropriating” MLAs from political parties that were part of the DMK alliance. “But it has stolen people’s representatives and caused a by-election,” she said in an apparent reference to the resignation of AIADMK MLAs, who later joined the TVK and have entered the fray on its ticket now.

Ms. Kanimozhi said DMK president M.K. Stalin had fielded Mr. Paranthamen, who would fight for and defend the Dravidian ideology and, more importantly, remain with the party after his election and not resort to defection.

“You took pity on the candidate and voted for her in the election. But she defected to the ruling party. If you vote for the AIADMK again, there may be another by-election,” she said. She added that even “oppressive measures” and arrests had not forced DMK leaders to change sides.

Ms. Kanimozhi said she would prefer to address Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay as “Sweet Bro” and accused him of campaigning among children and asking them to persuade their parents to vote for him.

“There is a case against him for instigating children to persuade their parents to vote for him. The Chief Minister, who campaigned among children, sought to cover up the death of a girl in Vandalur as it would affect his campaign in Madurantakam,” she alleged.

She claimed another girl had also been sexually assaulted and alleged that the Chief Minister had not spoken about the incident. “But our leader Stalin spoke to the parents of the girl and promised all help,” she said.

Ms. Kanimozhi said that though the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) had described Tamil Nadu as a safe State for women, the State had witnessed 500 crimes, including 300 sexual assaults against women and children, 200 murders, eight custodial deaths and 10 honour killings in the four months since the TVK came to power.

World.title: Pakistan will be there to defend Saudi Arabia in any conflict: Khawaja Asif
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said that Pakistan was “there to help” Saudi Arabia in any conflict.

“We are there to help Saudi Arabia in any conflict, whether it is coming from the Houthis or a country or any other outfit that threatens Saudi Arabia’s security. We will be there to defend them,” he said in a video clip, which appeared to be excerpted from a longer interview, published by Al Jazeera.

His remarks come amid fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government that has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

Against this backdrop, Pakistan, which has signed two defence agreements with Riyadh, has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

On Sept 18, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security was “unconditional”.

Earlier, Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated.

In his latest remarks, Asif said “there is no absolutely no doubt in our mind that Houthis are committing aggression against Saudi Arabia”.

He added that Pakistan was bound an arrangement to defend Saudi Arabia.

And “when I say that we are bound by this arrangement to defend Saudi Arabia, that means that whatever means are available at our disposal, they will be available to Saudi Arabia also”.

Here, the use of “arrangement” was apparently a reference to one of the defence pacts Pakistan has signed with Riyadh.

The first one, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA), was signed in Sept 2025, under which the two countries pledged that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

The two countries are also a party to the Makkah Defence Alliance, which also includes Turkiye. The pact was signed on August 7 and provides that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all.

The military leadership of the three countries also held a meeting last week in Riyadh. During the meeting, the military leaders expressed a shared determination to “immediately translate” their commitments under the Makkah Defence Alliance into effective military cooperation.

In his interview to Al Jazeera, Asif also said Houthis were “enemies of Saudi Arabia, and any enemy of Saudi Arabia is an enemy of Pakistan That should we very clear”.

“And Iranians are not accepting them (Houthis) as their proxy.

“Some of these proxies have become rogue. I don’t have to go into history, I can give you multiple examples of that. Some countries — A, B or C — they launch a proxy, and then the proxy has its own way of multiplying and then becoming a rogue sort of entity,” he added.

World.title: 3 Pakistanis among 5 crew lost during operation to recover ship hijacked by Somali pirates, FO confirms
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Wednesday expressed condolences over the death of three Pakistani nationals during an operation to recover the MT Honour 25 oil tanker, which had been hijacked by Somali pirates in April.

The maritime police force of semi-autonomous Puntland said on Tuesday that it had recovered the MT Honour 25 in an operation. The Palau-flagged oil tanker had 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis.

In a statement on Wednesday, FO said: “Pakistan is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of five crew members during the operation to recover the hijacked vessel, MT Honour 25, off the coast of Somalia.

“Among those who lost their lives are three Pakistani nationals: Rafiullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari.”

The FO added that four crew members were also injured, including three Pakistani nationals. “The injured have been taken to a nearby hospital and are receiving medical care,” it added.

The surviving crew members of MT Honour 25 “have been brought safely ashore at Bandar Beyla”, a town in Puntland, according to FO.

“Pakistan’s team at the Embassy in Djibouti is proceeding to Bandar Beyla to assist the Pakistani nationals.”

The FO said it remains in close contact with the Somali authorities and other concerned stakeholders through its missions and relevant authorities.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure proper medical care for the injured, facilitate the transportation of the mortal remains of the deceased, and ensure the safe return of the surviving Pakistani crew members,” the statement read.

On Tuesday, “The naval and ground units of the Puntland Maritime Police Force conducted a planned operation in the Dharin-Bar area of Bandar Beyla district,” Puntland maritime police said in its initial statement.

In another late-night statement, it announced that the operation had concluded and the recovered vessel was “now safe and under the Puntland government’s control”, adding that 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue.

“Before the operation begun, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew. Among those killed were three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar and one from India,” it said.

After the MT Honour 25’s hijacking in April, months had passed with no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages.

The hostages were said to be victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it was not clearly established who owned the ship — the man previously thought to be an owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them.

Since its hijacking, the crew had made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they had run out of clean water, food and medicine. Meanwhile, their families launched an international appeal, calling on foreign governments, the United Nations (UN) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to take coordinated action to help secure the release of their loved ones.

For its part, the FO maintained that it remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors.

Last month, in a meeting with the International Maritime Organisation’s (IMO) head, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar pressed for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of the Pakistani sailors.

Somali piracy has seen a resurgence, with at least 15 attacks since April, the highest since 2013.

World.title: Israel-bound plane rerouted to Saudi Arabia; pilots wounded in reported fight
World.content:
Two pilots were wounded after they reportedly fought on board the plane they were flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, and which was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.

The flydubai plane landed in Tabuk at 9:45 am (11:45am PKT) and its “captain and copilot were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital”, a statement from the company operating the airport said.

The low-cost carrier had earlier said flight FZ 1073 “experienced an incident while en route”. “The aircraft has landed safely in Tabuk Airport (TUU) and all passengers are safe and accounted for.”

Several Israeli media outlets reported that a fight had broken out between the plane’s pilots, reportedly causing a distress signal to be activated.

Israeli media also reported that two other pilots were flying on the plane as passengers, and that they had taken over the controls to carry out the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Neither the airline nor authorities of the countries involved provided details on what happened on board or on the pilots’ nationalities, but some Israeli media said one was Omani and the other Emirati.

According to data from the Flightradar website, the aircraft suddenly lost altitude during the flight, dropping from nearly 34,000 feet at 05:21am GMT to less than 17,000 feet at 05:22am GMT (10:22am PKT).

The flight from Dubai diverted over Jordanian airspace towards Saudi Arabia, transmitting a general emergency signal before transmitting another emergency signal that indicates a possible unlawful interference several minutes later, according to flight tracking website Flightradar24.

The Boeing 737 plane then again transmitted the general emergency signal before landing at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, the website said.

There were 180 Israelis on board the plane, according to Israel’s far-right national security minister Ben Gvir, who claimed the incident involved a “terrorist”.

‘Going down very fast’

An AFP correspondent in Tabuk, where the plane landed, saw heavy security near the airport, with several police vehicles and an ambulance parked at the terminal. Access to the terminal remained open.

At Ben Gurion airport, families gathered to await the return of their loved ones.

Yasmin Abukasis, mother of passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon, told AFP that her daughter called her from Saudi Arabia: “She said one pilot tried to kill the other pilot with a knife. They heard shouting”.

Another passenger went to the cockpit “and saw a lot of blood. She started screaming ‘come help’ and some people went in and caught the guy”, she added.

“All the while, the plane started going down very fast. People thought they were going to die.”

She added that two other pilots in the back later took over the controls.

Israeli media, citing anonymous sources, reported that the passengers on board had stepped in to separate the two pilots during their altercation, publishing photos of a passenger with a bloodied T-shirt.

Channel 12 reported that authorities were investigating whether or not one of the pilots had attempted a possible suicide by trying to crash the plane, with the other pilot apparently intervening to prevent the crash.

In a video from inside the plane that was reposted by Israeli social media users, one passenger, blood dripping from an open wound on his head, pleaded for assistance and said they were descending into Saudi Arabia, with which Israel has no diplomatic relations.

“We are here during an attack on the plane. We just subdued the terrorists and are preparing to land,” the man said in Hebrew.

Israeli jets scrambled

Israel’s Kan public broadcaster, Times of Israel and Channel 12 reported that the Israeli military had scrambled fighter jets after fears of a possible hijacking — with the hypothesis later dismissed.

Times of Israel, citing Kan, said the Mossad intelligence agency, Shin Bet and the Israeli military were involved in the investigation into the incident.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alleged that one of the pilots had planned to crash the plane and kill its mostly Israeli passengers, who stopped a “major disaster”.

“During the flight, as they approached the country, one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot, and apparently tried to crash the plane with everyone on board,” Netanyahu said in a video message, calling the passengers “heroes” who “prevented a major disaster”.

Netanyahu’s office earlier said he had held consultations on the matter and was “monitoring developments”.

“The incident is under control, and all measures are currently being deployed in order to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel,” a statement said.

Meir Zohar, the father of passenger Ido Zohar, told AFP his son had told him by text message that he was well, but that he had no other news.

“He told us that everything is okay, he didn’t tell me that much.”

Flydubai operates daily flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route that is popular among Israeli nationals.

It is not the first time a flight between Israel and the UAE has landed in Saudi Arabia. A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Riyadh in September 2025 due to a medical emergency, Israeli media reported at the time.

World.title: Tarar warns India's unilateral actions on IWT may have implications for water governance globally
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Wednesday warned that India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance could have implications for global transboundary water governance, urging the international community to take note of the “wider precedent”.

Tarar made the remarks while addressing a ceremony organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad to launch a report on the IWT issue.

Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025.

Following India’s move, Pakistan termed any attempt to suspend its water share an “act of war”, noting the IWT had no provision for unilateral suspension. It later argued that Delhi’s action was a violation of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties.

“We are a peaceful nation, but we cannot allow India to weaponise water because it is the basic right of the 240 million people of Pakistan,” Tarar said, drawing attention to the “wider precedent involved”.

“If a state can unilaterally put a binding international water treaty in abeyance despite established dispute resolution mechanisms, the implications extend to transboundary water governance across the world,” Tarar warned, adding that it may have implications for countries sharing water under similar frameworks.

Tarar reiterated that Pakistan will continue to engage the international community and defend the country’s vital national interests.

At the outset of his address, Tarar said, “I take great pride in the fact that wherever we go, we say we are the people of the Indus Valley [..] we identify ourselves with the Indus waters.”

He noted that when the treaty was signed, the signatories “did not envisage that there would come a time a few decades down the line when conditions in India would deteriorate so much that they would be legally ignorant, morally bankrupt and devoid of ethics”.

Tarar held that the IWT was legally binding upon both parties. “It contains stipulations that this legal instrument cannot be unilaterally revoked, rescinded, or altered,” Tarar added.

He further stated that the treaty cannot be “unilaterally altered, revoked, rescinded or held in abeyance, for that matter, but even if there is a dispute, both the parties have to adhere to the terms and conditions of the treaty”.

At this, Tarar recalled an August ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), saying, “The court upheld Pakistan’s stance, giving legitimacy and strength to the argument that there cannot be a unilateral attempt to change the status of this treaty”.

In its August order, the PCA had backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement.

Tarar further stated that Pakistan had approached the issue diplomatically: “We have engaged the international community and presented our point of view — legal and diplomatic — and as a nation-state, which respected the rights of others, in a manner that has been most effective.”

At this, the information minister recalled Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s speech at the recent United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).

“PM Shehbaz said that the IWT is the lifeblood of our people and our region, and any attempt to usurp this right be treated as an act of war,” Tarar said.

Tarar stated that Pakistan’s position on the IWT remained “absolutely clear,” adding that the treaty was an “instrument of peace and stability for the region”.

He noted that India had justified its actions with “alleged cross-border terrorism”; however, he went on to highlight sacrifices made by Pakistan in the fight against terrorism.

“We have economic losses of over $50bn over the past many decades,” Tarar said.

He continued: “When one Pakistani citizen lays down their life, yes, it is to make Pakistan safe, but it also makes the world a safer place.”

Tarar, drawing a contrast with neighbouring India, said, “India has illegally tried to alter the status of the IWT and has been accused at the international level of transnational aggression”.

Shifting his attention back to the IWT, Tarar said India’s actions were “highly condemnable” and unjustifiable at a “legal, diplomatic, and moral level”.

The IWT allocates the eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — to India, while the western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab — are largely allocated to Pakistan. The 1960 water-sharing agreement has also established mechanisms for data-sharing and dispute resolution.

World.title: FBR dismisses 'fake' notification on extension of income tax filing deadline
World.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) on Wednesday refuted a notification circulating in the media claiming that it had extended its deadline to file income tax returns for 2026, terming it “fake”.

“No such circular has been issued by the FBR,” the board’s spokesperson said on X.

A notification circulating on social media on Wednesday claimed that the deadline had been extended until Oct 15, as it had been last year.

It stated that the extension was decided on “in view of the requests from various trade bodies, taxpayers and tax bar associations”.

However, the FBR clarified that the deadline for income tax return submission for the tax year 2026 (TY26) remains Sept 30.

Trade bodies and professionals have sought an extension of the deadline, citing delays in the issuance of return forms and heavy online traffic as major hurdles in timely filing.

Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry President Atif Ikram Sheikh had also formally urged the government to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns to Oct 31 to facilitate trade, industry, and other tax filers.

The Karachi Tax Bar Association (KTBA) had submitted a five-page letter to the Member Inland Revenue (operations), highlighting several issues, including delays in the issuance of draft notifications and persistent technical glitches in the IRIS portal, which hinder the smooth filing of tax returns.

In the previous cycle, the FBR reported an overwhelming response, with overall tax return filings rising from 3.553 million in TY25 to 5.181m in TY26 until Sept 29 — an increase of 45.8 per cent.

The statutory deadline for filing tax returns is Sept 30 each year. However, historically, the date has been extended two to three times, often until the end of October.

In recent years, extensions were granted with only minor penalties, but the latest budget has substantially increased these charges, making compliance costlier for late filers.

Under the Finance Act 2026-27, the penalty for returning to the active taxpayers list (ATL) has been raised fivefold for companies to Rs100,000 from Rs20,000. It was also increased from Rs10,000 to Rs50,000 for associations of persons, and from Rs1,000 to Rs25,000 for individuals.

Last year, the FBR extended the deadline twice from Sept 30 to Oct 15 and subsequently to Oct 31 despite earlier saying it would not do so. These extensions were granted in response to requests made by various trade bodies, tax bar associations, and the general public.

World.title: Lahore to celebrate 10-day Basant festival from Jan 29 to Feb 7 next year
World.content:
LAHORE: The Punjab capital will celebrate Basant for 10 days from January 29 to February 7 next year, with a one-day break on Feb 5 for Kashmir Day, under a schedule approved by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Wednesday.

Lahore celebrated the Basant festival earlier this year from Feb 6 to 8 after an 18-year hiatus.

The festival was banned in 2007 because of an increasing number of deaths and serious injuries caused by sharp strings, particularly to motorcyclists and pillion riders, as well as by celebratory gunfire.

During a meeting, the chief minister directed the authorities to make arrangements for the 10-day celebration, according to a statement released by the government.

She described the festival as a gift for the people of Lahore to mark the arrival of 2027 and as a means of promoting Punjab’s cultural heritage and the historic traditions of the provincial capital.

Under the schedule approved by the chief minister, Basant festivities will begin on Jan 29 and continue until Feb 7. However, celebrations will remain suspended on Feb 5 to observe Kashmir Day.

“Ten-day Basant will promote Punjab’s cultural colours and Lahore’s centuries-old traditions across the world,” CM Maryam was quoted as saying.

According to the statement, the chief minister directed the administration to ensure better arrangements for public safety and convenience than those made during the previous festival.

She also appealed to citizens to celebrate responsibly, saying the authorities and the public should set a new example through a sense of duty, responsibility and commitment to protecting human lives.

CM Maryam directed the relevant departments to begin preparations well in advance and ensure that the extended festivities did not compromise public safety, the statement said.

She stressed that the success of the 10-day event would depend on strict adherence to safety regulations and responsible behaviour by citizens.

“The chief minister said Lahore’s cultural identity and traditions should be promoted while ensuring that celebrations remained safe and convenient for residents and visitors,” the statement concluded.

In August, CM Maryam announced that the festival would be held from Mar 12 to 14, 2027. However, in the latest announcement, the government has revised the schedule.

World.title: Shark stranded in South Korean canal draws 600,000 visitors as rescue bid fails
World.content:
A shark stranded in a canal in the South Korean port of Busan has become the ​country’s latest wildlife sensation, with the city saying about 600,000 ‌people have flocked to see it over the past two weeks.

The 3.5-metre shark was first spotted in a narrow waterway in North Port on September 18.
