World.title: US appeals court pauses execution of Tennessee killer Christa Pike
World.content:
The US state of Tennessee's first execution of a woman in at least 200 years has been halted by an appeals court just an hour before it was set to begin, after a federal appeals court sought a review of case details.

Christa Gail Pike was set to be executed by legal injection on Wednesday morning, local time, for a murder she committed at age 18.

Pike, now 50, and her boyfriend were convicted of stabbing and beating 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, their classmate at a job training facility in Knoxville in 1995.

But the federal appeals court is now seeking to review whether her allegations of childhood sexual abuse and rape were fully considered at her sentencing.

The case garnered widespread attention at the time in part because a pentagram that was carved on Slemmer's body and other elements of the crime stoked fears of Satan worship during the "satanic panic" of the 1980s and 1990s.

Colleen Slemmer was murdered in 1995 in Tennessee. (May Martinez via AP)

It was not immediately clear if Tennessee's attorney general was appealing the decision, or how long the execution might be delayed.

A phone message and email were left with a spokesperson for the attorney general's office seeking comment.

As the execution date drew near, it renewed debate over the death penalty for young offenders.

Pike does not deny committing the killing, but her supporters argue the state should consider Pike's age at the time, mental illness and a history of severe sexual abuse that included being raped from the time she was a toddler.

The execution has sparked public interest and protests. (AP: George Walker IV)

Assistant Federal Defender Stephen Ferrell said Pike's death sentence is an outlier because other 18-year-olds sentenced to death in Tennessee have had their sentences vacated.

The US Supreme Court on Tuesday denied a request from Pike's attorneys to halt the execution. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee on Monday denied Pike clemency.

"I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realise the gravity of what I'd done," Pike said in a statement included in her clemency petition.

Slemmer's mother wants the lethal injection to go forward, saying she has waited decades to see Pike's sentence carried out.

"Every time I think about it, I think about Colleen feeling that pain and trying to get up and run," May Martinez said in a telephone interview.

AP

World.title: Breaking: 'Strong indications' Iran involved in RAF airbase incident, UK prime minister says
World.content:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham says there are "strong indications" Iran played a role in an incident near a Royal Air Force Base in England.

Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offences over the incident, which unfolded on Sunday morning, local time. They were later released on bail.

In an interview with the BBC, Mr Burnham said UK authorities "believe Iran to have played a part" in the plot.

"There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened on the weekend," Mr Burnham said.

"But of course, it remains an ongoing, complex and serious police investigation, and of course we are working closely with our colleagues in the United States of America."

Iran has previously denied involvement.

RAF Fairford is located west of London and has been used by US aircraft in military operations against Iran in recent months.

World.title: Israel to 'ramp up' aviation security after pilot 'tries to crash plane'
World.content:
Israel's Prime Minister says a commercial flight with 174 people on board bound for Tel Aviv had to divert to Saudi Arabia after one pilot stabbed the other and "apparently tried to crash the plane".

Warning: This article contains graphic images.

The Boeing 737 operated by flydubai — a sister airline of Emirates — took off from Dubai International Airport in the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday morning, local time.

Tabuk Airport, in north-west Saudi Arabia, said its air-traffic control received a distress call from the flight FZ1073 at 8:44am (3:44pm AEST). It landed there safely around an hour later.

In a video address released by his office on Wednesday, Israel's PM Benjamin Netanyahu made several startling claims about what he described as a "highly severe security incident". He said:

One pilot had stabbed the other and attempted to crash the plane.

The flight entered a "tailspin", which prompted passengers to break into the cockpit with a member of the crew.

Once inside, the group found a co-pilot "trying to sabotage the plane's systems".

The plane only landed safely because a second crew on board took control.

Almost all the passengers on the flight were Israeli, Mr Netanyahu said, before praising the group that intervened at the front of the plane.

"They saved many lives," he said. "They prevented a heavy disaster."

The PM also claimed Saudi officials had arrested one of the pilots.

Authorities would "ramp up" flight security on Israeli and non-Israeli carriers, Mr Netanyahu's spokesman later added.

According to the website Flightradar24, the flydubai plane plunged about 4,000 metres in less than 30 seconds at one point during its journey.

Some of the details from Mr Netanyahu's video were corroborated by a flydubai spokesperson, who said an "altercation had occurred" on the flightdeck of FZ1073.

"At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation," they said.

This passenger on the flight filmed himself asking for help and posted the video on social media. (Reuters/Social media)

'We jumped and helped the pilot'

Verified images from inside the flight showed men covered in blood.

One of the passengers on board, Itzhak Liber, posted a video to social media shortly before the plane landed, in which he said: "We are here on the plane, there was a crazy man with a knife who stabbed one of the pilots.

"We jumped and helped the pilot. Friends, everything is OK now, as you can see we are landing in Saudi Arabia, you can see I am fine. That's it. We will see in a few minutes what will happen when we land."

Citing local security sources, Israeli media outlets and Reuters said the incident was being treated as a terror attack.

Passengers gather around an injured man on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. (Reuters/Social media)

Another man on the flight said in a video posted online: "We control the flight, we controlled the terrorists. Anyone who can hear me, we need help."

A third passenger posted on social media that he saw a "riot" at the front of the plane and that a third pilot onboard "managed to take control of the aircraft, and take us south to Saudi Arabia".

Israel Katz, the country's defence minister, on Wednesday described the incident as "a jihadist terror attempt" which was "thwarted only thanks to the bravery of several Israeli passengers who broke into the cockpit"..

Transporting the passengers from Tabuk to Tel Aviv has been complicated by the fact Saudi Arabia and Israel do not have formal diplomatic relations.

An Israeli request to send a plane to pick up the passengers was rejected. Flydubai said it had sent two planes to Tabuk later on Wednesday to pick up the stranded people.

World.title: More than 1,000 large companies paid no tax in Australia, ATO reveals
World.content:
Almost 30 per cent of large companies paid no tax in 2024-25, an Australian Taxation Office (ATO) report reveals.

The ATO's 10th corporate tax transparency report, which covers 4,299 entities that lodged tax returns two financial years ago, found there were 1,149 entities (27 per cent) that did not pay tax.

That left 3,150 (73 per cent) that did pay tax as the Australian economy faced slow growth, declining commodity prices and high interest rates.

These conditions contributed to a mixed performance among corporate taxpayers, with tax payable decreasing by $8.2 billion (8.6 per cent) to $87.5 billion, compared to the previous year.

Tax deduction red flags on the ATO's radar The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) is warning Australians to stop claiming private expenses on their tax returns.

The report highlights various explanations, including companies making an accounting loss or claiming tax offsets that reduced their tax bill to zero.

ATO acting deputy commissioner Michelle Sams said there were legitimate reasons why a company may pay no income tax.

"'It's important to remember that a nil tax result doesn't automatically imply wrongdoing," she said.

" Many large businesses legitimately pay no income tax but we continue to scrutinise these outcomes closely, as the community expects. "

Ms Sams said the proportion of large corporates paying no income tax was now the lowest level since corporate tax transparency reporting began in 2013-14. In that year the percentage of companies that paid no tax was 36 per cent.

AI companies under scrutiny over data centres

About 140 countries including Australia previously signed up to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Global Minimum Tax deal, a plan more than a decade in the making.

The tax deal imposes a minimum rate of 15 per cent on the profits of multinationals, aiming to end the days of "no-tax havens".

While the deal requires companies to pay that as a minimum on corporate profits, it's nevertheless a significant difference, considering the corporate tax rate in Australia is 30 per cent.

The ATO's Michelle Sams says paying zero tax does not imply wrongdoing. (Supplied: ATO)

Ms Sams said the ATO was using all its resources to stop profit shifting.

Since its establishment in 2016, she said the agency's Tax Avoidance Taskforce has collected $36 billion in additional tax revenue from multinationals, and large public and private businesses.

"We've got a big program of review and audit, 100 to 150 at any one time," Ms Sams said.

Multinationals fight off laws to boost tax transparency For those hopeful the aftermath of the PwC scandal will usher in a new era of tax transparency, there's reason to pause. Laws supposed to take hold on July 1 to increase transparency have been killed off.

The ATO was focusing on companies that use offshore financing and marketing hubs, as well as AI businesses.

"Increasingly we're being more focused on things like digital business models and supply chains, including the growth of cloud computing and [the] data hosting industry," Ms Sams said.

"Given the significant infrastructure, customers and economic activity in operating in data centres, that's an area that we're looking at to make sure the tax outcome is appropriate."

She said royalty arrangements held by multinationals were also under focus.

"For example, where we see big payments to related party offshore, we want to look to make sure that we understand the nature of that payment where it reduces profit subject to tax in Australia."

Ms Sams said when foreign private equity firms dispose of assets, "we're looking to see, is that when there's a gain made … and that the appropriate amount of taxes are paid on that gain".

Mining and energy sector paid most tax

The ATO is required by law to publish tax information reported by certain large corporates each year.

The 2024-25 report covers 4,299 corporate entities, of which:

1,824 are foreign-owned companies, with an income of $100 million or more

593 are Australian public entities, with an income of $100 million or more

1,882 are Australian-owned resident private companies, with an income of $100 million or more.

ABC Business Daily The podcast that helps you unpack the latest business and finance news.

The ATO said tax payable continues to be highly concentrated in a small number of large entities.

Despite being the only segment to decline in tax payable again for 2024-25, the mining, energy and water segment continues to be the largest contributor.

The ATO said 41.1 per cent ($35.9 billion) of total tax payable in the corporate transparency population was paid by the mining, energy and water segment, a 25.8 per cent ($12.5 billion) decrease from the prior year.

Petroleum resource rent tax collection up

Despite lower oil prices in 2024-25, petroleum resource rent tax (PRRT) collections increased from the previous year.

This was mainly driven by the increase in PRRT taxpayers paying the tax under the deductions cap.

PRRT payable increased by more than 26 per cent, rising from $1.48 billion in 2023-24 to $1.87 billion in 2024-25, marking the second highest amount since reporting began.

Corporate tax paid by the oil and gas segment for the year was $10.6 billion, the sector's second highest contribution since reporting began.

World.title: House prices plummet for sixth consecutive month as experts warn of greater falls
World.content:
Australian house prices fell for a sixth straight month in September, and experts say the property market could experience falls of up to 15 per cent in the coming months off the back of higher interest rates and cuts to housing tax breaks.

Cotality's Home Value Index fell 1.1 per cent in September taking cumulative declines to 5.2 per cent below March's peak.

Brisbane saw the sharpest monthly drop among capitals (-1.5 per cent), while Sydney saw a 1.4 per cent fall and Melbourne was down 0.7 per cent.

Darwin (+0.4 per cent) was the only housing market to avoid a fall.

Across the capitals, 97 per cent of suburbs recorded value declines over the past three months, which Cotality's research director Tim Lawless said showed the broad-based scope of the negative housing cycle.

Tim Lawless predicts house values will continue to fall into 2027. (ABC News)

Mr Lawless predicted housing values were likely to continue falling into 2027 from higher rates.

"I think a 10 per cent to 15 per cent drop is probably a fairly reasonable estimate at the moment," he said.

"It really depends on how far do interest rates rise and when do we actually start to see the RBA moving into a more dovish period where rate cuts might be on the agenda."

Developer says more builders will go under

Property developer Soheil Abedian is predicting further property price falls. (ABC News: Glenn Mullane)

Mr Lawless is not the only expert predicting house price falls.

Queensland developer Soheil Abedian has built tens of thousands of homes and is behind luxury developments on the Gold Coast, including Australia's tallest building, Q1, and the former Palazzo Versace resort.

He said the Middle East war, Labor's budget changes to negative gearing and the capital gains tax, and interest rate hikes, would continue to dent property prices and could lead to more builders going under.

"Forty per cent of every single dwelling produced is going to the investor. What does it mean? It means that the rich [are] becoming richer and the poor [are] becoming poorer. And I can say from a selfish point of myself, thank you Mr Albanese [for making] me richer," he told ABC News in an exclusive interview.

Property developer Soheil Abedian is behind multiple luxury developments on the Gold Coast. (ABC News: Glenn Mullane)

He said if interest rates continued increasing in the next six to 12 months the construction sector would see greater bankruptcies.

"You cannot do any development in Australia that is not bankable," Mr Abedian said.

"If [there is a] 10 to 15 per cent reduction we have in the value of the homes, the number of the bankruptcies that we have witnessed in the last twelve months, that increases rapidly and will damage the industry more."

Soheil Abedian's portfolio includes the former Palazzo Versace Hotel on the Spit at Southport, Gold Coast. (ABC Gold Coast: Damien Larkins)

Mr Abedian, who is continuing to build developments on the Gold Coast, wants the government to reverse its changes to property tax breaks and help developers subsidise home builds for first-time buyers.

'Massive greed' will send more builders broke More builders are tipped to collapse over the next 18 months, due to speculation in the recent boom.

He said the cost of construction was getting exorbitant and partly blamed unions demanding wages that were too high.

"We built almost 25 years ago, Q1 — an 80-storey tower, 575 apartments, 50 metres down the ground and built up 325 metres high. It took us three-and-a-half years," he said.

"Now we are building a 37-storey building; we are building only 97 apartments, and it's taking us three-and-a-half years."

Economist says 'worst-case' could lead to recession

Shane Oliver says a worst-case scenario could see house prices fall by 20 per cent. (ABC News: Amy Murray)

While some economists predict another rate rise in November, AMP chief economist Shane Oliver believes rates have peaked.

"There is still a risk, a high risk of one more hike," he said.

"But I think by the time we get to the November meeting, there will be enough evidence suggesting that the demand is really slowing in our economy and that will enable the Reserve Bank to leave rates on hold."

Mr Oliver said in a worst-case scenario where the Iran war drags on, oil prices skyrocket to $150 a barrel and people begin to lose their jobs, house price falls could be as high as 20 per cent.

"This is already shaping up as the biggest downturn in property prices that we've seen in the last 40 years," he said.

"We're not there yet. The worst-case scenarios in the past few years have been an 8 per cent top-to-bottom fall."

He said anything more than 15 per cent could increase the risk of a recession.

"If you have a 20 per cent fall, then you're knocking about 2 per cent off consumer spending … that could tip us into a recession," he said.

Four rate hikes this year have decreased what average wage earners can afford to pay for properties. (ABC News: Crystalyn Brown)

Mr Oliver said even without a recession, the four rate hikes so far this year will hurt many, reducing what the amount an average wage earner on $109,000 can afford to pay for a home by about $45,000 compared to January this year.

"Average wage earners can currently afford to buy about a $500,000 property, but average property prices in Australia are around $900,000," he said.

"So that huge gap, it basically reflects the poor affordability problem that Australia faces."

Fewer home listings and sales

Cotality found that housing turnover has also eased, with the estimated number of national home sales over the past three months tracking 19.1 per cent lower than a year ago and 13.3 per cent below the previous five-year average.

There were also fewer fresh listings coming to market. Mr Lawless said capital city homes were now taking a median of 39 days to sell compared with 23 days a year ago, resulting in an accumulation of advertised supply.

Figures show rental vacancies have increased. (ABC News: Monish Nand)

Mr Lawless said rental vacancies have also risen despite a sharp pullback in investment.

CEOs wade into migration debate There are divergent views among business leaders, from migrant and non-migrant backgrounds, about the impact of planned immigration cuts and the types of migrants that should be allowed into Australia.

He noted this may be because renters are forming larger households in an effort to combat stretched rental affordability.

The national vacancy rate reached 2 per cent in September, up from a record low of just 1.5 per cent in February 2026.

This is the highest national vacancy rate since January 2025, but still well below the pre-COVID decade average of 3.3 per cent.

World.title: 'Extraordinarly reckless': Prince Harry says children targeted by paparazzi
World.content:
Prince Harry's children have been stalked by "certain European paparazzi" while at school in the English countryside, his spokesperson says, marking the latest security incident in the royal's long-running battle with media outlets.

The spokesperson said on Wednesday, local time, that photographers had walked the perimeter of the children's new school before stopping to look in the grounds and monitor the children there.

Security issues have plagued the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, and their children Archie and Lilibet, following their return to Britain from California last month.

The family have sought to keep the location of their new home and the children's school private. The children have already changed schools after heavy traffic on the route to the original location caused concerns for their security team.

"The decision by photographers to conduct themselves in this way around a school is extraordinarily reckless," the spokesperson said in a statement.

While the British press have been broadly respectful of the family's privacy since they moved back, the couple's spokesperson said "certain European paparazzi appear unwilling to respect the privacy of children at school".

Harry and Meghan to move back to UK Harry, the younger son of King Charles, and his wife intend to relocate from the US to a private, non-royal residence outside London, the ABC understands.

Harry has long blamed the press for the death of his mother Princess Diana, who was killed in 1997 when the car she was travelling in crashed as the driver sped away from chasing paparazzi.

He has compared the press' treatment of Meghan Markle to that suffered by his mother.

The couple — who stepped down from royal duties in 2020 and became private citizens — have their own security team but want the British government to provide their family with automatic police protection, as is the case for other senior members of the royal family.

Harry's brother Prince William, the heir to the throne, has had similar experiences with European paparazzi and has in the past won privacy cases against French magazines for publishing photographs of his family while not on official duties.

The brothers, who were once close, have been estranged since Harry stepped down and published a book detailing the breakdown of the relationship and gave several interviews which criticised the royal family.

Reuters

World.title: After 10-year probe, police want 54 people charged over Grenfell Tower blaze
World.content:
Almost a decade since London's deadly Grenfell Tower fire disaster, police have asked prosecutors to consider charging 54 people and 20 companies and organisations.

Seventy-two people died, including 18 children, after a refrigerator electrical fault sparked a fire that ripped through the 23-storey social housing building in North Kensington in June 2017.

The public inquiry's final report in 2024 blamed the disaster on failings by the government, the ​construction industry and, most of all, the companies involved in fitting the exterior with flammable cladding that had been marketed as safe.

Senior police had said no criminal charges would be brought while the inquiry was underway.

Now, two years after its completion, the Metropolitan Police said it had asked the Crown Prosecution Service to consider charges including corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, health and safety offences, fraud and fraud-related offences and misconduct in public office.

Police have also submitted all their evidence files to prosecutors.

Marcio Gomes survived London's Grenfell Tower blaze. (ABC News: Daniel Pannett)

Survivors and victims' families say it is a long-overdue but important milestone, which they hope will lead to prosecutions.

"It's disappointing it's taken this long. I mean it's nearly 10 years on and there's been no accountability, no charges, nothing's really changed if I'm brutally honest," survivor Marcio Gomes told the ABC.

"Having said that, I know forensic elements do take time, so I would prefer they get things right rather than rushing a few things and then all of a sudden certain people can't get prosecuted because [police have] done things not quite in the right way."

Mr Gomes, who lived on the 21st floor, is the father of Grenfell's youngest victim; his baby boy Logan was stillborn while his wife Andreia lay in a coma in the days after the fire. She survived.

The couple's two daughters, Luana and Megan, were also in a coma and survived.

Mr Gomes said he wanted prosecutors to review the evidence thoroughly and "throw the book" at those they find to be responsible because they had "blood on their hands".

'Tortuous' wait for accountability

Police have said the investigation has taken time because it has been "immense".

Officers have analysed about 27,000 pieces of evidence and gathered 14,400 witness statements.

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Kevin Southworth said it was a "milestone moment" in the police investigation.

"We appreciate, of course, it has taken nine years to get to this point. As we have said before, this is one of the most complex investigations ever undertaken by any UK law enforcement agency. The scale is truly enormous," he said.

"While we know this has had a significant impact on those waiting for answers, it has necessarily taken this long to ensure our investigation is meticulous and presents the very best possible evidence to the CPS for charging decisions."

The CPS has committed to making the charging decisions before the 10th anniversary of the fire in June 2027. Any trials would be among the most complex in British history and could take years to get underway.

"It's been deeply frustrating. I would kind of almost use the word tortuous. It's just so painful having to wait so long," Grenfell survivor and campaigner Ed Daffarn told the ABC, adding that it was "particularly galling" the alleged perpetrators had been "able to get on with their lives" since the blaze.

Peter Apps has been investigating the Grenfell Tower disaster. (ABC News: Imogen Cook)

Journalist Peter Apps has published a book on the disaster.

"I think it's hard not to be surprised, when you put all the evidence together about Grenfell, how much was known by so many people," Apps said.

"There were many different parties who could have prevented this, and they had the information they needed to, which is why the inquiry, in the end, said every single death at Grenfell Tower was avoidable.

"You just needed people to act on what they knew."

Highly combustible cladding made of plastic and aluminium on the side of the Grenfell Tower meant the fire spread rapidly.

It remains on buildings around the world today, including in Australia.

"This was a global issue because these are global companies and multinational companies who are selling this product through global supply chains," Apps said.

Remediation work on buildings with flammable cladding across Australia is ongoing.

Demolition work began on Grenfell Tower last year. (Reuters: Isabel Infantes)

Lessons to learn

The fire was Britain's deadliest in a residential building since World War II and prompted a national reckoning over building standards and the safety and conditions ​of social housing for low-income communities.

Mr Daffarn had flagged concerns about building maintenance and fire safety with building management and the local council before the fire.

"As I stood underneath the smouldering embers of Grenfell Tower in the days after the fire, I was convinced that it would be the catalyst for change, for proper change," Mr Daffarn said.

"[But] standing here nearly 10 years after that event, I'm very sad to say that that change has not really occurred.

"It wouldn't be right to say no lessons have been learned, because some lessons have been learned, but people in social housing are still not treated with dignity and respect, there are still people up and down the UK living in dangerous buildings, and the construction industry has not reformed itself in the way that it needs to."

Grenfell Tower is being demolished, but​ police are building replicas of parts of it to help future judges and juries understand what happened and who might be to blame.

Mr Gomes fought back tears as he told the ABC he felt compelled to keep campaigning for Grenfell survivors and victims' families for two reasons: to honour the memory of baby Logan and push for change.

"There's still a lot of work to be done to make sure it never happens again," he said.

World.title: Jai Arrow told 'nothing' about pre-grand final tribute
World.content:
Jai Arrow says he has been told "nothing" about a tribute awaiting him ahead of Sunday's NRL grand final.

It was widely reported today that Arrow would do a lap of Stadium Australia while a selection of Australian musicians perform Gerry and the Pacemakers' song and Liverpool FC anthem You'll Never Walk Alone.

Earlier this year, Arrow retired from the NRL after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).

Speaking to the ABC at this evening's Dally M Awards in Sydney, Arrow said he was unsure of the details of the ceremony.

"[I know] nothing yet, apparently I'm going around … but I don't know anything," Arrow said.

"So it'll be interesting. It won't just be for me, it'll be for everyone fighting MND."

Loading...

Arrow was honoured with the Provan-Summons Medal at the awards night for embodying the spirit of the game, which is measured against the values of respect, honesty, bravery and sportsmanship.

He said the proposed pre-game tribute on Sunday would be an opportunity to continue raising awareness of MND.

"I can use my platform to spread awareness," he said.

Meanwhile, NRL executive chairman Peter V'landys was tight-lipped about the tribute but promised fans they would be "happy and impressed" with the performers selected.

"You'll see, there'll be superstar Australian performers, that's all that we'll say, and everyone will be very happy and impressed with what we've got," he said.

"But it's not about them; it's about Jai, it's about what Jai does; he inspires people.

"We've received a lot of correspondence at the NRL about how his inspiration has made them see their illnesses through."

V'landys also said the league will be donating $100,000 to Arrow's family, as well as $1 million to a "fund for underprivileged kids who can't afford to play rugby league".

"If we can lift a lot of other people with Jai's courage and leadership, that's what we're going to do on Sunday night," V'landys said.

The NRL was left without pre-match entertainment for the grand final after talks with Australian artist Tones and I broke down earlier this month.

World.title: The new luxury: Why Perth buyers are abandoning beach views for sheds and workshops
World.content:
PropertyNewsProperty market The new luxury: Why Perth buyers are abandoning beach views for sheds and workshops Indigo Lemay-Conway October 1, 2026 — 2:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Aside from affordability, Perth home buyers are looking for space when it comes to buying their next property. That’s according to Domain’s Spring Homebuyer Report, released today, which revealed the top search trends in Perth this year have been pools, granny flats, land and workshops. Domain’s national property editor Alice Stolz said the trends showed Perth buyers were moving away from beachfront views and towards more space to play and grow. “What we’re seeing is that basically most Perth buyers are looking for space, which is kind of the ultimate luxury,” she said.



“What that means is, it’s not just pools. Basically, buyers are searching for other ways to add volume to what their parcel of land or home is.” Stolz said land and dual living had climbed the ranks in search trends over the past year. “We’re particularly seeing a strong interest in things like granny flats, land, and workshops when it comes to what people are searching for in the Perth market,” she said. “I think what that is also reflective of is the Perth market has obviously seen huge supersonic growth over the past few years, and many people are kind of trying to get more bang for their buck in what they’re paying for. “So, even if they can’t sort of flex that much on price, can they find other ways to kind of have more value in that parcel of their property?”



The search trends match the regions which have the highest demand in Perth at the moment, with Mundaring and Kalamunda leading the way in 2026. Ray White Aldridge & Associates sales representative Nigel Aldridge said it was a trend he had noticed with buyers in Kalamunda. “Kalamunda has gone through quite a transformation in terms of demographics. So a lot of the people that built their houses up there, and the same with Mundaring, actually, in the 70s and the 80s, they’re moving out quite quickly,” he said. “But what’s happened is that a lot of younger people have moved back in, and I think what happens with those areas is that they actually represent very good value when they’re actually broken down.



“People can buy quite a big block and get a substantial home, for the price that you might pay for a smaller home on a smaller block closer to the city, for instance.” Sheds and workshops have topped the list of must-haves for buyers in the area. “You can do a whole lot on 1000 square metres or 2000 square meters. All of those things: granny flat shed, pool, lifestyle,” he said. “A lot of people want sheds and storage.” But it’s the multi-generational home that is coming up through the trends at the moment.



“A multi-generational home has become, I wouldn’t say really popular, but certainly, it’s been creeping in, and we’ve seen the demand for that increase,” Aldridge said. “Bearing in mind that it’s coming from almost a zero base, and it’s starting now, so it’s interesting. “I’ve noticed that a couple of times we’ve sold properties to people whose plan is to add an ancillary dwelling, or they’ve sold their property to move into a property with a child or an older parent.” Stolz said that sheds and workshops also have benefits for first homebuyers looking to make some money in the long run.



“I think seeing granny flats, land, workshops, and sheds on the list really speaks to me about the affordability constraints that many buyers are facing, and how they get more flexibility on what they do purchase,” she said. Related Article Interest rates How far house prices have risen since the last time rates were this high “If they’re a first-home buyer, and they’re scrimping and saving to get a deposit, if they’ve got things like a granny flat, even a workshop or a shed, and I know this sounds odd, but often people then become quite creative. “They’ll think, if I get it compliant, could I potentially rent that out as an extra space to earn some income on the side as the owner of that property?” Despite space being the main trends on the search list, it was a good old pool that came out on top for almost all cities in Australia except for Canberra.



Stolz said it shows people still value the use of a pool in their backyard. “The fact it’s still number one, sort of everywhere in the country except for poor old Canberra, really speaks volumes to me about the fact that we really value our homes being a sanctuary and somewhere where we can sort of just live in a little bubble of our home,” she said. “We do still really value having a house with a backyard that’s big enough for a pool in it.” Across June to August, Perth was the only city to record annual growth in new housing and unit supply.

World.title: Pilot arrested after midair stabbing and crash attempt, ‘heroes’ averted major disaster: Israeli PM
World.content:
Updated WorldMiddle EastAviation Pilot arrested after midair stabbing and crash attempt, ‘heroes’ averted major disaster: Israeli PM David Crowe Updated October 1, 2026 — 12:10am ,first published 4:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

London: A commercial aircraft flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after issuing an alert that sparked fears of a disaster when one of the two pilots stabbed the other in an apparent attempt to crash the plane. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the early evidence suggested that crew members and passengers responded to the attack by entering the cockpit and stopping the attacker, in an “extremely serious” security incident. The midair crisis began when flydubai Flight FZ1073 suddenly lost altitude and issued an emergency alert more than two hours into its journey, leading the Israeli government to scramble fighter jets in response. Loading Netanyahu made his televised remarks on Wednesday afternoon in Israel (shortly after 11.30pm AEST) in the first official statement on the attacks by the Israeli government after hours of speculation about whether the incident was a hijacking, an altercation between pilots or a brutal attempt to kill all on board.



“I salute the heroes who demonstrated resourcefulness and extraordinary courage,” Netanyahu said. “They saved many lives and averted a terrible disaster. The pilot who committed the stabbing has been arrested and is currently being interrogated by Saudi authorities.” Netanyahu said he had spoken to a passenger and to officials who told him one of the pilots stabbed the other and apparently tried to crash the aircraft. He said the pilot suspected of launching the attack had been arrested. A photo purportedly showing one of the passengers on flydubai FZ1073 with blood on his shirt. Amichai Stein/Twitter At least one passenger joined a crew member in breaking into the cockpit to stop the pilot attempting to damage the plane. Another crew member then joined them and managed to stabilise the aircraft, he said.



Public flight radar sites show that the Boeing 737 MAX was diverted to Saudi Arabia and landed about 90 minutes after a shocking plunge in altitude, with passengers describing “blood in the cockpit” after the fight on board. Other air crew and passengers on board managed to subdue the pilot and bring him under control. Israeli media cited unnamed officials who said it was suspected that one of the pilots intended to crash the plane and there was a “growing assessment” that the emergency had been intended as an act of terror. Other options were also being looked into, including the possibility of a mental health episode. “We heard screams on the plane,” one passenger said in a text message to Israeli media network Channel 12 that was reported by The Times of Israel and other outlets.



“Then they opened the cockpit and we saw blood, and someone had stabbed the pilot with a pocketknife.” In one video shared by one person on the flight, the captain is covered in blood as some passengers support him and praise him for saving the aircraft from disaster. A second member of the crew, possibly the other pilot, is seen tied up nearby and apparently unconscious. The owner of Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport said the captain and co-pilot were “found to have injuries” and taken to hospital. View post on X Netanyahu called urgent meetings to monitor the emergency after the aircraft first issued a 7700 “squawk” code to signal an international emergency, before changing this to a 7500 code to signal a hijacking or unlawful interference, according to reports.



The Israel Defence Forces chief of staff, Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir, held an assessment of the incident with senior officers, The Times of Israel reported. The aircraft departed Dubai at 7.05am local time on Wednesday (1.05pm AEST) and initially flew over the southern part of the Persian Gulf before crossing over Saudi Arabia and heading towards Israel. Fluctuations in its altitude began about two hours into the trip, according to Flightradar24. The plane then dropped 14,000 feet (4300 metres) in less than 30 seconds and issued its first alert about 2½ hours into the flight. The emergency lasted for the next 90 minutes before it turned out of Jordanian airspace and landed at Tabuk, a city in the far west of Saudi Arabia. A plane carrying passengers from the earlier flight left Saudi Arabia and landed at Ben Gurion International Airport in Israel on Wednesday night to cheers and a crowd waving Israeli flags. Israeli passenger Haim Lazarovich as he arrived in Israel after a second flight in the wake of the emergency. AP Photo/Ariel Schalit



Passengers arrive at Ben Gurion International Airport in Israel. AP Photo/Ariel Schalit Earlier in the day, Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister’s office, told Reuters the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking, describing it as a “different incident”. He did not immediately respond to a further request for comment on whether Israel was treating it as a “terror incident”. Israeli journalist Amichai Stein reported an account of the emergency from those on board and posted images of one passenger with a blood-stained shirt. “We heard screams and saw blood,” one passenger said, according to Stein. “The pilot was stabbed. There were moments when we thought we weren’t going to make it out alive.” Stein is a contributor to The Jerusalem Post and the diplomatic correspondent for iNews24 in Tel Aviv.



View post on X The flight experienced “an incident while en route”, Flydubai said in a statement. All passengers were safe and accounted for, the spokesperson said, without providing further details. The Israeli media said authorities were planning to question the crew and inspect the aircraft as part of an investigation into the scare. The airline, which is owned by the investment arm of Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, is expected to send another aircraft to the Saudi airport to transfer the passengers to Tel Aviv. Budget airline flydubai is owned by Dubai. iStock



Israeli airspace was briefly closed during the emergency. Netanyahu’s office had earlier issued a brief statement to reassure citizens. “The incident is under control, and all measures are currently being deployed in order to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel,” the prime minister’s office said. World.title: ‘Be prepared’: Victorians warned of thunderstorm asthma risk ahead of intense pollen season
World.content:
Exclusive NationalVictoriaHealthcare ‘Be prepared’: Victorians warned of thunderstorm asthma risk ahead of intense pollen season Henrietta Cook October 1, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Victorians are being urged to prepare for potentially deadly thunderstorm asthma as health experts warn of an intense hay fever season following a wet and warm winter. Ten years ago, Victoria experienced the world’s largest and most catastrophic thunderstorm asthma event, one which led to the deaths of 10 people and caused breathing issues in thousands of others. Thunderstorm asthma is expected to affect more Victorians this year, after a warm and wet winter. Chris Hopkins Chief Health Officer Dr Caroline McElnay said a relatively warm and rainy winter had led to a lot of grass growth around the state, contributing to an early start to the pollen season. “We can’t control the weather or the pollen, but we can reduce exposure,” McElnay said.



From today until December 31, the VicEmergency website and app will provide three-day forecasts of thunderstorm asthma risk for each of the state’s nine weather districts. Related Article Good Weekend Thunderstorm asthma: the night a deadly storm took Melbourne's breath away It will do this using seven high-tech pollen counters distributed around the state. McElnay said people with asthma and hay fever were particularly vulnerable to thunderstorm asthma and should follow the forecasts, continue taking prescribed medication, and comply with their asthma action plans. They should also close windows and avoid being outside during storms and when it’s windy. Thunderstorm asthma occurs when there is a sudden change in weather, which can lead to grass pollen grains absorbing moisture in the air and bursting. This releases thousands of allergenic particles, which can be inhaled into the depths of the lungs, triggering asthma symptoms.



People with hay fever can unexpectedly develop asthma symptoms when this occurs. Related Article Health People suddenly get asthma after moving to Australia and researchers don't know why McElnay, who suffers from hay fever, recently bought an inhaler ahead of thunderstorm asthma season. “It’s better to be prepared,” she said. McElnay developed the common condition when she moved from the UK to New Zealand. The thunderstorm asthma forecasts are also used by health services so they can prepare for a potential rise in people turning up to emergency departments.



“What we’re trying to minimise is the number of people whose asthma would be triggered or would be so severe that they need to seek emergency care,” McElnay said. Dr Naghmeh Radhakrishna, a respiratory and allergy physician at St Vincent’s Hospital and The Alfred, treated patients who wound up in intensive care following the catastrophic thunderstorm asthma event on November 21, 2016. “There was one patient I saw who ended up needing resuscitation,” she recalled. “He was a young guy in his late 30s or early 40s. He had a severe episode and also had allergic rhinitis.” She advises people with hay fever to also get tested for asthma.



“The people who died during the thunderstorm event were the people who basically had undiagnosed asthma, or they had asthma but it wasn’t well controlled,” she said. Dr Naghmeh Radhakrishna Paul Jeffers Radhakrishna said immunotherapy and desensitisation treatments could gradually retrain a person’s immune system to tolerate pollen, reducing hay fever symptoms. Since the events of November 2016, the state government has invested in and expanded Victoria’s world-leading Epidemic Thunderstorm Asthma Risk Forecast System. The system was modernised last year with automated pollen counters, which use advanced imaging to deliver faster and more precise data, replacing manual traps. Health Minister Ingrid Stitt described the sophisticated pollen counters as a nation-leading tool that kept Victorians healthy and safe.



Related Article Exclusive

Illness Why your hay fever might actually be spring asthma “We want every Victorian to be safe this pollen season – that’s why we’re encouraging everyone to be prepared,” she said. Edwin Lampugnani, chief executive of AirHealth, which provides daily pollen counts to thousands of Australians through the Melbourne Pollen and Sydney Pollen websites and apps, said satellite data showed verdant landscapes, particularly in north-west Victoria. “Everything is looking very, very green,” he said. “It’s much greener than it was in 2025.” He said this led to the grass producing more pollen.



“We’re looking at a stronger season, or a more intense season than we saw last year,” he said. National Asthma Council Australia spokesperson and respiratory physician Professor Peter Wark said effective day-to-day control of asthma was the best defence during the pollen and thunderstorm asthma season. Related Article Healthcare Nothing to sneeze at: Why so many Australians suffer from hay fever National asthma guidelines changed last year, with doctors urged to move away from solely prescribing blue puffers as a standalone treatment for those aged over 12. It’s now recommended that people with asthma use anti-inflammatory relievers. “Even people with hay fever who have never had asthma should see their GP if they experience symptoms such as breathlessness, wheezing and tightness in the chest. These symptoms do not occur with hay fever alone,” Wark said.



About 11 per cent of Australians have asthma, the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare says. One in four Australians suffer from allergic rhinitis, the scientific name for hay fever. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: House prices slump extends to six months
World.content:
NationalProperty market House prices slump extends to six months Matt Wade October 1, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Home values in Australia have fallen by 5 per cent from their peak in March, with Sydney and Melbourne leading the downturn. The national property slump has stretched to six months after a 1.1 per cent fall in September, Cotality’s Home Value Index shows. Values fell in every capital city except Darwin last month. Home values in Australia fell for the sixth straight month in September. Wolter Peeters Sydney’s property market has taken the biggest hit, with prices now 8.6 per cent below their February peak. The city’s median dwelling value is $1,198,596, Cotality’s figures show. Price declines in Sydney are now a little deeper than the equivalent stage of the previous 2022-23 downturn “highlighting how rapidly demand has weakened across the nation’s largest housing market”.



Melbourne property values are now 7.2 per cent below their peak in November 2025 and 7.5 per cent lower than the record high for property prices registered in March 2022. But Cotality, a property analytics firm, said the Melbourne property market is now showing a “milder rate of decline” with prices down 0.7 per cent in September, the smallest monthly fall among the state capitals. Property market sentiment has been hit by multiple interest rate hikes this year, along with changes to the taxation of housing investment and lingering economic uncertainty caused by conflict in the Middle East. On Tuesday, the Reserve Bank lifted official interest rates by 0.25 of a percentage point to a 15-year high of 4.6 per cent in a bid to dampen inflationary pressures in the economy. That followed hikes in February, March and May.



Cotality’s report said housing market conditions are likely “to remain under downward pressure over the coming months with the latest interest rate increase adding to a formidable set of demand-side headwinds.” The federal government’s overhaul of capital gains tax and negative gearing, legislated earlier this year, has also contributed to weaker conditions in the property market. “Less favourable negative gearing and capital gains tax arrangements have already seen a sharp reduction in investor demand,” Cotality’s report said. Brisbane recorded the sharpest decline in September, with house prices down 1.5 per cent in the month. Property prices in the city have fallen 5.4 per cent since peaking in May. House prices in Perth fell 0.5 per cent in September to be down 6 per cent since their April peak.



Tim Lawless, Cotality’s research director, said property values have fallen in more than 90 per cent of capital city suburbs over the past three months, “highlighting the broad-based scope of this negative housing cycle”. Related Article Analysis

Interest rates To avoid another rate rise, things might have to get worse “The housing downturn reflects a combination of affordability constraints, higher interest rates, elevated living costs, and weaker consumer sentiment, all of which have reduced purchasing capacity and dampened buyer demand,” Cotality’s report said. There has also been a sharp decline in housing turnover which threatens to hit stamp duty collections, an important source of state government revenue. Cotality’s estimates of the number of home sales over the past three months nationally are nearly 20 per cent lower than a year ago and 13.3 per cent below the previous five-year average.



The volume of home sales compared to a year ago was down most sharply in Brisbane (minus 27.2 per cent) and Sydney (minus 26.5 per cent). “The sharp drop in sales has implications for the broader economy, with lower sales likely to hit some retail segments as well as stamp duty revenues for state governments,” Lawless said. Separate figures released by Housing Australia, the federal government’s housing delivery agency, show 102,000 first-time buyers have taken up Labor’s 5% Deposit Scheme to purchase a home. The scheme was expanded to all first home buyers a year ago, and the government estimates one in two first home buyers nationally are now using it. Cotality’s report said regional property markets have proved more resilient than in capital cities. Regional dwelling values fell by 0.7 per cent in September but are still up 5.6 per cent annually.



Darwin was the only capital city to register a house price increase in September (0.4 per cent). Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. Subscribers can sign up to our weekly Inside Politics newsletter.

(MA15+) 114 minutes

I’ll say this for Verity, the latest film adaptation of a Colleen Hoover novel (after It Ends With Us, Regretting You and Reminders of Him): it lays its cards on the table, right from the title.

Verity means truth (from the Latin veritas). It also happens to be the name of a bestselling crime fiction author, Verity Crawford (Anne Hathaway), whose novels tap into her own thoughts and longings and anti-social impulses to such a degree that her husband Jeremy (Josh Hartnett) stopped reading them after the first one, because he didn’t want his perception of the woman he loves to be tainted. Is the book version of her the truth, or the version he knows?

Dakota Johnson in Verity. Amazon/MGM Studios via AP

The story isn’t Verity’s, though; its narrator and central character is Lowen Ashleigh (Dakota Johnson), also a novelist, but very much at the other end of the publishing mountain. We first meet her as she’s doing an apologetically hushed-voice reading in a sparsely attended book store, interrupted when one of the attendees gets a phone call. “Sorry,” the woman says. “Sorry,” responds the timorous Lowen.

World.title: Wheelchair-bound Nathan Cleary wins Dally M Medal at end of horror week
World.content:
Nathan Cleary could never have imagined collecting his first Dally M Medal while seated in a wheelchair at home.

Cleary has been at the centre of some brilliant moments on the field this season, but the image of him being crowned the game’s best player last night while recovering at home from a badly broken leg will not be forgotten any time soon.

Panthers halfback and Dally M winner Nathan Cleary. NRL Photos

The 28-year-old capped a whirlwind 72 hours by collecting the award that had so far eluded him during his brilliant career.

Brisbane’s Tamika Upton took out her third Dally M as the game’s best female player, and can cap an outstanding season with another premiership on Sunday.

Upton finished on 31 points, polled a full six points in the penultimate round, then one in the last round to beat Wests Tigers’ Raecene McGregor (29 points).

Cleary was the red-hot favourite to take out the Dally M in 2020, only to be pipped by Canberra’s Jack Wighton. But nothing was going to stop him as he polled 67 votes, 14 clear of Cronulla’s Braydon Trindall, with Dylan Edwards a further vote back in third.

The game’s best player suffered a double compound fracture of his leg in Sunday’s preliminary final loss to Newcastle as a result of a tackle that led to Newcastle’s Phoenix Crossland being handed a four-match ban. If Cleary wearing the Dally M Medal around his neck in his lounge room was a lovely touch, so was Crossland’s heartfelt teary apology a night earlier when he received his ban, and told those at the judiciary hearing he felt guilty for taking the gloss off the grand final.

The Penrith halfback was earlier this week handed the Rugby League Players Association’s Players’ Champion, which complemented the Brad Fittler Medal he won for being NSW’s best player and the Wally Lewis Medal, which is awarded to the standout player in the Origin series.

Cleary was also one of three Panthers included in the Dally M team of the year with Edwards and winger Tom Jenkins.

Andrew Webster was crowned coach of the year, fellow New Zealand Warrior James Fisher-Harris the captain of the year and Canberra halfback Ethan Sanders the best rookie.

Sunday’s grand finalists, the Sydney Roosters, had centre Rob Toia and prop Naufahu Whyte named in the team of the year. Newcastle, however, failed to have a player included in that side.

South Sydney’s Jai Arrow was forced to medically retire after being diagnosed with motor neurone diseases this season, and the heart-warming scenes he was involved in on several occasions, including being allowed to bring up his 100th game for the club in the final round before being brought from the field, earned him two awards, the Provan-Summons Medal, and the Peter Frilingos Headline Moment.

World.title: Bogongs change their tune
World.content:
Paul Duncan of Leura has been experiencing first-hand the return of the bogong moth (C8): “In the mornings the front and back fly-screen doors are covered with them, and one needs to use the leaf blower to move them on or they will fly inside. In earlier times they would swarm around the nearest street light, which in turn attracted the local owls, but they seem to have disappeared. Hopefully they, too, will return.”

For Central West locals, there are issues. Just ask Donald Hawes of Peel: “We are welcoming the current fluttering of bogong moths at our place outside Bathurst but they’ve played havoc with the organ at All Saints Cathedral in town. The trumpet, bassoon, trombone and clarinet pipes, which all have a large reed at the base, have become jammed with errant moths and are unplayable. After the great number of pipes, ranging from about 70 millimetres to nearly five metres, have been taken down, cleaned, returned and re-tuned, a screen will have to be installed to keep the moths out, just as we do for the blowies at home.”

Sticking with nature, Janice Creenaune of Austinmer notes that “my middle child has had a big week watching multiple diamond pythons copulating in his front garden in Bulli. One large and beautiful female and multiple males ‘balled in ecstasy’. An amazing sight.”

Andrew McPherson of Tathra “can’t help but wonder if AI (C8) would have squashed the millennium bug”.

“The mention of Lady Marmalade reminds me of Je t’aime … moi non plus, the seductive, oh-so French song from Serge Gainsbourg and Jane Birkin, from 1969,” writes Pauline McGinley of Drummoyne. “It was in French, with much suggestive, heavy breathing and less-than-coy lyrics. It had us high school French students furtively translating away! It was played freely for a short while on the radio but the censorship and controversy had kicked in by the time it reached No.1 on the pop charts, and then only the music, sans lyrics, was permitted.”

World.title: The new luxury: Why Perth buyers are abandoning beach views for sheds and workshops
World.content:
PropertyNewsProperty market The new luxury: Why Perth buyers are abandoning beach views for sheds and workshops Indigo Lemay-Conway October 1, 2026 — 2:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Aside from affordability, Perth home buyers are looking for space when it comes to buying their next property. That’s according to Domain’s Spring Homebuyer Report, released today, which revealed the top search trends in Perth this year have been pools, granny flats, land and workshops. Domain’s national property editor Alice Stolz said the trends showed Perth buyers were moving away from beachfront views and towards more space to play and grow. “What we’re seeing is that basically most Perth buyers are looking for space, which is kind of the ultimate luxury,” she said.



“What that means is, it’s not just pools. Basically, buyers are searching for other ways to add volume to what their parcel of land or home is.” Stolz said land and dual living had climbed the ranks in search trends over the past year. “We’re particularly seeing a strong interest in things like granny flats, land, and workshops when it comes to what people are searching for in the Perth market,” she said. “I think what that is also reflective of is the Perth market has obviously seen huge supersonic growth over the past few years, and many people are kind of trying to get more bang for their buck in what they’re paying for. “So, even if they can’t sort of flex that much on price, can they find other ways to kind of have more value in that parcel of their property?”



The search trends match the regions which have the highest demand in Perth at the moment, with Mundaring and Kalamunda leading the way in 2026. Ray White Aldridge & Associates sales representative Nigel Aldridge said it was a trend he had noticed with buyers in Kalamunda. “Kalamunda has gone through quite a transformation in terms of demographics. So a lot of the people that built their houses up there, and the same with Mundaring, actually, in the 70s and the 80s, they’re moving out quite quickly,” he said. “But what’s happened is that a lot of younger people have moved back in, and I think what happens with those areas is that they actually represent very good value when they’re actually broken down.



“People can buy quite a big block and get a substantial home, for the price that you might pay for a smaller home on a smaller block closer to the city, for instance.” Sheds and workshops have topped the list of must-haves for buyers in the area. “You can do a whole lot on 1000 square metres or 2000 square meters. All of those things: granny flat shed, pool, lifestyle,” he said. “A lot of people want sheds and storage.” But it’s the multi-generational home that is coming up through the trends at the moment.



“A multi-generational home has become, I wouldn’t say really popular, but certainly, it’s been creeping in, and we’ve seen the demand for that increase,” Aldridge said. “Bearing in mind that it’s coming from almost a zero base, and it’s starting now, so it’s interesting. “I’ve noticed that a couple of times we’ve sold properties to people whose plan is to add an ancillary dwelling, or they’ve sold their property to move into a property with a child or an older parent.” Stolz said that sheds and workshops also have benefits for first homebuyers looking to make some money in the long run.



“I think seeing granny flats, land, workshops, and sheds on the list really speaks to me about the affordability constraints that many buyers are facing, and how they get more flexibility on what they do purchase,” she said. Related Article Interest rates How far house prices have risen since the last time rates were this high “If they’re a first-home buyer, and they’re scrimping and saving to get a deposit, if they’ve got things like a granny flat, even a workshop or a shed, and I know this sounds odd, but often people then become quite creative. “They’ll think, if I get it compliant, could I potentially rent that out as an extra space to earn some income on the side as the owner of that property?” Despite space being the main trends on the search list, it was a good old pool that came out on top for almost all cities in Australia except for Canberra.



Stolz said it shows people still value the use of a pool in their backyard. “The fact it’s still number one, sort of everywhere in the country except for poor old Canberra, really speaks volumes to me about the fact that we really value our homes being a sanctuary and somewhere where we can sort of just live in a little bubble of our home,” she said. “We do still really value having a house with a backyard that’s big enough for a pool in it.” Across June to August, Perth was the only city to record annual growth in new housing and unit supply.

World.title: Pilot arrested after midair stabbing and crash attempt, ‘heroes’ averted major disaster: Israeli PM
World.content:
Updated WorldMiddle EastAviation Pilot arrested after midair stabbing and crash attempt, ‘heroes’ averted major disaster: Israeli PM David Crowe Updated October 1, 2026 — 12:10am ,first published 4:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

London: A commercial aircraft flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after issuing an alert that sparked fears of a disaster when one of the two pilots stabbed the other in an apparent attempt to crash the plane. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the early evidence suggested that crew members and passengers responded to the attack by entering the cockpit and stopping the attacker, in an “extremely serious” security incident. The midair crisis began when flydubai Flight FZ1073 suddenly lost altitude and issued an emergency alert more than two hours into its journey, leading the Israeli government to scramble fighter jets in response. Loading Netanyahu made his televised remarks on Wednesday afternoon in Israel (shortly after 11.30pm AEST) in the first official statement on the attacks by the Israeli government after hours of speculation about whether the incident was a hijacking, an altercation between pilots or a brutal attempt to kill all on board.



“I salute the heroes who demonstrated resourcefulness and extraordinary courage,” Netanyahu said. “They saved many lives and averted a terrible disaster. The pilot who committed the stabbing has been arrested and is currently being interrogated by Saudi authorities.” Netanyahu said he had spoken to a passenger and to officials who told him one of the pilots stabbed the other and apparently tried to crash the aircraft. He said the pilot suspected of launching the attack had been arrested. A photo purportedly showing one of the passengers on flydubai FZ1073 with blood on his shirt. Amichai Stein/Twitter At least one passenger joined a crew member in breaking into the cockpit to stop the pilot attempting to damage the plane. Another crew member then joined them and managed to stabilise the aircraft, he said.



Public flight radar sites show that the Boeing 737 MAX was diverted to Saudi Arabia and landed about 90 minutes after a shocking plunge in altitude, with passengers describing “blood in the cockpit” after the fight on board. Other air crew and passengers on board managed to subdue the pilot and bring him under control. Israeli media cited unnamed officials who said it was suspected that one of the pilots intended to crash the plane and there was a “growing assessment” that the emergency had been intended as an act of terror. Other options were also being looked into, including the possibility of a mental health episode. “We heard screams on the plane,” one passenger said in a text message to Israeli media network Channel 12 that was reported by The Times of Israel and other outlets.



“Then they opened the cockpit and we saw blood, and someone had stabbed the pilot with a pocketknife.” In one video shared by one person on the flight, the captain is covered in blood as some passengers support him and praise him for saving the aircraft from disaster. A second member of the crew, possibly the other pilot, is seen tied up nearby and apparently unconscious. The owner of Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport said the captain and co-pilot were “found to have injuries” and taken to hospital. View post on X Netanyahu called urgent meetings to monitor the emergency after the aircraft first issued a 7700 “squawk” code to signal an international emergency, before changing this to a 7500 code to signal a hijacking or unlawful interference, according to reports.



The Israel Defence Forces chief of staff, Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir, held an assessment of the incident with senior officers, The Times of Israel reported. The aircraft departed Dubai at 7.05am local time on Wednesday (1.05pm AEST) and initially flew over the southern part of the Persian Gulf before crossing over Saudi Arabia and heading towards Israel. Fluctuations in its altitude began about two hours into the trip, according to Flightradar24. The plane then dropped 14,000 feet (4300 metres) in less than 30 seconds and issued its first alert about 2½ hours into the flight. The emergency lasted for the next 90 minutes before it turned out of Jordanian airspace and landed at Tabuk, a city in the far west of Saudi Arabia. A plane carrying passengers from the earlier flight left Saudi Arabia and landed at Ben Gurion International Airport in Israel on Wednesday night to cheers and a crowd waving Israeli flags. Israeli passenger Haim Lazarovich as he arrived in Israel after a second flight in the wake of the emergency. AP Photo/Ariel Schalit



Passengers arrive at Ben Gurion International Airport in Israel. AP Photo/Ariel Schalit Earlier in the day, Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister’s office, told Reuters the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking, describing it as a “different incident”. He did not immediately respond to a further request for comment on whether Israel was treating it as a “terror incident”. Israeli journalist Amichai Stein reported an account of the emergency from those on board and posted images of one passenger with a blood-stained shirt. “We heard screams and saw blood,” one passenger said, according to Stein. “The pilot was stabbed. There were moments when we thought we weren’t going to make it out alive.” Stein is a contributor to The Jerusalem Post and the diplomatic correspondent for iNews24 in Tel Aviv.



View post on X The flight experienced “an incident while en route”, Flydubai said in a statement. All passengers were safe and accounted for, the spokesperson said, without providing further details. The Israeli media said authorities were planning to question the crew and inspect the aircraft as part of an investigation into the scare. The airline, which is owned by the investment arm of Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, is expected to send another aircraft to the Saudi airport to transfer the passengers to Tel Aviv. Budget airline flydubai is owned by Dubai. iStock



Israeli airspace was briefly closed during the emergency. Netanyahu’s office had earlier issued a brief statement to reassure citizens. “The incident is under control, and all measures are currently being deployed in order to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel,” the prime minister’s office said.
